COBOL words
notes: kb/Work PB65 (2026-08-18): ONE screen (DataBinder.ScreenRepositoryIntrinsicName) asked by every declaration funnel — data-name, condition-name, index-name, file-name, paragraph/section name — rejects (COBOLNET1649) a user-defined word spelling an intrinsic-function-name the REPOSITORY identifies (FUNCTION name INTRINSIC, or every catalogued name under FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC); LENGTH/RANDOM/SIGN/SUM are reserved words already. A catalogued name the REPOSITORY does not identify stays a legal user-defined word (SQRT as a table, MOD as an item — the golden's control) and its FUNCTION-less spelling a data reference. Editions: the REPOSITORY function-specifier is 2002+ (85 has no REPOSITORY).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: The lexer's FLOAT_BODY (and its DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA twin FLOAT_COMMA_BODY, kb/Work PB98) is exactly the form — a fixed-point literal, the letter E without intervening spaces, a fixed-point exponent; the sign-adjacent twins (function-argument regions, SUBSCRIPT mode) keep -1.5E3 one token (kb/Work R17).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99). 'shall include a decimal point' is the lexer's shape (a point-less 1E10 is a user-defined word, §8.3.1.1 — it is diagnosed as an undefined name, which it is); 'from 1 to 36 digits' is checked at the ONE normalizer both funnels share (COBOLNET1661 — a 40-digit significand); a 36-digit significand seeds a floating-point numeric-edited item exactly (the golden's E1).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99). 'a maximum of four digits' — COBOLNET1661 for a fifth (1.0E12345, which used to reach Roslyn as an overflowing C# double literal, CS0594); the IMPLEMENTOR-DEFINED maximum / minimum exponent VALUE is documented in CONFORMANCE.md §7 A.1 item 82 and enforced at compile time: the binary64 range for a literal in a native arithmetic expression / statement (about 4.9E-324..1.8E+308 — 1.0E+400 / 1.0E-400 → 1661), decimal128's under STANDARD-DECIMAL (1.0E+400 / 1.0E+398 evaluates to 100), the receiver's binary form for a VALUE on a FLOAT-SHORT (binary32) / FLOAT-LONG (binary64) item (§13.18.63.3 SR2), and no bound beyond the receiver's PICTURE for a VALUE on a fixed-point or floating-point numeric-edited item (PIC 9E+9999 VALUE 1.0E+9999).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99). A zero significand with a nonzero exponent (0.0E+5), a negative zero significand (-0.0E+0) or a negative-signed exponent (0.0E-0) is COBOLNET1661 — in a VALUE clause, a level-88 and a statement alike (the ONE normalizer).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99). The literal's value — significand × 10^exponent — is carried EXACTLY wherever the standard's semantics are the value's: a VALUE clause (NumericLiteral.ExpandFloatingPoint for a fixed-point subject, EditComposeFloat for a floating-point numeric-edited one), an OPERAND position (a MOVE source, a relation / EVALUATE comparand, a PERFORM VARYING FROM / BY value, a function argument — NumericRenderer.LiteralOperandNum → CobolDec.FromParsed on the exact-decimal lane; before PB99 MOVE 1.2345678901234567890123E+3 stored 1234.56789012345685803008 and FROM 1.0E+3 set a 20-decimal item to 999.999…9161), and every position under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL (§8.8.1.5.2 r1). Inside a NATIVE arithmetic expression or statement the literal is a binary64 operand (numeric design D16 — §8.8.1.3's implementor-defined method; documented, CONFORMANCE.md §7 item 82).

subject: Figurative constant values
notes: kb/Work PB71 (2026-08-18): literal-1 is an alphanumeric (plain or hexadecimal), boolean or national literal, or a concatenation of them - ONE grammar arm (ALL allLiteral), ONE constructor (BoundAllLiteral.Of - the category rides on literal-1's class through CobolLiteral.ClassOf), the & fold per 8.8.3.3 GR2; a zero-length literal-1 is COBOLNET1648 and a mixed-class concatenation COBOLNET1540 (the version pass); the national/boolean literal-1 is the COBOL-2002 introduction below 2002 (COBOLNET0900). Before: ALL N"..." had no grammar arm, ALL B"..." parsed and died at run time, VALUE refused NX"..."/BX"..." and every ALL literal (a raw-text classifier).

subject: Figurative constant values
notes: kb/Work PB110 (2026-08-19): ALL symbolic-character-1 with an undeclared name is COBOLNET1670 citing this rule; a declared one substitutes (the golden's ALL-ZED line). The BARE form is a word reference — an undeclared word is the ordinary undefined-reference diagnostic.

subject: Figurative constant values
notes: kb/Work PB110 (2026-08-19): the figurative fill — repeated character by character to the associated item's size, then right-truncated — over a VALUE clause (VAL-FILL3: position 3 of a PIC X(3) VALUE BELL holds the character) and a fixed-length MOVE receiver (MOVE-FILL: position 4 of an X(4)); the ALL-literal fill of PB71's golden is the same rule over a longer literal-1. One node (BoundAllLiteral) carries the semantics for the classic figuratives, ALL literal-1 and the symbolic characters alike.

subject: Figurative constant values
notes: kb/Work PB110 (2026-08-19): where the context does not size the string — a) in a concatenation, one character (the ConcatFolder figurative arm); b) a figurative other than ALL literal-1, one character (the golden's STRING-SC line: a bare symbolic character contributes ONE character to STRING); c) ALL literal-1, the literal's length (PB71's golden).

subject: Function-identifier
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB61 — the LENGTH/BYTE-LENGTH folds enumerated from the rule branches; one builder for a runtime-length group; SR6 decided from the definition before binding). SR6 'if a function's definition permits arguments and a left parenthesis immediately follows … the left parenthesis is always treated as the left parenthesis of that function's arguments' — decided ONCE, from the DEFINITION (the catalog signature, or a REPOSITORY user function's USING formals — SR6 names function-prototype-name-1 too) and BEFORE any argument binds, on every route: FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (1:4) drew the §15.3 arity error (the empty list bound first; only RANDOM, MinArgs 0, reached the SR6 arm) and keyword-omitted UPPER-CASE (1:4) under FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC died as 'not defined' (the MinArgs guard sent it to the data path). Now COBOLNET1543 (SR6/SR8) on all of them; ResultRefMod no longer carries an SR6 arm. Negatives pb61-sr6-function-keyword-refmod (85+), pb61-sr6-keyword-omitted-refmod and pb61-sr6-udf-prototype-refmod (2002+); FunctionRefModSr6SweepTests sweeps the CATALOG — every argument-permitting row in both forms draws 1543 (never 1504/1639), every zero-argument row (CURRENT-DATE (1:8), the standard's own D.14.3.6 shape) does not.

subject: Reference-modification
notes: kb/Work PB70 (2026-08-18): the SR1 list is ONE exclusion rule (RefModExclusion) at bind - COBOLNET1647 for a strongly-typed or variable-length (8.5.1.12) group, a numeric item of a non-DISPLAY/NATIONAL usage, an edited/numeric leaf subordinate to a strongly-typed group, an index item, a pointer, an object reference; an admitted GROUP is viewed through its character image (GroupImagePlace). Residues: a numeric item of usage NATIONAL (admitted by SR1) has no national image channel yet (loud stage); bit and national GROUPS read as ordinary groups until GROUP-USAGE is modelled (PB79).

subject: Reference-modification
notes: The POSITIVE half (a function-identifier IS admissible as identifier-1) and the NEGATIVE half (it shall be an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function) are both enforced. Before fix-queue PB8 the shape was a COBOL0001 parse error at every edition, so neither half could be reached. A non-conforming class is rejected with COBOLNET1629; national and alphanumeric results are covered by the golden, and the user-defined-function result reference-modifies through RefModPlace using the RETURNING item's own category.

subject: Reference-modification
notes: Found unenforced by the PB8 sibling sweep, not by PB8's own repro: MOVE A (3:4)(2:2) COMPILED CLEAN and silently returned A(2:2), because dataReferenceSuffix* admits unlimited ref-mods and the resolver kept only the first of each carrier while the DEFAULT-mode form outranked the SUBSCRIPT-mode one. Now counted in ONE place per reference kind and rejected with COBOLNET1630. A subscript followed by a ref-mod (the legal 8.4.3.1.4 GR1 a-to-g order) is unaffected.

subject: Reference-modification
notes: kb/Work PB73 (adjudicated 2026-08-18): leftmost-position is a boolean position for a boolean item — in EITHER form (GR5a makes the positions bits under USAGE BIT and characters otherwise): a BIT-form slice moves bits 2-3 into a boolean receiver (01) and INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN(BB4(1:3)) = 5; a DISPLAY-form slice is the same class-boolean unique item over character positions (INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN(B4(2:3)) = 2). An alphanumeric position for an alphanumeric item; a national position for a national one.

subject: Reference-modification

subject: Reference-modification
notes: kb/Work PB70 + PB73 (2026-08-18): the unique data item is elementary, without JUSTIFIED, and has the same class, category, and usage as that DEFINED for identifier-1 except the EXHAUSTIVE list — (a) alphanumeric-edited → alphanumeric (the RB leg: an edited slice moves to a boolean receiver), (b) national-edited → national (a staged skeleton), (c) numeric / numeric-edited → national under a national usage, alphanumeric otherwise (RefModPlace.CategoryOf's one rewrite arm) — so a boolean slice (bit- or display-form) stays boolean and an alphabetic slice stays alphabetic (Table16Operand.Of(Place)'s rider); PB72's 2026-08-09 reading (every display-form view alphanumeric) is reversed by PB73. notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB129): the _outermost final-transfer flag is now cleared by EVERY recursion - BoundNegate, BoundPower and BoundComputedOperand join BoundBinary - so a division under a unary minus, an exponent base or an operand wrapper computes at the D2 guard scale with truncation and the receiver's ROUNDED mode binds to the final transfer only (14.7.4.3 GR3-GR10; 8.8.1.2 r1's treated-as-a-single-operand). Pinned twice: (1/3) ** 0 under PROHIBITED is exactly 1.00 (the CA5 sibling - the leak reinstated the pre-CA5 spurious EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION), and (A/B) ** 2 = 1 * (A/B) ** 2 = 11.1111 (the leak made multiplying by one change the value).

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: Citation re-validated INDEPENDENTLY: `--check 8.8.1.2 "When operands are at the same level of inclusiveness, the following hierarchical order of execution is implied"` => OK §8.8.1.2 2); the four ranks are at specs/ISO_COBOL.md under that rule (1st unary +/-, 2nd exponentiation, 3rd multiplication and division, 4th addition and subtraction). || UPHELD (the grammar read, re-done from the file rather than from the adjudicator's quotation): `arithmeticExpression : additiveExpression`; `additiveExpression : multiplicativeExpression ( addOp multiplicativeExpression )*`; `multiplicativeExpression : powerExpression ( mulOp powerExpression )*`; `powerExpression : unaryExpression ( POWER unaryExpression )*`; `unaryExpression : addOp unaryExpression | primaryExpression`; `addOp : PLUS | MINUS`; `mulOp : STAR | SLASH` — four strata in the standard's order, with unary INSIDE the power operand, so `- A ** 2` is powerExpression(unary(`- A`), POWER, unary(`2`)) = (-A)**2 and rank 1 sits above rank 2 as the standard (unusually) requires. `ExpressionBinder.BindExprCore` has one arm per context type and re-derives no precedence. ADVERSARIAL PROBE THE ADJUDICATOR DID NOT RUN: `primaryExpression`'s `numericLiteral` is `signedNumericLiteral : (PLUS | MINUS)? numericLiteralCore`, so for `- 2 ** 2` BOTH `unaryExpression` alternatives are viable and the parse depends on ANTLR resolving the ambiguity to the lowest-numbered alternative rather than on anything the grammar states. I traced both outcomes: alt 1 gives BoundNegate(BoundNumLiteral "2") -> `Negate` -> NumX("(-2)", scale 0) and alt 2 gives BoundNumLiteral("-2"), and `Power`'s `integerOperands` arm sends both to `PowNativeIntDec` with base -2, so the VALUE is 4 either way — not a defect, but the rank-1-over-rank-2 ordering for a LITERAL base is a coincidence of ANTLR's tie-break, not a stated property, which is a further reason this boundary needs a pinned golden. For an IDENTIFIER base (`- A ** 2`) alt 2 cannot match at all, so the ordering is structural there. || REFUTED (the verdict, not the read): the adjudicator's own notes state 'NOT PINNED BY ANY TEST: rank 1 over rank 2 … and rank 2 over rank 3' and then record CONFORMS. Ground rule 5 is explicit — an edge unverified is PARTIAL. I confirmed the gap myself: 2023/pb18_native_power_exact_and_rule6 and 2023/pb65_power_receiver contain `2 ** -2`, `2 ** XN`, `A ** 2`, `10 ** 30`, `N ** 3`, `1.5 ** 2` — every one a unary EXPONENT (the Table-3 (operator, unary) cell), never a unary BASE; and no golden in tests/conformance evaluates `2 ** 3 * 4`. WHICH HALF IS UNVERIFIED: rank 1 above rank 2 (`- 2 ** 2` must be +4, not -4) and rank 2 above rank 3 (`2 ** 3 * 4` must be 32, not 4096). VERIFIED HALF: rank 3 above rank 4, by conformance:2014/func_expr_arg, which I read in full — its header cites §8.4.3.2 SR8 / §8.8.1 and its `ORD=00034` line (`FUNCTION ORD(FUNCTION CHAR(66 / 2 + 1))`, .out asserts 00034) genuinely discriminates, since `66/(2+1)` would answer 22. || CROSS-RULE EFFECT (see GR-8.8.1.2-1): the two ranks with no test are precisely the two whose visitor arms leak `NumericRenderer._outermost` — `Visit(BoundNegate)` (rank 1) and `Visit(BoundPower)` (rank 2) — so a rank-1 or rank-2 operation applied to a parenthesized quotient consumes an operand that was already rounded as if it were the statement's final transfer. The ORDER of execution is right; the operand handed to the operation is not. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a spec-derived golden asserting `COMPUTE R = - 2 ** 2` = 4 and `COMPUTE R = 2 ** 3 * 4` = 32, with an identifier base as well as a literal one so the ANTLR tie-break is not what is being measured. Editions: I scanned Annex E and found no change item for §8.8.1.2; the four-rank list is unchanged since COBOL-85, so the batch default applies.

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: Citation re-validated INDEPENDENTLY: `--check 8.8.1.2 "the order of execution of consecutive operations of the same hierarchical level is from left to right"` => OK §8.8.1.2 3). || UPHELD, with my own evidence rather than the adjudicator's. Derived first: every level left-folds, exponentiation included — the standard states no right-associativity exception for `**`, so `2 ** 3 ** 2` = (2**3)**2 = 64, not 512. READ: `ExpressionBinder.BindChain` is `foreach (var child in StatementBinder.Children(node)) { if (child is AddOpContext or MulOpContext) op = child.GetText()[0]; else { var x = BindExprCore(child, context); acc = acc is null ? x : new BoundBinary(acc, op, x); } }` — a strict left fold serving BOTH AdditiveExpressionContext and MultiplicativeExpressionContext; and `ExpressionBinder.BindPower` is `acc = BindExprCore(bases[0], context); for (int i = 1; i < bases.Length; i++) acc = new BoundPower(acc, BindExprCore(bases[i], context));` — the same left fold for rank 2. I ALSO CHECKED THE CHILD ENUMERATOR the adjudicator took on trust: `StatementBinder.Children` is `for (int i = 0; i < node.ChildCount; i++) yield return node.GetChild(i);` — plain index order, no filtering, so no operand can be skipped and no pair re-ordered. `CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator.EvalArith`, the only other walker of this tree, left-folds identically over `node.ChildCount`. || TEST EVIDENCE VERIFIED BY READING BOTH GOLDENS AND THEIR .out FILES, not by trusting the citation: (a) tests/conformance/2014/func_expr_arg.cob header says verbatim '** folds LEFT per 8.8.1.2 r3', its body has `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION MAX(2 ** 3 ** 2, 1)` and func_expr_arg.out asserts `POW=00064` — right-folding gives 512, so it discriminates rank 2 and cites this exact rule; (b) tests/conformance/2002/arith_standard.cob has `COMPUTE W1 = 2 / 7 * 7` into PIC 9V9(5) with hand-derived §8.8.1.5 arithmetic in the header, and arith_standard.out asserts `W1=200000` — `2/(7*7)` = 0.0408 would print 004081, so rank 3 left-to-right is pinned, in the SDIDI lane. Both are spec-derived (hand-derived expectations, ISO citations in the headers), neither is a differential, neither is nist:/characterization:/MatchesLegacy. Rank 4 (`A - B - C`) has no golden, but it is the SAME `BindChain` loop already discriminated at rank 3 by (b) — associativity is decided once, in the binder, and no renderer re-associates (I verified `CombineCore` emits self-parenthesized forms only). Rank 1 is prefix-unary, where 'left to right' has no content. || I ALSO CHECKED THE SUBSCRIPT FAST PATH, a second evaluator the adjudicator did not consider: `ReferenceResolver.RenderSegment` splices `+ - * / ( )` into C# text, and C# gives those operators the same precedence and the same left associativity as COBOL, and `**` has no case arm so it routes to the D18 materializer — so rule 3's ORDER holds there too. (That path's VALUE defect — C# integer division — is recorded against GR-8.8.1.2-1; it is not an ordering defect.) The `_outermost` leak recorded against GR-8.8.1.2-1 likewise does not touch associativity. Editions: no Annex E change item for §8.8.1.2 (scanned); batch default.

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: Citation re-validated INDEPENDENTLY: `--check 8.8.1.2 "The ways in which identifiers, literals, operators, and parentheses may be combined in arithmetic expressions are summarized in Table 3"` => OK §8.8.1.2 4). I re-read Table 3 in specs/ISO_COBOL.md together with its repaired table note (rows = first symbol, columns = second; 'P' permissible, '—' invalid) rather than the input file's rendering. || UPHELD, and independently reproduced: the divergent cell is row 'Unary + or −' x column 'Unary + or −' = '—'. `unaryExpression : addOp unaryExpression | primaryExpression` is DIRECTLY self-recursive on its first alternative, so `- - A`, `+ - A` and any number of stacked signs parse, and `ExpressionBinder.BindExprCore`'s arm `Core.UnaryExpressionContext u => u.primaryExpression() is { } pr ? BindExprCore(pr, context) : u.addOp().GetText() == "-" ? new BoundNegate(BindExprCore(u.unaryExpression(), context)) : BindExprCore(u.unaryExpression(), context)` recurses and wraps a second BoundNegate, with no diagnostic at any --std or strictness setting. || NEW EVIDENCE THE ADJUDICATOR DID NOT HAVE — THERE ARE TWO ACCEPTING PATHS, NOT ONE: `CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator.EvalArith`'s `Core.UnaryExpressionContext` arm (`var inner = EvalArith(u.unaryExpression(), where); return inner is null ? null : u.addOp().GetText() == "-" ? -inner : inner;`) recurses through the same self-recursion, so a §7.3.6 compile-time arithmetic expression (`>>IF`, `>>EVALUATE`, CONSTANT) accepts `- - 2` as well. Any gate added for this cell has to cover both walkers, which is why PARTIAL rather than CONFORMS is the honest label even though the leniency is over-acceptance. Framing check: §4.2.10 item 1 makes an accepted element not defined in the standard a NONSTANDARD EXTENSION, which §4.2.10 requires to be documented; this one is undocumented and ungated, contrary to the project's dialect-gating doctrine. || THE OTHER TWELVE '—' CELLS: I re-derived their unreachability rather than inheriting it. (id|lit, id|lit), (')' , id|lit), (')' , '(') have no juxtaposition production inside `arithmeticExpression` (juxtaposition exists only in `functionArgList` and the SUBSCRIPT-mode `subToken+` capture, which are §15.3 / §8.4.2.3 constructs); (op, op), (unary, op), ('(', op) cannot occur because every operator loop requires an operand between operators; (op, ')'), (unary, ')'), ('(', ')') cannot occur because `LPAREN arithmeticExpression RPAREN` has a non-empty body; (id|lit, '(') is absorbed by `dataReference`'s `subscriptPart`/`refModPart` suffixes, which are part of the identifier; (id|lit, unary) and (')' , unary) resolve to the 'P' cells (id|lit, op) and (')' , op) because DEFAULT lexer mode emits PLUS/MINUS and the SIGNED_INTEGERLIT/SIGNED_DECIMALLIT twins exist only in the SUBSCRIPT and function-argument regions. I VERIFIED the one premise the adjudicator asserted without checking — `numericLiteral : signedNumericLiteral : (PLUS | MINUS)? numericLiteralCore` DOES admit a signed literal in DEFAULT mode as a `primaryExpression`, so a sign after an operand is genuinely ambiguous at the grammar level; ANTLR's lowest-alternative tie-break sends it to the `addOp` loop, which is the 'P' reading, so no new over-acceptance arises there. || NO TEST AT ALL, measured not assumed: I listed tests/conformance/negative (757 files) and grepped every .cob for a doubled sign and for '8.8.1.2' / 'Table 3' across tests/conformance — the only files naming §8.8.1.2 are 2014/func_expr_arg, 2014/options_paragraph, 2023/pb13_float_quantize_siblings, 2023/pb18_native_power_exact_and_rule6 and 2023/pb65_power_receiver, all positive goldens about other rules. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a negative fixture rejecting `- - A` with a §8.8.1.2 r4 / Table 3 diagnostic (dialect-gated if the leniency is kept) that ALSO covers the compile-time walker, plus a negative sweep over the remaining twelve '—' cells so their unreachability becomes measured. AUTHORITY NOTE, upheld: the OCR bias was falsely-RESTRICTIVE, so any transcription error in a permissions table would turn 'P' into '—' and could only widen this same over-acceptance finding. Editions: no Annex E change item for §8.8.1.2 (scanned); batch default.

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB136): both defects of the D10 transitional subscript evaluator closed. (1) The splitter's new-segment logic now handles a depth-0 '(' - after ')' or a literal it always opens a NEW subscript; after an IDENTIFIER the split is DECLARATION-INFORMED (a name with no OCCURS cannot be subscripted, so its '(' begins the parenthesized-expression subscript the spec's own NOTE 2 prints, while `DOG (BAKER (I) 3)` keeps BAKER's paren as its own subscript) - the rule-5 restructuring the batch-8 note asked for, threaded as an optional predicate so the intrinsic-argument caller keeps its exact behavior. (2) A quotient-bearing segment routes to the D18 exact evaluator UNCONDITIONALLY: the old token splice was C# integer division over long reads, so an all-integer quotient truncated silently where GR1b evaluates the exact result - (3+4)/2 = 3.5 now raises the EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT fatal when checking is on (probed verbatim) and takes the documented lenient truncation otherwise. PB41's scaled-operand routing caught only segments with scaled OPERANDS; the all-integer quotient was exactly the case it could not see.

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: CONFORMS as of 2026-08-03 (fix-queue PB28, landed this session). Rule 6 has three parts. r6a (zero base requires exponent > 0) and r6c (negative base requires an integer exponent) are mandatory 'shall' requirements setting EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION, Fatal in Table 14. BEFORE the fix the STANDARD-DECIMAL arm enforced both (CobolDec.Pow) and EVERY NATIVE arm enforced neither, so the same program answered differently depending only on whether an ARITHMETIC clause was present: 0 ** 0 returned 1 (IEEE's convention, not COBOL's) and -2 ** 0.5 returned 0 (Math.Pow yields NaN and the quantizer made it zero), both with an ON SIZE ERROR phrase present and NOT taken. CheckPowRule6 now screens every native arm. MEASURED ACROSS EVERY REACHABLE COMBINATION, not sampled: native at --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023, and ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL at 2023 - all five raise both legs and leave the receiver unmodified per SS14.7.5. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is loudly refused (COBOLNET0806), so that arm is unreachable rather than unverified. r6b ('if the evaluation yields both a positive and a negative real number, the value returned is the positive number') is a SELECTION rule, not a screen, and cannot arise here: both bodies (CobolIntrinsics.PowNativeInt / PowNativeReal and CobolDec.Pow) yield a single value. Checked in the same pass rather than left to be discovered as a fourth leg.

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: Citation re-validated INDEPENDENTLY: `--check 8.8.1.2 "Arithmetic expressions allow the user to combine arithmetic operations without the restrictions on composite of operands and receiving data items"` => OK §8.8.1.2 7). || UPHELD, and I re-derived the exempting rule from the spec text rather than from the adjudicator's paraphrase: §14.7.7 rule 2 reads 'For ADD, DIVIDE, MULTIPLY, and SUBTRACT statements when native arithmetic is in effect … the composite of operands shall not contain more than 31 digits', with 'The composite of operands is a hypothetical data item resulting from the superimposition of specified operands in a statement aligned on their decimal points' — COMPUTE is absent from that list, and because the composite superimposes ALL the statement's specified operands (which for `ADD a TO b` includes the receiver b), the single absence covers BOTH halves of rule 7, the operand half and the receiving-data-item half. || EVIDENCE, re-run: `grep -rn CheckComposite src/Cobol.Net.Compiler --include=*.cs` gives `StatementValidation.CheckComposite` as the ONE implementation and ELEVEN call sites — ADD x2, SUBTRACT x2, MULTIPLY x2, DIVIDE x4 (all in ArithmeticBinder) and CorrespondingBinder once. REFUTED IN THE NOTES (not the verdict): the adjudicator wrote 'exactly seven invocations' and then enumerated eleven; the enumeration is right and the count was a slip, corrected here so the next reader does not inherit it. `ArithmeticBinder.BindCompute` calls it ZERO times — after the Format-2 boolean re-routes it is `var rhs = host.Expr.BindExpr(expr); return new BoundCompute(rhs, host.Expr.Receivers(compute.computeStore()), host.BindSizeError(compute.computeOnSizeError()));` — no digit gate on the expression and none on the resultant identifiers. || THE PROBE THE ADJUDICATOR DID NOT RUN, which is what makes this a read rather than an absence-of-evidence: I enumerated the OTHER digit gate as well. `grep -rn CheckDigitCapacity` across src/Cobol.Net.Compiler and src/Cobol.Net.Frontend returns exactly two call sites — `DataBinder` on `pic.DigitPositions` (the PICTURE formation rule) and `ExpressionBinder.CheckLiteral` on a numeric literal's own digit count (§8.3.1.2, 1..18 at '85, 1..31 at 2002+). Neither is a composite of operands and neither is driven by a COMPUTE receiver, so no second gate reintroduces the restriction on the expression path. || HONEST QUALIFICATION, upheld as not a divergence: the expression path does impose the documented implementor-defined intermediate (`NumericRenderer.DeU` -> `CobolNum.Widen`, the Int128 lane, and CobolDec's decimal128 bounds under a standard mode), which is §8.8.1.3 / §8.8.1.5.2 latitude recorded in CONFORMANCE.md — a precision limit on the intermediate, not a syntactic restriction on how operations may be combined. || NO QUALIFYING TEST (CONFORMS-but-untested, a legitimate outcome under ground rule 3): conformance:2023/ca4_giving_composite pins the ADD/SUBTRACT Format-2 composite EXCLUSION (§14.9.2.3 SR1b), i.e. the statement side; nothing in the corpus contrasts a legal COMPUTE against an illegal ADD over the same operands. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a spec-derived golden with two operands whose superimposed composite exceeds 31 digits (e.g. PIC 9(20)V9(11) each) where `COMPUTE R = A + B` compiles and runs to a hand-derived value, paired with the existing negative posture for `ADD A TO B` over the same items. Editions: no Annex E change item for §8.8.1.2 (scanned); batch default.

subject: Standard-binary arithmetic
notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 8.8.1.4.2 'Any operand of an arithmetic expression that is not already in SBIDI is converted into SBIDI form'` -> OK (§8.8.1.4.2 rule 1). Expected behavior derived BEFORE reading code: when standard-binary arithmetic is in effect every operand is lifted into an SBIDI (a binary128-equivalent carrier, §8.8.1.4.2 paragraph 3 + NOTE 3: 113-bit significand, exponent range 2**-16494..2**16384), inexact lifts rounding per §11.9.11 (whose rule 2a implies NEAREST-EVEN under this mode). READ: DataBinder.BindDeclarations, DataBinder.cs:318-320 -- `if (Options.Arithmetic == ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary) Edition.Error('COBOLNET0806', 'ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is an obsolete feature ... and is not supported; use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL')`. READ EditionContext.Error (EditionContext.cs:109): `Diagnostics.Add($'{Prefix()}error {code}: ...')` -- unconditional, no severity policy, no --permissive downgrade path, so the mode is a hard compile failure at EVERY edition and strictness; ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary is produced ONLY by OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf (OptionsBinder.cs:68). CONSEQUENCE: no operand is ever converted to SBIDI because no SBIDI exists -- I grepped src/ for the §8.8.1.4.2 NOTE 3 range constants (16384, 16271, 16382, 16494) and for `SBIDI`: ZERO hits outside comments; the only 128-bit floating carrier named anywhere is Usage.FloatBinary128, itself rejected COBOLNET1564 (PictureAnalyzer.cs:588, Annex A.3 item 17 processor-dependent non-support). The rounding half is unimplemented independently: OptionsModel.IntermediateRounding (OptionsModel.cs:44) defaults UNCONDITIONALLY to CobolRounding.NearestAwayFromZero with the comment citing '§11.9.11 r3' -- the standard-DECIMAL rule -- and there is no ArithmeticMode arm anywhere that supplies §11.9.11.2 rule 2a's NEAREST-EVEN default for standard-binary. Editions derived from the spec, NOT from ConstructRegistry: F.2 item 3 newly designates 'STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item' obsolete in this edition (an element must have been a live facility in the prior edition to be newly designated obsolete), and E.2 item 21 records that the 2002-era 'Standard Arithmetic' mode -- the clause alternative STANDARD-BINARY/-DECIMAL superseded -- is removed at 2023; the OPTIONS paragraph does not exist at 85. Hence 2014,2023. WHAT WOULD CLOSE THE ROW: either an SBIDI carrier (a real or emulated binary128 with §11.9.11.2 r2 rounding) plus a spec-derived golden that shows an inexact decimal operand (0.1) landing as the nearest-even 113-bit approximation, OR an explicit OWNER decision recording documented-non-support under §4.2.6 / A.3 item 2 (see the finding note on GR-8.8.1.4.4-4). Per ground rule 6 the documented-non-support disposition is not mine to award, so the verdict is NOT-IMPLEMENTED. NOT cited as closing evidence: conformance-test:StandardDecimalTests.StandardBinary_DocumentedUnsupported pins the REJECTION (COBOLNET0806 + the word 'obsolete'), i.e. it is a green test holding this gap open, never evidence for this rule's behavior. || UPHELD: verdict, code-location and editions all re-derived independently. (a) I re-read §8.8.1.4.2 in the spec at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:7947-7982 -- rule 1 and NOTE 3 are verbatim as quoted, and NOTE 3's range constants are exactly the four I grepped. (b) My own grep of src/ for `SBIDI` returns ONE hit and it is a comment (CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs:666: 'standard-binary (cap 35) is unreachable (COBOLNET0806 rejects ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY outright; its SBIDI range joins this map if that ever lands)'); my grep for 16384|16494|16382|16271 across src/ returns NOTHING. No carrier exists. (c) I confirmed the gate is unconditional by reading the ONE severity funnel rather than assuming: ConstructRegistry.Check (src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ConstructRegistry.cs:30) is the only edition-gating entry point and DataBinder's 0806 does not go through it at all -- it is a bare EditionContext.Error at DataBinder.cs:318, and EditionContext.Error is EditionContext.cs:109 exactly as stated. (d) Editions: I validated the two Annex anchors myself -- F.2's preamble at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:44050-44057 ('A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements except for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent') with item 3 at :44067, and E.2 item 21 at :43077-43083 (the removed list is FLAG-85, FLAG-NATIVE-ARITHMETIC, Standard Arithmetic, MOVE of QUOTE). 2014,2023 stands: 2023 still defines the facility (obsolete, not removed), 2014 is the edition in which STANDARD-BINARY/-DECIMAL split the mode that E.2 item 21 says was 'classified as obsolete in the previous COBOL standard', and the OPTIONS paragraph itself is a 2002 introduction so 85 is impossible. || REFUTED (new finding, NOT a verdict change -- it makes the row WORSE, not better): the rule's own PRECONDITION cannot be expressed in five of the seven source-unit kinds. §8.8.1.4.1 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:7935) makes standard-binary arithmetic 'in effect when the STANDARD-BINARY phrase of the ARITHMETIC clause is specified in the OPTIONS paragraph', and the spec puts `[ options-paragraph ]` in EVERY source-unit skeleton -- §10.6.1 prints it under program-prototype, function-prototype, program-definition, function-definition, class-definition, factory-definition, instance-definition, interface-definition AND method-definition (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:11028-11207), and §11.2.1's identification-division general format (:11319-11337) shows `[ options-paragraph ]` following the brace of all seven id paragraphs. READ THE GRAMMAR: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:92-94 `identificationBody : programIdParagraph identificationParagraph* | functionIdParagraph identificationParagraph*` is the ONLY production that reaches `identificationParagraph` (:153) and hence `optionsParagraph` (:169) -- confirmed by grepping the whole Grammar/ tree: `identificationParagraph` appears at exactly those three lines. src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolOO.g4's `classDefinition` (:18-24), `factoryParagraph` (:31-37), `objectParagraph` (:52-58), `interfaceDefinition` (:72-79) and `methodDefinition` (:81-89) admit NO options paragraph. So `CLASS-ID. C. OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY.` is a bare ANTLR SYNTAX ERROR, not COBOLNET0806 -- the compiler never identifies the unsupported processor-dependent element there, and the same production gap also rejects the SUPPORTED clauses (ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL, DEFAULT ROUNDED, INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING, ENTRY-CONVENTION -- which spec line 42527 says explicitly 'may be specified in the OPTIONS paragraph of a class' and 'of an interface or prototype' -- FLOAT-BINARY, FLOAT-DECIMAL, INITIALIZE) in every class, factory, object, method and interface definition. This is a rejects-legal-source defect; no kb/Work note covers it (grep of kb/Work for 'OPTIONS paragraph' returns only PB3, which is about ORD and the collating table).

subject: Standard-binary arithmetic
notes: Rule re-read in context and cross-read at its target clause: §14.7.5's size-error case list (spec lines 21770-21784) -- case 6 is 'if standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, when an arithmetic operation on the intermediate data item would cause the new value to be outside of the range allowed for a standard-binary intermediate data item'; case 5 is the native leg and case 7 the standard-decimal leg. Expected behavior: an SBIDI overflow raises the size error condition + EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW, an underflow EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW, bounded by the §8.8.1.4.2 NOTE 3 range. READ: the exception names EXIST (ExceptionCatalog.cs:186/190 register EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION and EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW as level-3 Fatal), and the SIBLING legs are implemented -- CobolDec (CobolDec.cs:59, :125, :423, :431) raises EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW/-UNDERFLOW citing §8.8.1.5.2 r2, the decimal128 SDIDI range (§14.7.5 case 7), and CobolNum.cs:292 raises the native D1 escape-boundary overflow (§14.7.5 case 5). NO code implements case 6: grep of src/ for the SBIDI bound constants (2**16384 / 2**16271 / 2**-16494 / 2**-16382) returns nothing, and no range check anywhere is keyed on ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary. The gate is upstream anyway: DataBinder.BindDeclarations (DataBinder.cs:318-320) fails the compile with COBOLNET0806 before any statement is bound, so the mode's arithmetic never executes. BOTH halves unimplemented (overflow AND underflow), so this is not a PARTIAL. Editions 2014,2023 by the F.2 item 3 / E.2 item 21 derivation recorded on GR-8.8.1.4.2-1. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an SBIDI intermediate with its §8.8.1.4.2 NOTE 3 bounds checked at every arithmetic step, plus goldens driving one overflow (2**16384-scale product) and one underflow (below 2**-16494) under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY with and without ON SIZE ERROR. No qualifying test today. || UPHELD: I re-read §14.7.5's case list at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:21764-21784 myself -- case 6 is verbatim as quoted and is the ONLY standard-binary leg; case 1 ('if the rules for evaluation of exponentiation are violated') and the no-SIZE-ERROR-phrase rule 1 below it are the EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION route used by GR-8.8.1.4.4-4. I independently confirmed the two halves are absent and the sibling legs present: `grep -rn 'EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW|EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW' src/Cobol.Net.Runtime` shows ExceptionCatalog.cs:188 L3('EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW', EcFatality.Fatal) and :190 L3('EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW', EcFatality.Fatal) (the adjudicator wrote :186/:190; :186 is EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION and :188 is EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW -- a one-line slip, not a substantive error), and `grep -rn '16384|16494|16382|16271' src/ --include=*.cs` returns EMPTY, so no SBIDI bound is checked anywhere. PARTIAL was considered and rejected on the same grounds the adjudicator gives: neither the overflow nor the underflow half exists, and ground rule 5's 'one of two halves verified => PARTIAL' needs at least one half implemented. The rule is unreachable behind the DataBinder.cs:318 gate regardless.

subject: Standard-binary arithmetic
notes: The rule delegates wholly to §11.9.11, so I read §11.9.11.2 (spec lines 11970-11990) rather than stopping at the pointer: rule 2 is the standard-binary block -- a) NEAREST-EVEN implied when the INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING clause is absent; b) NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO SHALL NOT be specified; c) NEAREST-EVEN rounds to the nearest exactly-representable SBIDI value whose rightmost bit is zero; d) PROHIBITED + inexact => EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION and undefined results; e) TRUNCATION rounds toward zero. READ: OptionsBinder.cs:60-61 maps the clause through RoundingModes.MapIntermediate into OptionsModel.IntermediateRounding; OptionsModel.cs:41-44 gives that property the unconditional default `CobolRounding.NearestAwayFromZero`, its doc comment citing '§11.9.11 r3' -- the standard-DECIMAL rule 3a default. There is NO arm on ArithmeticMode anywhere in the default: rule 2a's NEAREST-EVEN implication is absent, and rule 2b's prohibition on NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO under standard-binary is never checked (grep of src/ for IntermediateRounding returns exactly the six sites above plus NumericRenderer.IntermediateMode at NumericRenderer.cs:396, which stringifies the mode into the CobolDec calls and is reached only from the StandardDecimal routing). Rules 2c/2d/2e cannot exist without an SBIDI, which does not exist (see GR-8.8.1.4.2-1). Compounding it, DataBinder.BindDeclarations rejects the mode outright (COBOLNET0806), so none of this is reachable. Editions 2014,2023 (same derivation). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a standard-binary arm on the IntermediateRounding default (NEAREST-EVEN), a COBOLNET diagnostic for rule 2b, SBIDI-level implementations of 2c/2d/2e, and goldens per leg. Deliberately NOT cited: StandardDecimalTests.StandardBinary_DocumentedUnsupported (pins the rejection, not the rounding). || UPHELD: I read §11.9.11.2 myself at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:11970-12000 -- rule 2's five sub-items are exactly as the adjudicator renders them (2a NEAREST-EVEN implied, 2b NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO shall not be specified, 2c rightmost-bit-zero, 2d PROHIBITED => EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION + undefined, 2e TRUNCATION toward zero), and rule 3a is the standard-DECIMAL NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO default. READ OptionsModel.cs:41-44: `public CobolRounding IntermediateRounding { get; init; } = CobolRounding.NearestAwayFromZero;` with the doc comment 'Default ... when absent (§11.9.11 r3)' -- unconditional, no ArithmeticMode arm, exactly as claimed; and OptionsBinder.cs:61 `if (c.intermediateRoundingClause()?.intermediateRoundingMode() is { } ir) return m with { IntermediateRounding = RoundingModes.MapIntermediate(ir) };` has no mode-awareness either, so rule 2b's prohibition genuinely has no enforcement site. NEW FINDING (minor, citation hygiene -- CLAUDE.md rule 1's exact failure mode): that doc comment's '§11.9.11 r3' is written ONE LEVEL SHORT -- §11.9.11 has no numbered rules; the rule is §11.9.11.2 rule 3 a). The same short form appears on OptionsModel.DefaultRounding ('§11.9.6 r2', where the rules live in §11.9.6.3) and on OptionsModel.Arithmetic ('§11.9.5.2 r4', which IS correct). Cosmetic today, but it is the citation shape the project has twice let propagate into goldens.

subject: Standard-binary arithmetic
notes: Expected behavior derived first: under standard-binary, operand-1 ** 0 with operand-1 nonzero yields exactly the SBIDI value 1 (§8.8.1.4.4 rule 1). READ: NumericRenderer.Power (NumericRenderer.cs:544-553) is the ONE exponentiation dispatch. Its standard arm is `if (StandardDecimal) return new NumX(RuntimeApi.DecPow(DecOperand(b), DecOperand(e), IntermediateMode), 0, Dec: true);` and `internal bool StandardDecimal => ctx.Data.Options.Arithmetic is ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal or ArithmeticMode.Standard` (NumericRenderer.cs:559). ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary is NOT in that set -- the two-arm dispatch has a standard-decimal arm and a native default, and no standard-binary arm; a StandardBinary compile would fall through to the native Int128/binary64 path (CombineNative / PowNativeInt), which is a DIFFERENT algorithm from the SBIDI one this rule mandates. That fall-through is unreachable today only because DataBinder.BindDeclarations (DataBinder.cs:318-320) fails the compile with COBOLNET0806 first -- and I verified the unreachability by reading, not assuming: EditionContext.Error (EditionContext.cs:109) is unconditional (`error {code}:`), has no --permissive branch, and OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf (OptionsBinder.cs:68) is the sole producer of the enum value. The §8.8.1.5.4 twin of this rule IS implemented (CobolDec.Pow, reached through RuntimeApi.DecPow) -- that is the structural template a standard-binary implementation would mirror, and its existence is why this row is NOT-IMPLEMENTED rather than merely unwritten. Editions 2014,2023 (F.2 item 3 / E.2 item 21 derivation). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an SBIDI Pow with rule 1's x**0 => 1 leg plus a golden under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY. No qualifying test. || UPHELD, with the line references corrected: I opened NumericRenderer.cs and read the dispatch myself. `private NumX Power(NumX b, NumX e, bool expIsNonNegativeLiteral = false)` is at line 543 (not 544), its standard arm `if (StandardDecimal) return new NumX(RuntimeApi.DecPow(DecOperand(b), DecOperand(e), IntermediateMode), 0, Dec: true);` at :551-552, and the predicate `internal bool StandardDecimal => ctx.Data.Options.Arithmetic is ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal or ArithmeticMode.Standard;` is at line 394, NOT :559 -- the adjudicator's :559 points into the middle of Power's comment block. The SUBSTANCE is exactly right: I enumerated every read of the mode in the whole tree (`grep -rn 'Options.Arithmetic' src/`) and got six sites -- ExpressionBinder.cs:666 and NumericRenderer.cs:394 test {StandardDecimal, Standard}; IntrinsicBinder.cs:2349/:2376/:2429 test StandardDecimal alone; IntrinsicBinder.cs:2356 is the only StandardBinary arm in the compiler and it is a §15.83.3-r3 usage BAN, not an arithmetic implementation; StatementValidation.cs:107 tests != Native. Nothing renders a standard-binary exponentiation, so rule 1's x**0 => 1 has no SBIDI implementation and the mode falls to the native default arm.

subject: Standard-binary arithmetic
notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 8.8.1.4.4 'the equivalent arithmetic expression is defined by the implementor'` -> OK (§8.8.1.4.4 rule 2, sub-item e). Expected behavior: for a positive exponent, integer exponents 1/2/3/4 have PINNED expansions (x; x*x; (x*x)*x; (x*x)*(x*x)) -- note d) is (x*x)*(x*x), not ((x*x)*x)*x, and the difference is observable in binary floating point because each multiplication rounds; every other positive exponent is implementor-defined but must be developed over SBIDI operands with each +,-,*,/ obeying ISO/IEC 60559:2020. READ: NumericRenderer.Power (NumericRenderer.cs:544-553) routes only `StandardDecimal` (= StandardDecimal or Standard, NumericRenderer.cs:559) to RuntimeApi.DecPow/CobolDec.Pow, whose header comment (NumericRenderer.cs:546-551) documents exactly this rule shape for the SDIDI twin: 'an integer exponent evaluates by repeated SDIDI multiplication (r2a-r2d exactly; r2e's implementor-defined form for larger integers ...)' citing §8.8.1.5.4. There is NO SBIDI counterpart: no ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary arm in Power, no SBIDI carrier in src (grep for SBIDI / the NOTE 3 range constants: nothing), and the mode is rejected at bind (DataBinder.cs:318-320, COBOLNET0806, unconditional per EditionContext.cs:109). Sub-item e) is an A.1-style implementor-defined element INSIDE an unimplemented facility, so it is not a separable NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION -- there is no expression to define because there is no mode. All five sub-items unimplemented; not a PARTIAL. Editions 2014,2023 (F.2 item 3 / E.2 item 21 derivation, not from ConstructRegistry). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an SBIDI Pow whose 1/2/3/4 legs emit the exact association the rule prints (a golden distinguishing (x*x)*(x*x) from ((x*x)*x)*x on a value where the roundings differ), plus a documented choice for e) recorded in CONFORMANCE.md. || UPHELD: I re-ran the citation myself -- `python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 8.8.1.4.4 'the equivalent arithmetic expression is defined by the implementor'` -> `OK  §8.8.1.4.4 2) b)  (Exponentiation in standard-binary arithmetic)` (the locator prints the enclosing rule 2's sub-item indexing; the matched line is sub-item e as quoted). I read §8.8.1.4.4 at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:7988-8038 and confirm the association the adjudicator flags: sub-item c) is '((operand-1 * operand-1) * operand-1)' and sub-item d) is '((operand-1 * operand-1) * (operand-1 * operand-1))' -- d) is the balanced tree, and under 60559 rounding that is observably different from a left-associated chain, so a future implementation cannot substitute a repeated-multiply loop for it. I also verified the NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION question the adjudicator disposed of: sub-item e is implementor-defined, but §4.2.5 makes implementor definition apply only 'to required normative elements ... and to optional language elements for which an implementor claims support' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:2128) -- support is not claimed here, so there is nothing to decide separately and NOT-IMPLEMENTED is correct rather than NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION. Line refs corrected as on GR-8.8.1.4.4-1 (Power at :543, StandardDecimal at :394).

subject: Standard-binary arithmetic
notes: Expected behavior: a negative exponent is evaluated as the SBIDI reciprocal 1 / (operand-1 ** FUNCTION ABS(operand-2)) -- i.e. the positive-exponent expansion of rule 2 is performed FIRST and the single division applied last, which is a different rounding sequence from repeated division. READ: NumericRenderer.Power (NumericRenderer.cs:544-553); the only standard-mode arm is `if (StandardDecimal)` -> RuntimeApi.DecPow, and the comment at NumericRenderer.cs:549 names 'r3's reciprocal for a negative exponent' for the §8.8.1.5.4 SDIDI twin implemented in CobolDec.Pow. Nothing implements the SBIDI form: ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary is absent from NumericRenderer.StandardDecimal (NumericRenderer.cs:559) and is rejected upstream by DataBinder.BindDeclarations (DataBinder.cs:318-320) with the unconditional COBOLNET0806 (EditionContext.cs:109 -- no permissive downgrade). No SBIDI carrier exists to divide in. Editions 2014,2023 (F.2 item 3 / E.2 item 21 derivation). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the SBIDI reciprocal leg plus a golden under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY where the single-division association is observable (e.g. 3 ** -3 vs three successive divisions). No qualifying test exists; StandardDecimalTests.StandardBinary_DocumentedUnsupported is not one (it asserts the compile FAILS). || UPHELD: rule 3 read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:8034 -- '(1 / (operand-1 ** FUNCTION ABS (operand-2)))', so the reciprocal is taken of the WHOLE rule-2 expansion, one division, and the adjudicator's rounding-sequence point is right. READ the cited comment myself: NumericRenderer.cs:546-551 is the block naming '§8.8.1.5.4 ... r3's reciprocal for a negative exponent ... The ONE runtime implementation is CobolDec.Pow' -- it is the SDIDI twin's comment and cites §8.8.1.5.4, never §8.8.1.4.4, so nothing in it can be stretched onto this row. I also read the native default arm below it (NumericRenderer.cs:554-575): it explicitly documents that a NEGATIVE or run-time exponent 'CANNOT LAND AT A COMPILE-TIME SCALE' and routes those shapes to the SDIDI carrier -- which is reachable only under {StandardDecimal, Standard}, confirming there is no standard-binary reciprocal path at all. Line refs corrected (:543 / :394 as above). I verified the closing-evidence claim by reading tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/StandardDecimalTests.cs:111-119: StandardBinary_DocumentedUnsupported compiles a PROGRAM-ID unit at --std 2023 and asserts `Assert.False(ok)` plus COBOLNET0806 -- a rejection test, correctly refused as closing evidence.

subject: Standard-binary arithmetic
notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 8.8.1.4.4 'EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION exception condition is set to exist'` -> OK (§8.8.1.4.4 rule 4). Expected behavior: 0 ** 0 under standard-binary sets EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION (level-3, Fatal per Table 14 / §14.7.5's no-phrase rule 1: 'if the rules for evaluation of exponentiation are violated'). READ: the exception EXISTS and the shape is implemented for the OTHER two modes -- CobolDec.Pow (CobolDec.cs:94-112) raises EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION on a zero base with a non-positive exponent, its message citing 'ISO §8.8.1.2 r6a / §8.8.1.5.4 r4' (CobolDec.cs:106), and on a negative base with a noninteger exponent citing §8.8.1.2 r6c (CobolDec.cs:112); the native twin is CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs (CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs:157/161, §8.8.1.2 rules 6a/6c). NEITHER cites §8.8.1.4.4 rule 4 and neither is reachable under standard-binary: CobolDec.Pow is reached only via NumericRenderer.Power's `if (StandardDecimal)` arm (NumericRenderer.cs:552), and StandardDecimal excludes ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary (NumericRenderer.cs:559). Upstream, DataBinder.BindDeclarations (DataBinder.cs:318-320) fails the compile with COBOLNET0806 for the mode. So the SBIDI rule has no implementation -- a sibling rule of the same SHAPE is implemented for a different mode, which is precisely the case ground rule 5 says must not be stretched into CONFORMS. subject: ACCEPT statement
notes: 'If a device is capable of transferring data of the same size as the receiving data item, the transferred data is stored in the receiving data item.' Our device transfers exactly RecordSize = 80, so this rule governs a receiver of exactly 80 character positions. Read AcceptSource.Device(int width): `while (sb.Length < width) { line = Console.In.ReadLine(); if (line is null) break; sb.Append(line.Length < RecordSize ? line.PadRight(RecordSize) : line); if (width <= RecordSize) break; }` then `return sb.Length >= width ? sb.ToString(0, width) : sb.ToString().PadRight(width);`. For width == 80 one record is read, padded to 80, and returned whole -- stored, not edited, not truncated; the caller (EmitAcceptDevice) writes it with PlaceRenderer.Write / WriteGroupImage, again a whole-field store. Every receiver shape computes the correct width for this comparison (ref-mod slice length; group DisplayTextWidth; numeric DisplayTextWidth so the sign-separate position counts; otherwise pic.Length). No divergence found. CONFORMS-but-untested: the AcceptDifferentialTests device cases all use widths of 3, 4, 5, 10 or 100, so none exercises the exact-size case; a golden with an X(80) receiver and an 80-character record would close it, and there is no spec-derived test to cite today. || UPHELD: I specifically probed whether the over-long-record defect I found on GR-14.9.1.4-4 reaches this row, and it does not. At width == 80 the guard `if (width <= RecordSize) break;` fires after the first append regardless of that record's length, and `sb.ToString(0, width)` then keeps exactly the leftmost 80 characters -- so a 200-character line still yields the correct 80-character store (the excess falls under GR4b, not GR3) and a short line still pads to 80. The two boundary values that could have broken it, width == 80 with a shorter record and width == 80 with a longer record, both behave. notes: READ: NumericRenderer.CombineCore (349-388), CombineNative (411-420), CombineAdditive (~470-477), EmitCore.UnscaledLit (136-147) and IntLiteralX (160-168); docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.1 item 123 ('The native intermediate data item is a scaled Int128 ... every <=31-digit operand and every aligned sum of them is exact'). DIVERGING HALF -- a FLOATING-POINT LITERAL operand: GR4's premise is 'none of the operands is DESCRIBED WITH USAGE binary-char ... float-extended'. notes: READ: CorrespondingBinder.CorrMatch (91-151) and CorrEligible (160-165) against Sec.14.7.6's six pair-selection rules, which I re-read in full at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:21821-21841. Rule 1 (same data-name and same qualifiers up to but not including D1/D2, FILLER excluded): CorrEligible rejects a nameless (FILLER) entry, and the matcher descends ONLY into name-matched group x group pairs (lines 117-124), so a pair's relative qualification path is identical to D1/D2 by construction. Rule 2 is MOVE-only and is correctly routed to the `verb is CorrVerb.Move` arm (125-130) so it does not apply to ADD. Rule 3 ('In an ADD or SUBTRACT statement, both of the data items are numeric data items') is the `else if (s.Pic?.Category is not PicCategory.Numeric || d.Pic?.Category is not PicCategory.Numeric) continue;` at 134-135 -- a silent non-correspondence, not an error, which is what 'a pair of data items correspond if' requires; pinned by AddCorresponding_Rule3_NonNumericNamesakeIsNotAPair (a PIC 9 / PIC X namesake leaves the target 'A' untouched while the numeric namesake still adds). Rule 4 (OCCURS / REDEFINES / RENAMES, class index): CorrEligible tests IsTable, RedefinesTargetName, Renames and Usage.Index; the class object / pointer / message-tag legs are unmodelled but are unreachable for ADD because rule 3 already requires category numeric on BOTH sides. Rule 5 (nothing subordinate to an ineligible intermediate group) holds because the recursion filters with CorrEligible BEFORE descending, so an OCCURS/REDEFINES group's whole subtree is never visited. Rule 6 is applied SYMMETRICALLY (srcCount at 105-112 as well as cands.Count at 114), which is stricter than the legacy matcher and is what 'the name of each data item ... is unique after application of the implied qualifiers' says. SECOND SENTENCE ('the results are the same as if the user had referred to each pair ... in separate ADD statements'): pairs are emitted in D1 declaration order (the `foreach (var s in src.Children)` walk = Sec.14.7.6's 'the implied statements are executed in the order in which the elements in the group data item immediately following CORRESPONDING are specified'), the one statement rounded-phrase reaches every pair (conformance:2014/corresponding_rounded_mode), the group anchors are hoisted so item identification happens once at statement start (CorrAccess.Hoist), and the statement-level SIZE ERROR aggregation Sec.14.7.6 imposes on top of 'separate statements' is pinned by AddCorresponding_SizeError_AggregatedAcrossPairs (one 'SE' dispatch, the erring receiver unchanged at 5, the later pair still stored at 30, the NOT phrase ignored). A zero-pair group pair is a legal empty implied set (line 78-80). || REFUTED -- CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. THE CLOSING EVIDENCE FOR RULES 4 AND 5 IS A LEGACY-ORACLE TEST. conformance-test:CorrespondingDifferentialTests.AddCorresponding_TableShape_OccursChildExcluded (CorrespondingDifferentialTests.cs:235-236) is `AssertSameAsLegacy(...)`, i.e. `DifferentialGolden.Assert`, whose default mode (`COBOLNET_DIFF_MODE` unset -> 'golden', DifferentialGolden.cs:29-31) asserts only that COBOL.NET still equals a committed .out BAKED FROM A LIVE LEGACY RUN (bake mode, lines 51-62). With it gone, rule 4's OCCURS/REDEFINES leg and rule 5's subtree leg have NO spec-derived test on ADD at all. THREE FURTHER UNVERIFIED EDGES, each read out of the code: (a) Sec.14.7.6's no-phrase aggregation -- 'the level-3 EC-SIZE exception condition for the LAST of the implied statements that raised a size error condition is set to exist after all of the implied statements are completed' -- IS implemented (ArithmeticEmitter.EmitArith:236-247 latches `__sizeEcN` by ASSIGNMENT per failing store, so last-wins, and EcEmitter.EmitSizeHandling runs after the pair loop) but has no test whatsoever; (b) CorrEligible's FILLER leg excludes a nameless entry AND, by `continue`-ing before the descent, its ENTIRE SUBTREE, and the code's own doc-comment (lines 152-158) justifies that with 'the legacy/NIST-proven reading' -- the oracle, not a derivation -- while its stated premise ('a FILLER level contributes no qualifier') is precisely the argument that an item under a FILLER group DOES satisfy rule 1's 'the same data-name and the same qualifiers, if any, up to, but not including, D1 and D2' relative to a same-named item declared directly under D2. That reading is unadjudicated against the spec here and is a live silent-non-correspondence risk; (c) CorrespondingEmitter.Emit runs EVERY pair inside ONE `try` (ArithmeticEmitter.EmitArith:245), so a CobolSizeError raised during a pair's EVALUATION (CobolNum.Widen off an unsigned-wide operand) would ABORT the remaining implied statements, which Sec.14.7.6 forbids ('after all of the implied statements are completed') -- reachability unmeasured, the per-pair composite cap makes it unlikely, but the shape is there. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an AssertOutput (not AssertSameAsLegacy) golden for the OCCURS/REDEFINES exclusion on ADD CORR; a no-SIZE-ERROR-phrase >>TURN EC-SIZE golden proving the LAST erring pair's condition is the one set; and a spec derivation for the FILLER-group subtree with a golden either way.

notes: This rule is a pointer at five clauses, so it was adjudicated as 'is each referenced mechanism actually wired to ADD'. FOUR OF FIVE ARE. Sec.14.7.7 Arithmetic statements: rule 2 is StatementValidation.CheckComposite, rule 4 + NOTE 3 are the Snapshot/one-initial-evaluation discipline in ArithmeticEmitter. THE FIFTH LEG IS SHORT -- Sec.14.6.13.2 Incompatible data: I re-read it at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:21630-21664; rule 2 makes EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE exist whenever the content of a NUMERIC sending item that is not standard-floating-point 'is referenced during the execution of a statement' and would fail a numeric class condition -- an ADD's identifier-1, its Format-2 identifier-2, and (per NOTE 2) its Format-1 identifier-2 read-side all qualify. notes: Rule (--check OK, §14.9.3.3 1): data-name-1 shall be described with the BASED clause. Read `PtrBinder.PtrResolveBased`: it looks the name up and returns it only on `if (item is { IsBased: true }) return item;`, otherwise raising COBOLNET0869 '...shall be a BASED level-01/77 item (ISO §14.9.39 SR18 / §14.9.3 SR1 — rebasing or allocating a non-BASED item is not ISO COBOL)'. `PtrBinder.BindAllocate`'s form-2 arm calls it for drefs[0] and returns BoundNop on failure, so a non-BASED data-name-1 never reaches the emitter. Evidence: conformance:negative/allocate-non-based is exactly this rule's fixture (`01 W PIC X(5).` + `ALLOCATE W RETURNING P.`, reject-at 2002 2014 2023, .err expecting 'the operand shall be a BASED level-01/77 item') and is registered in tests/conformance/negative/manifest.json. OBSERVATION, not a downgrade: PtrResolveBased deliberately bypasses the SymbolTable (`dref.ChildCount == 1 && ctx.Data.ByName.TryGetValue(...) ? list[0] : null`, a bypass the class doc flags as a behavior-sensitive follow-up). It rejects a qualified/subscripted operand, which costs nothing here because BASED is a level-01/77 clause and such a name has no higher group to qualify it; and `ByName` is per-program-unit (BinderDriver.cs:383 constructs a DataBinder inside the per-unit loop), so the list[0] pick cannot cross program units. The SR1 predicate itself is exactly the rule. || UPHELD, and the 'no higher group to qualify it' premise is now MEASURED rather than assumed: specs/ISO_COBOL.md:15101 (§13.18.x SR16) reads 'The BASED clause may be specified only in data description entries in the linkage section, in the working-storage section, and in the local-storage section. The level number of such data description entries shall be 1 or 77' — so a based entry is never in an FD and has no containing group, and the only legal reference to it is the bare name that `dref.ChildCount == 1` admits. I read PtrBinder.cs:194-203 and confirmed the predicate is `item is { IsBased: true }` with the 0869 error on every other path, and I read the fixture + its .err and confirmed the manifest registration by loading tests/conformance/negative/manifest.json. Residual, recorded not scored: with two same-named level-01 entries (a reference the standard already requires to be unique or qualified, §8.4.2.2) `list[0]` silently picks the first rather than diagnosing ambiguity — an UNDER-rejection of source that is already nonconforming, so it does not affect this row's verdict.

subject: ALLOCATE statement
notes: Rule (--check OK, §14.9.3.3 4): if data-name-2 references a RESTRICTED data-pointer, data-name-1 shall be specified, shall reference a typed data item, and data-name-2 shall be restricted to data-name-1's type. A restricted data-pointer is created by `USAGE POINTER TO type-name-1` — §13.18.60.4 GR23 (--check OK): 'If type-name-1 is specified, this data item is a restricted data-pointer' — or by ADDRESS OF a strongly-typed group (§8.4.3.11 / Annex D at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:38732-38736). NOT DECLARABLE in this compiler: grammar rule `usageKeyword` carries a bare `| POINTER` alternative with no `(TO cobolWord)?` tail, unlike its two neighbours `programPointerUsage : PROGRAM_POINTER (TO cobolWord)?` and `functionPointerUsage : FUNCTION_POINTER (TO cobolWord)?` which DO parse their restricted forms. So `05 P USAGE POINTER TO T.` is a syntax error and no restricted data-pointer can exist; correspondingly there is no restriction check anywhere in the ALLOCATE path (PtrBinder.PtrResolvePointer tests category only, and grep shows no StrongTypeModel call from PtrBinder). Per owner decision D13 an absent feature is NOT-IMPLEMENTED, not documented non-support: the compiler rejects legal COBOL (a conforming program declaring a restricted data-pointer) rather than adjudicating this rule. What would close the row: the `POINTER [TO type-name-1]` grammar tail, a restricted-type field on the pointer's PicInfo, the SR4 check in BindAllocate, plus a positive golden and a negative fixture (restricted data-name-2 with the CHARACTERS form, which SR4 forbids outright). || UPHELD, with the load-bearing DIAGRAM checked rather than inferred: the §13.18.60.2 USAGE general format at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:19873 prints `│ <u>POINTER</u> [ TO type-name-1 ]` — the TO tail is in the standard's own format, and the OCR bias runs toward falsely-RESTRICTIVE, so the tail is certainly real. I read CobolData.g4:412-444 myself: `usageKeyword` really does list a bare `| POINTER` (line 440) while `programPointerUsage` (line 441) and `functionPointerUsage` (line 442) are separate rules that DO carry `(TO cobolWord)?`, so the omission is a one-alternative gap in an otherwise-parallel trio, not a design posture. I re-ran --check on §13.18.60.4 GR23 and it returned OK on the quoted restricted-data-pointer sentence. This is REJECTS-LEGAL-SOURCE, not merely an unchecked rule: `05 P USAGE POINTER TO T.` is a parse error today.

subject: ALLOCATE statement
notes: Rule (--check OK, §14.9.3.3 5): with both data-name-1 and data-name-2 present and data-name-1 a strongly-typed group item, data-name-2 shall be restricted to data-name-1's type. Read `PtrBinder.BindAllocate`'s form-2 arm end to end: it calls PtrResolveBased (IsBased only) and PtrResolvePointer (PicCategory.Pointer only) and builds BoundAllocate — no type/restriction test at all. A grep of every `StrongTypeModel.` call site in src/Cobol.Net.Compiler lists DataBinder, IntrinsicArgumentRules, ConditionBinder, StringUnstringBinder, ReferenceResolver and StatementValidation — PtrBinder is NOT among them, so strong typing is modelled (StrongTypeModel.IsStrongGroup / SameStrongType back the §14.9.25.3 SR2 MOVE and §8.8.4.2.3 comparison gates) but never consulted here. Consequence, given SR4's finding that a restricted data-pointer cannot be declared at all: EVERY `ALLOCATE strongly-typed-based-group RETURNING P` is source the standard forbids (P can only be unrestricted) and this compiler silently accepts it, defeating the type-safety guarantee Annex D states at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:38741 ('the address of a strongly-typed group item … can only be assigned to a data-pointer restricted to the same type'). notes: Rule re-read in context at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 14.9.4.4 1) under the 'FORMATS 1 AND 2' heading; citation validated (`cite.py --check 14.9.4.4 "The instance of the program, function, or method that executes the CALL statement is the activating runtime element."` -> OK, General rules 1). It is not maintained across nested activations. Read ProgramTable.CallProgram lines 180-233: for an INITIAL or RECURSIVE unit it does `inst = n.Factory(ParentInstance(n)); n.Instance = inst;` and the `finally` restores ONLY `n.Active--`, the module frame and the EC masks - `n.Instance` is NEVER restored to the outer activation's instance. ProgramTable.ParentInstance reads exactly that field (`_byPath[n.ParentPath].Instance`), and ProgramEmitter.EmitProgramClass emits a contained program's container handle as `private readonly {parent.ClassName} __outer;` assigned once in the constructor, with every inherited GLOBAL item reaching container storage through it (`private ref {type} {b.Field} => ref {b.Path};   // GLOBAL item of a containing program (ISO 13.18.27 GR2)`, BinderDriver.BindUnitData building `__outer.` prefixes). So for a RECURSIVE container R containing C: R#1 calls C -> C is a cached singleton (`inst = n.Instance ??= n.Factory(ParentInstance(n))`) with __outer = inst1; R#1 calls itself -> inst2, `R.Instance = inst2`; inst2 calls C -> the SAME cached C, still bound to inst1, so the callee reads and writes the OUTER activation's storage. The reverse is broken too: after inst2 returns, `R.Instance` still names inst2, so a per-activation callee constructed from inst1's CALL gets a TERMINATED instance as its activating element. Reachable on conforming source: the WORKING-STORAGE composition is loud-staged (DiagnosticCatalog.RecursiveContainedWs, negative fixture tests/conformance/negative/recursive-contained-ws.cob) but LOCAL-STORAGE is not, and 13.18.27.3 SR1b (`cite.py --check 13.18.27.3` -> OK) permits IS GLOBAL on 'A data description entry whose level-number is 1 that is specified in the file, working-storage, local-storage, or linkage section' - so `PROGRAM-ID. R RECURSIVE.` + `LOCAL-STORAGE SECTION. 01 LS-G PIC 9(4) GLOBAL.` + a contained C that references LS-G compiles and answers with the wrong activation's automatic data. SECOND, INDEPENDENT HALF: the recursive attribute is not per-containment either - BinderDriver.MakeUnit sets `recursive` ONLY from this unit's own PROGRAM-ID clause plus `if (isFunction) recursive = true`, while 11.10.4 GR4 (`cite.py --check 11.10.4 "The RECURSIVE clause specifies that the program and any programs contained within it are recursive."` -> OK) makes every program contained in a RECURSIVE program recursive, so those containees take the cached-singleton instance model (last-used state) instead of the per-activation instance this rule's 'instance ... is the activating runtime element' requires. What would close the row: an activation STACK of instances per node (push/pop around `inst.Call`) so ParentInstance answers 'the instance that is executing the CALL', __outer rebound per activation for a contained callee, the 11.10.4 GR4 attribute inheritance, plus a golden with a RECURSIVE container, a LOCAL-STORAGE GLOBAL item and a contained callee printing it at two depths. Editions: no Annex E delta touches this rule (E.2's only CALL entry is item 1 bullet 3, the ON OVERFLOW removal), so the batch default applies.

notes: This rule-id carries TWO spec rules: 14.9.4.4 3h) item 3 ('If checking for the exception condition is not enabled, subsequent behavior is as specified in 14.6.13.1, Exception conditions') and the whole of 3i). || UPHELD, including the swallow finding, which I re-derived from the emitted control flow rather than trusting the note. (3i, propagation) EmitPropagationPickup emits the activator-side pickup of a callee-staged GOBACK/EXIT PROGRAM ... RAISING condition, running the 14.9.49 F3 selection over the dynamic name and honoring RESUME (14.6.13.1.3 #6). (3h#3) with no phrase and no enabled name, `!hasPhrase && ecProg.Count == 0` emits the BARE invocation, so the CobolCallException propagates to ProgramTable.RunMain's `catch (CobolCallException cx) { AbnormalTermination(cx.Message) }` - the documented 14.6.13.1.3 #8 implementor choice. UNVERIFIED / DIVERGENT HALVES: (a) a CALL written with ONLY a NOT ON EXCEPTION phrase and no enabled checking SILENTLY SWALLOWS a failure - `hasPhrase = c.OnException is not null || c.NotOnException is not null` is TRUE, so the unfiltered `catch (CobolCallException) { __callErr = true; }` is emitted, `c.OnException` is null so only the `if (!__callErr) { not }` block is written, the NOT-ON body is skipped, and execution falls to the end of the CALL with no diagnostic and no status - while the identical CALL without the NOT ON phrase terminates the run unit loudly. GR3h has no ON EXCEPTION phrase in that source, so item 2 or item 3 governs, and this implementation's item-3 disposition everywhere else is loud termination - so the phrase changes the outcome of a rule it is not a party to. (b) 3i's 'the ON EXCEPTION phrase, if specified, is ignored' is violated for a condition raised INSIDE a successfully-called program that surfaces as a CobolCallException - CobolArgAdapt.Omitted's EC-PROGRAM-ARG-OMITTED unwinds past ProgramTable.CallProgram's try/finally into the caller's phrase catch and runs imperative-statement-1. notes: The rule requires the compiler to validate that program-prototype-name-1 names a program prototype declared in the REPOSITORY paragraph. READ: BindCancel has exactly two arms, literal and dataReference (lines 244-262); there is no third arm and no lookup against any prototype registry. A program-prototype-name written in a CANCEL therefore arrives as a `dataReference`, fails `ctx.Refs.Resolve`, and produces `BoundUnsupported($"CANCEL target '{dref.GetText()}'")` - emitted as a RUN-time `NotImplemented.Run` that says nothing about prototypes. Upstream, the subject of the rule cannot even be declared: CallBinder.BindCall's DiagnosticCatalog.CallAsPrototypeName message states it verbatim - 'The REPOSITORY grammar has no `PROGRAM program-prototype-name` entry (ISO 12.3.8.2's program-specifier), so no source can declare one - this arm is genuinely blocked on the P13 prototype registry.' So there is no subject to validate and no diagnostic to fire. Per ground rule 6 the absence of support is NOT-IMPLEMENTED, not documented non-support and not an owner decision. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the 12.3.8.2 PROGRAM specifier in the REPOSITORY grammar plus a prototype registry, a BindCancel arm resolving program-prototype-name-1 against it, a targeted COBOLNET diagnostic when the name is not a REPOSITORY program prototype, and a conformance:negative fixture for the violating source. || UPHELD: BindCancel's two arms confirmed at CallBinder.cs:244-262, and there is no prototype lookup on the CANCEL path.
