subject: COMPUTE statement
notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB128): the arithmetic-resultant category screen lives at the ONE receiving chokepoint's Receivers overloads (COBOLNET1675), keyed per caller: COMPUTE identifier-1 admits elementary numeric or numeric-edited (SR1); the F1->F2 reroute's boolean receivers ride ResolveReceiving too (the arithmetic screen deliberately not applied there - SR2 is PB157's). Also rejected: index data items (13.18.60.3 SR10's closed list) and ref-mod slices (8.4.3.3.4 GR6c).

subject: COMPUTE statement
notes: DERIVED FIRST: identifier-2 must be ELEMENTARY and of category BOOLEAN — so a group item (including a GROUP-USAGE BIT group) and any non-boolean elementary item are both violations. READ: ArithmeticBinder.BuildComputeBoolean, the shared tail of the direct Format-2 bind AND the F1->F2 re-route, so BOTH arms of that dispatch are screened by one body. Its per-receiver loop resolves the reference, then `var cat = p is RefModPlace rm ? rm.Inner.Item.Pic?.Category : p.Item.Pic?.Category; if (cat is not PicCategory.Boolean) Error(COBOLNET1511, "… shall be an elementary boolean item (ISO 14.9.8 Format 2 SR2)")`. MATCHED: a GROUP item has no PicInfo, so `Pic?.Category` is null and the check rejects it. The RefModPlace arm ACCEPTS a reference-modified boolean item, and that is correct, not a leak: 8.4.3.3.4 GR6 (--check verified) — 'The unique data item is considered to be an elementary data item without the JUSTIFIED clause. The unique data item has the same class, category, and usage as that defined for identifier-1, except that:' — and category boolean is not among the excepted categories. VERIFIED BOTH WAYS: rejection — conformance-test:BooleanOperatorTests.BooleanComputeReceiver_NotBoolean_Rejected1511 compiles `COMPUTE N = A B-AND B` with `01 N PIC X(4)` at --std 2002 and asserts the compile fails with COBOLNET1511; acceptance — conformance:2002/boolean_ops runs six Format-2 statements into `01 R PIC 1(4)` against the Annex A Table A.2 oracle. EDITIONS 2002+: identifier-2 requires the boolean data class, absent from the 1985 standard. SECONDARY OBSERVATION: BuildComputeBoolean calls `ctx.Refs.Resolve(store.dataReference())` DIRECTLY rather than going through ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceiving, so a Format-2 boolean receiver BYPASSES 'THE ONE RECEIVING CHOKEPOINT' and with it the CONSTANT RECORD screen (13.18.15.3 SR2 / DataBinder.RejectConstantStore), the CAPACITY-register screen (13.18.38 SR30-32) and the report-counter screen. It does NOT reintroduce the PB70 silent-drop — an unresolvable receiver gets its own COBOLNET1511 — but `COMPUTE <boolean field of a CONSTANT RECORD> = A B-AND B` would not be rejected by 13.18.15.3 SR2 the way every Format-1 receiver is. || REFUTED: CONFORMS -> DIVERGES. THE DERIVATION IS WRONG AT ITS FIRST SENTENCE, AND THE CODE INHERITS THE ERROR. The adjudicator's premise — 'a group item (INCLUDING A GROUP-USAGE BIT GROUP) … is a violation' — is contradicted by the standard twice: §8.5.2.5 item 3 (--check verified, 'Boolean category'): 'A group item explicitly or implicitly described with a GROUP-USAGE clause with the BIT phrase.' is a data item of category boolean; and §13.18.29.1 (--check verified): 'A GROUP-USAGE clause with a BIT phrase specifies that the group item defined by the subject of the entry is to be treated as an ELEMENTARY item of usage bit and category boolean, unless specified otherwise.' A bit group therefore satisfies BOTH halves of SR2's 'elementary boolean data item' — it is legal identifier-2, not a violation. WHAT THE CODE DOES: ArithmeticBinder.cs:240-243 reads `p.Item.Pic?.Category`, and DataBinder.cs:2558 stores `GroupUsage = pic is null ? groupUsage : GroupUsage.None` — a bit group has NO PicInfo, so `cat` is null and the receiver is REJECTED with COBOLNET1511 'shall be an elementary boolean item'. LEGAL SOURCE REJECTED, with a diagnostic that asserts the opposite of §13.18.29.1. REPRO: `01 BG GROUP-USAGE BIT. 05 B1 PIC 1(4) VALUE B"1100". 01 A PIC 1(4) USAGE BIT. 01 B PIC 1(4) USAGE BIT. … COMPUTE BG = A B-AND B.` -> COBOLNET1511 at --std 2002+. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE PROOF THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A READING: the SENDING side of the very same statement accepts a bit group — ConditionBinder.cs:104-107, the leaf whose own comment reads 'THE ONE category reader (D20/PB79): … or a bit group's as-if PICTURE 1(m) — a bit group IS a boolean operand (§13.18.29.4 GR1a)', which uses `p.Item.OperandPic?.Category` (= `Pic ?? AsIfPic`, DataItem.cs:83) — and BooleanRenderer.cs:26 already renders a bit-group BoundBoolRef through its AsBits() face. So `COMPUTE R = BG B-AND A` binds BG happily as an operand while `COMPUTE BG = A B-AND A` rejects BG as a receiver. SECOND, INDEPENDENT LEG OF THE SAME ROW: even if the SR2 screen were fixed, the Format-2 STORE would be wrong — ArithmeticEmitter.cs:160 computes the receiver width as `t is RefModPlace ? -1 : t.Item.Pic?.Length ?? 0`, again raw `Pic`, so a bit-group receiver would take width 0 and `RuntimeApi.StrStoreBoolean(value, 0, …)` would store an empty boolean value. Both legs are the same root as GR-14.9.8.4-3's: kb/Work PB79 declared `DataItem.OperandPic` 'THE ONE READER for category' and converted the sites it enumerated, but the COMPUTE Format-2 receiver screen and receiver width were not among them, and PB79's golden tests/conformance/2023/pb79_group_usage_bit.cob contains NO COMPUTE statement at all — I read it end to end — so nothing has ever exercised a bit group in either COMPUTE position. WHY THE EXISTING TEST DID NOT CATCH IT (the adjudicator's 'the ELEMENTARY half is enforced by the same test as the CATEGORY half' is exactly the collapse): BooleanComputeReceiver_NotBoolean_Rejected1511 uses `01 N PIC X(4)` — an ELEMENTARY alphanumeric item — so it exercises only the category half and says nothing about groups; no test anywhere passes a group of ANY kind as identifier-2. TEST-REF REMOVED: the row is not closed. TO CLOSE: read the receiver category through `p.Item.OperandPic?.Category` (and the store width through AsIfPic.Length), a golden with a GROUP-USAGE BIT identifier-2 asserting the stored bit string, and a conformance:negative fixture keeping the ALPHANUMERIC-GROUP receiver rejected so the widening does not swallow §8.5.2.5's actual boundary. The adjudicator's SECONDARY OBSERVATION about the bypassed ResolveReceiving chokepoint is UPHELD and becomes part of the fix: routing Format-2 receivers through the chokepoint would fix the CONSTANT RECORD / CAPACITY leaks in the same change.

subject: COMPUTE statement
notes: DERIVED FIRST, AND THE DERIVATION IS THE POINT. SR3 bars one thing: boolean-expression-1 consisting SOLELY of 'the figurative constant ALL literal'. 8.8.2 enumerates the permissible boolean expressions as EIGHT alternatives, of which two are distinct and separately listed (both --check verified against 8.8.2): '— the figurative constant ZERO (ZEROS, ZEROES),' AND '— the figurative constant ALL literal, where literal is a boolean literal,'. The two are not the same alternative, and 8.3.3.6.3 SR2 (Format 6, i.e. `ALL literal-1`) settles it from the other side: 'Literal-1 shall be an alphanumeric, boolean, or national literal … The literal shall be neither a figurative constant nor a zero-length literal.' A figurative ZERO therefore can never BE 'the figurative constant ALL literal' — it is 8.3.3.6.2 Format 1 — so SR3 does not reach it. EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR: `COMPUTE <elementary boolean item> = ZERO` is LEGAL and must compile; `COMPUTE <elementary boolean item> = ALL B"1"` must be rejected. READ: ArithmeticBinder.BindComputeBoolean. Its SR3 body is `var rhs = host.Cond.BindBoolExpr(boolExpr); if (rhs is BoundBoolAll) Error(COBOLNET1511, "a boolean COMPUTE expression shall not consist solely of an ALL literal (ISO 14.9.8 Format 2 SR3)")`. The preceding SoleFigurativeZero guard — which exists precisely because BindBoolExpr NORMALISES a bare figurative ZERO into `BoundBoolAll("0")`, the very node `ALL B"0"` produces — is gated on `computeStore(0)` NOT being boolean. DIVERGENCE: with a BOOLEAN receiver the guard is skipped by design, the normalised ZERO reaches the `rhs is BoundBoolAll` test, and `01 B PIC 1(4). … COMPUTE B = ZERO.` is REJECTED with a diagnostic naming a construct the source does not contain — legal source rejected, and the message is wrong on its own terms in exactly the way the same message was wrong before PB51. This is the SECOND ARM of the very dispatch PB51 fixed: PB51 corrected the non-boolean-receiver arm and its own note leaves this one open verbatim ('COMPUTE <boolean-item> = ZERO still reports COBOLNET1511 … whether 14.9.8 Format 2 SR3's "an ALL literal" should bar a bare ZERO at all is a separate reading question. Left as measured, not silently widened.'). WHAT IS NEW HERE AND NOT IN PB51: the reading is now DECIDED against the spec rather than left open — 8.8.2's enumeration plus 8.3.3.6.3 SR2 make ZERO and `ALL literal` disjoint alternatives, so SR3 cannot bar the figurative ZERO and the current rejection is a defect, not a latitude. SECOND, INDEPENDENT HALF ALSO OPEN: SR3's ACTUAL prohibition has no test at all. No fixture or unit test anywhere compiles `COMPUTE R = ALL B"1"` alone and asserts COBOLNET1511; BooleanOperatorTests' only ALL case is `COMPUTE R = A B-AND ALL B"1"` in ComputeFormat2_MatchesOracle, which is an ACCEPTANCE case (SR3 says 'consist SOLELY of', and 8.8.2 rule 4 bars only BOTH operands being ALL literals). So the rule as written is enforced but unverified, while a construct it does not cover is rejected. TO CLOSE: make the SR3 test read the PARSE TREE the way SoleFigurativeZero already does — reject only a source-level Format-6 `ALL <boolean-literal>` — regardless of receiver category; then a golden asserting `COMPUTE B = ZERO` stores boolean zeros to B's width, and a conformance:negative fixture asserting `COMPUTE B = ALL B"1"` is COBOLNET1511. || UPHELD: DIVERGES, on an independent derivation and independent citation checks. I re-ran both supporting citations myself: `cite.py --check 8.8.2 "the figurative constant ALL literal, where literal is a boolean literal"` -> OK, and `cite.py --check 8.3.3.6.3 "The literal shall be neither a figurative constant nor a zero-length literal."` -> OK (§8.3.3.6.3 rule 2). §8.8.2's list, which I read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 8143-8152, does carry ZERO and `ALL literal` as two separate bullets, so SR3's 'the figurative constant ALL literal' cannot denote a bare ZERO. I traced the code path myself: ArithmeticBinder.cs:202-204 skips the SoleFigurativeZero re-route when `Probe(computeStore(0))` IS boolean, so the normalised `BoundBoolAll("0")` reaches the `rhs is BoundBoolAll` test at :216 and errors. And I confirmed the second half by measurement, not assertion — a grep for `ALL B"` across tests/ returns exactly three COMPUTE-adjacent hits (BooleanOperatorTests.cs:41 and boolean_ops.cob:33, both `A B-AND ALL B"1"` acceptance cases, plus a comment line in pb51_compute_figurative_zero.cob), so SR3's actual prohibition has no negative fixture. ONE FINDING TO ADD, same rule, not a verdict change: SR3's test lives ONLY in BindComputeBoolean and NOT in the shared tail BuildComputeBoolean, so the F1->F2 re-route arm (ArithmeticBinder.cs:153-160) never applies SR3 at all. No source shape reaches that arm with a sole ALL literal today (the re-route needs a boolean receiver or a sole boolean data reference), so it is latent rather than live — but it is the same two-arm shape as the defect above, and the fix should put the parse-tree SR3 test in the shared tail so both arms carry it. No overturn.

subject: COMPUTE statement
notes: DERIVED FIRST: arm (a) — under native or standard-decimal arithmetic, an arithmetic-expression-1 that is a SINGLE fixed-point numeric literal or a SINGLE fixed-point numeric data item must yield the EXACT algebraic value of that literal/item, and 'rounding, truncation, and decimal point alignment specifications do not apply to the production of that exact algebraic value' (so any per-receiver alignment must happen at the STORE, rule 2, not while producing the value); arm (b) — otherwise, evaluate per 8.8.1. READ: ArithmeticEmitter.EmitCompute (both its multi-receiver and single-receiver paths) and the renderer leaves it calls, NumericRenderer.Visit(BoundNumRef) => FieldNum(n.Place) and NumericRenderer.Visit(BoundNumLiteral) => LiteralNum(n.Text). VERIFIED HALF (arm (a) under NATIVE): neither leaf consults the ReceiverContext scale — a sole data-item RHS renders at the ITEM's own PICTURE scale and a sole literal at the literal's own scale; ReceiverContext.Scale only sets the WORKING scale for division/multiplication intermediates. conformance:2014/rounded_modes is a direct spec-derived probe of exactly this: `01 SRC PIC 9V99 VALUE 2.25` (scale 2) is the sole RHS of nine `COMPUTE X ROUNDED MODE IS …` statements into `01 X PIC 9.9` (scale 1), and NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO is expected to give 2.3 — reachable ONLY if the exact 2.25 survives to the rounder; had the value been aligned to the receiver's scale during production the golden would read 2.2 for every mode. UNVERIFIED HALVES, each specific: (i) arm (a) under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL — conformance:2014/arithmetic_standard_decimal exercises only a MULTI-operand expression (`COMPUTE W = 2 / 7 * 7`), i.e. arm (b); no golden puts a SOLE fixed-point item or literal on the RHS under a standard mode, and the standard-decimal literal path is a different leaf (LiteralNum's `StandardDecimal && IsFloatingPointForm` branch -> RuntimeApi.DecFromParsedLiteral). (ii) arm (a) with a sole fixed-point LITERAL under any mode — every rounded_modes case uses a data item. NOT IMPLEMENTED, and it is part of arm (a)'s own text: 'within the constraints specified in 14.6.13.2, Incompatible data'. 14.6.13.2 rule 2 never fires from a COMPUTE: EcBinder gates the condition with `node is BoundMove`, so only 14.6.13.2 rule 4's de-editing MOVE is wired — the traceability inventory agrees, GR-14.6.13.2-2 is an unadjudicated GAP row while GR-14.6.13.2-4 is the only CONFORMS in that family. UNREACHABLE BY DECISION: the NOTE's standard-binary reading cannot be exercised — DataBinder rejects ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY outright with COBOLNET0806 as an obsolete feature. TO CLOSE: a golden with `OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.` and a sole wide fixed-point item plus a sole fixed-point literal as arithmetic-expression-1, each stored ROUNDED into a narrower receiver; plus the 14.6.13.2 rule 2 wiring, which belongs to that clause's own rows. || UPHELD: PARTIAL, re-derived independently and confirmed at the source rather than from the notes. (1) The arm-(a) evidence is REAL and stronger than stated: NumericRenderer.cs:116 `public NumX Visit(BoundNumLiteral n) => LiteralNum(n.Text);` and NumericRenderer.cs:143 `public NumX Visit(BoundNumRef n) => FieldNum(n.Place);` take NO ReceiverContext argument AT ALL, so there is no channel by which a receiver's scale could reach the production of a sole literal's or a sole item's value — that is exactly 'Rounding, truncation, and decimal point alignment specifications do not apply to the production of that exact algebraic value' (§14.9.8.4 1a, --check verified). (2) The NOT-IMPLEMENTED half is confirmed at the exact line: EcBinder.cs:517 `if (node is BoundMove && ctx.EcState.Turn.Enabled("EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE", null, line))` — the entire EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE enable arm is gated on the node being a MOVE, so arm (a)'s own 'within the constraints specified in 14.6.13.2' cannot fire from any COMPUTE. (3) Both cited goldens exist on disk. I attempted and failed to break arm (b): the multi-receiver path's `ReceiverContext(Targets.Max(ScaleOf), …)` widest-scale render plus Snapshot is a §8.8.1 evaluation choice, not an alignment applied to a sole operand, so it does not contaminate arm (a). No overturn; the two named unverified halves and the TO CLOSE stand as written.

subject: COMPUTE statement
notes: DERIVED FIRST: ONE value (rule 1's) is stored into EACH identifier-1, and each store is governed by 14.6.8 (alignment/transfer), 14.7.4 (that receiver's own ROUNDED phrase) and 14.7.5 (SIZE ERROR). READ: ArithmeticEmitter.EmitCompute (the multi-receiver path renders the RHS once at the widest receiver scale, materializes it via Snapshot, then loops `foreach (var r in c.Targets) StoreArith(r.Place, v, r.Rounding)`), ArithmeticEmitter.StoreArith (its four receiver arms — float-edited, LOCALE format-2 edited, fixed numeric-edited via EditFormat/EditTryFormat, plain fixed numeric via StoreArgs — each rescaling to the RECEIVER's scale with the RECEIVER's mode), and ArithmeticEmitter.EmitArith (the 14.7.5 two-phase wrapper: a __sizeErr flag set either by a per-receiver TryStore failure or by a CobolSizeError/OverflowException during evaluation, then the ON / NOT ON imperative). VERIFIED: 'into EACH data item referenced by identifier-1' with the value taken once — conformance:2023/pb51_compute_figurative_zero writes `COMPUTE N I = ZERO` over two differently-shaped receivers; the 14.7.4 delegation with a PER-RESULTANT ROUNDED phrase — conformance:2014/ca5b_prohibited_multi_receiver_size_error writes `COMPUTE X ROUNDED MODE IS PROHIBITED Y ROUNDED MODE IS PROHIBITED = 10 / 3` and asserts the receivers are left UNCHANGED, and conformance:2014/rounded_modes walks all eight modes plus bare ROUNDED through COMPUTE; the 14.6.8 delegation into a numeric-EDITED receiver — conformance:2002/float_edited stores `COMPUTE WS-E = WS-F + 1` into `01 WS-E PIC ZZ9.99` through StoreArith's NumericEdited/EditMask arm; the 14.7.5 delegation in both directions — conformance:85/phrase_order_arithmetic and conformance:85/optional_on_size_error take the ON branch on `999 * 99` into PIC 9(3) and the NOT branch on `1 + 1`. UNVERIFIED HALF, named precisely: the 14.7.5 storing-rule-2 PARTIAL COMMIT across a MULTI-receiver COMPUTE. EmitArith's own comment asserts it and the loop shape supports it, but ca5b — the only multi-receiver size-error golden — has BOTH receivers failing, so the mixed direction has never been observed: nothing anywhere pins that a COMPUTE with one receiver that overflows and one that does not leaves the overflowing receiver unchanged WHILE the other takes the value, and then runs the ON SIZE ERROR imperative once. TO CLOSE: a golden shaped `01 BIG PIC 9(6). 01 SML PIC 9(2). COMPUTE BIG SML = 123456 ON SIZE ERROR DISPLAY "SE" NOT ON SIZE ERROR DISPLAY "OK" END-COMPUTE.` asserting BIG=123456, SML unchanged at its prior value, and exactly one "SE". || UPHELD: PARTIAL. I re-derived the obligation from the spec text before reading the notes and the unverified half is REAL, not a bookkeeping scruple. §14.7.5's storing rule 2 (--check verified against §14.7.5): 'If the absolute value of the result of the arithmetic operation exceeds the maximum value allowed for any resultant identifier, the content of that resultant identifier is not changed from the content that existed at the start of the execution of the arithmetic statement. The values of resultant identifiers for which the size error condition did not occur are the same as they would have been if the size error condition had not existed for any of the resultant identifiers.' — so the mixed case is a NORMATIVE requirement with a specific observable, not an implementor choice. READ MYSELF: ArithmeticEmitter.cs:225-275 EmitArith emits `bool __sizeErrN = false;` then `try { … } catch (CobolSizeError) { flag = true; } catch (OverflowException) { flag = true; }`, and StoreArith's fixed-numeric arm emits, PER RECEIVER, `if (!NumTryStore(args, mode, tmp, …)) flag = true; else <Write(target, …)>` — a failing receiver sets the flag and falls through WITHOUT a break, so later receivers do store; rule 2 is implemented and genuinely unobserved. I also tried to find a SECOND defect on this row and did not: the multi-receiver `ReceiverContext(Targets.Max(ScaleOf), …)` + `Snapshot` gives one value stored into each, which is what 'The value obtained according to rule 1 is then stored … into each data item referenced by identifier-1' requires. No overturn. NOTE ON SCOPE: this row measures the FIXED-POINT/EDITED store funnel; the boolean store (Format 2's 'stored in each data item referenced by identifier-2') belongs to GR-14.9.8.4-3, where it is now DIVERGES.

subject: COMPUTE statement
notes: DERIVED FIRST: three obligations — (a) boolean-expression-1 evaluates per 8.8.2 and subject to 14.6.13.2; (b) the RESULT WIDTH is 'the number of boolean positions in the largest boolean ITEM referenced in the expression' (ITEM, so literals and ALL literals contribute nothing); (c) the resulting value is stored in EACH identifier-2. READ: ArithmeticEmitter.EmitComputeBoolean and ConditionBinder.Gr3Width. Gr3Width returns the item length for a BoundBoolRef (the ref-mod length for a RefModPlace), max over a BoundBoolBinary's arms, the operand's width through BoundBoolNot and BoundBoolShift, and its DEFAULT arm is `_ => 0` with the comment 'literals / ALL / error contribute no ITEM width' — the ITEM-only reading. EmitComputeBoolean then applies `RuntimeApi.BoolResize(value, Gr3Width)` only when the width is > 0, renders the RHS ONCE and materializes it into a temp when there is more than one target, and stores per receiver through `RuntimeApi.StrStoreBoolean(value, width, t.Item.Justified)` — which is 14.6.8.6 verbatim. VERIFIED: the 8.8.2 evaluation against the Annex A Table A.2 oracle — conformance:2002/boolean_ops (B-AND/B-OR/B-XOR/B-NOT, nesting, a figurative ALL B"1" operand), conformance:2023/boolean_shift (rule 9's 'result length = the FIRST operand'), conformance:2023/boolean_shift_mixed (rule 7b precedence); the resize primitive in isolation — unit:CobolBoolTests.Resize_LeftAlignRightFillOrTruncate, whose own header cites 14.9.8 GR3 / 14.6.8.6 and covers right zero-fill, right truncation, exact and zero width. UNVERIFIED HALVES, named: (i) the MIXED-WIDTH composition end to end. EVERY Format-2 golden declares uniform `PIC 1(4)` operands AND a `PIC 1(4)` receiver, so 'the LARGEST boolean item wins' and the receiver-width pad/truncate are both no-ops in every case that has ever run — a Gr3Width that returned the FIRST operand's width, or an EmitComputeBoolean that skipped the resize entirely, would pass the whole corpus. (ii) the ref-mod width leg is self-declared residue: ConditionBinder.RefModLen only reads a LITERAL ref-mod length and otherwise falls back to the inner item's FULL length, which is not the unique data item's boolean-position count. NOT IMPLEMENTED, and it is part of the rule's own text: 'subject to the specifications in … 14.6.13.2, Incompatible data' — 14.6.13.2 rule 1 is unwired; EcBinder admits the condition only for `node is BoundMove`, and the inventory's GR-14.6.13.2-1 is still an open GAP row. EDITIONS: 2002+ — identifier-2 and boolean-expression-1 both require the boolean data class; the shift operators reachable here are 2023 per Annex E.2 item 3. TO CLOSE (i): a golden with `01 A PIC 1(3). 01 B PIC 1(6). 01 R PIC 1(8).` and `COMPUTE R = A B-OR B.` asserting the 6-position GR3 value left-aligned and zero-filled to 8, plus a narrower receiver proving right truncation, plus a second receiver on the same statement to exercise `{ identifier-2 } …`. || REFUTED: PARTIAL -> DIVERGES, and the code-location moves to the symbol that owns the wrong answer (ConditionBinder.cs#Gr3Width; ArithmeticEmitter#EmitComputeBoolean is its only consumer). The adjudicator wrote 'WIDTH MATCHES THE RULE EXACTLY' and stopped at the ITEM-vs-literal distinction. It does not match: the rule says 'the largest boolean ITEM referenced in the expression', and §8.5.2.5 item 3 (--check verified) enumerates as a data item of category boolean 'A group item explicitly or implicitly described with a GROUP-USAGE clause with the BIT phrase.', with §13.18.29.1 (--check verified) saying such a group 'is to be treated as an elementary item of usage bit and category boolean'. So a GROUP-USAGE BIT group IS one of the boolean items whose positions GR3 counts. DEFECT 1 — WRONG ANSWER, SILENT. ConditionBinder.cs:175 reads `BoundBoolRef r => r.Place is RefModPlace ? RefModLen(r.Place) : r.Place.Item.Pic?.Length ?? 0` — raw `Pic`, which is NULL for a bit group (DataBinder.cs:2558 sets `GroupUsage = pic is null ? groupUsage : GroupUsage.None`), so a bit-group operand contributes width 0. The SENDING side accepts it: ConditionBinder.cs:106 — the leaf the file itself labels 'THE ONE category reader (D20/PB79) … a bit group IS a boolean operand' — uses `p.Item.OperandPic?.Category` and returns BoundBoolRef, and BooleanRenderer.cs:26 renders it (`n.Place.Item.IsAsIfElementary ? OperandText.FieldImage(n.Place) : …`, comment 'a bit GROUP's is its AsBits() … D20/PB79'). REPRO: `01 BG GROUP-USAGE BIT. 05 X PIC 1(6). 01 A PIC 1(3) USAGE BIT. 01 R PIC 1(8) USAGE BIT. … COMPUTE R = BG B-OR A.` — Gr3Width = max(0, 3) = 3, CobolBool.Resize truncates the value to 3 positions (CobolBool.cs:111-117), then StrStoreBoolean pads to 8; the rule requires 6 positions before the store. Wrong value, no diagnostic. DEFECT 2 — CRASH ON LEGAL SOURCE, SILENT AT COMPILE TIME (the PB7 shape: it compiles). §8.8.2's first alternative (--check verified) is 'an identifier referencing a boolean data item'; §8.5.2.5 item 4 makes 'A boolean function' such an item, and kb/Work PB68 LANDED exactly that reading for the condition channel (ConditionBinder.cs:112-124 binds a sole boolean-result function to BoundBoolCall). subject: CONTINUE statement
notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.9.4 "Implicit CONTINUE statements shall be processed as if AFTER ZERO SECONDS were specified."` -> OK, GR 2). Derived expectation first: the rule constrains only the DURATION of the implicit no-ops the standard places at control-flow junctions -- it does not create them -- and, since AFTER ZERO is not less than zero, an implicit CONTINUE must also never raise EC-CONTINUE-LESS-THAN-ZERO. So the testable content is: no implicit CONTINUE may reach the pause facility. VERIFIED MECHANICALLY rather than by inspection-of-intent: `CobolTiming.ContinueAfter` has exactly one emit site in the compiler -- RuntimeApi.ContinueAfter (CodeGen/Roslyn/RuntimeApi.cs:133-134) is referenced only by StatementEmitter.Visit(BoundContinueAfter) (StatementEmitter.cs:148-157), and BoundContinueAfter is constructed only by ControlFlowBinder.BindContinue when `cont.arithmeticExpression()` is non-null. READ each implicit site and confirmed each is a zero-cost label or fall-through: DispatchEmitter.EmitParagraphBody emits `__sent{pc}_{k}:` at each inter-sentence boundary as 'the 14.9.19 GR6 implicit CONTINUE after the separator period' (DispatchEmitter.cs:274-290); ControlFlowEmitter emits `__f3fin{n}: ;   // implicit CONTINUE preceding FINALLY (14.9.14.4 GR4 / 14.9.28.4 GR16)` (Verbs/ControlFlowEmitter.cs:109) and `__f3end{n}: ;` for the post-END-PERFORM one; ResumeSignal's RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT and ExitPerformSignal both land on those labels. NO QUALIFYING TEST-REF, and that is honest rather than a gap in the code: the rule's whole content is 'does not pause', which no golden can assert (a wall-clock assertion would be a flake). notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB143) at the ARCHITECTURE the refuter asked for: keyed record images now live in ONE store per resolved host path (KeyedStoreTable, registry-owned - the same key PhysicalFileTable arbitrates sharing/locks by), attached by every relative/indexed connector over that path. Position/key state (FPI, key of reference, GR29a slot, GR38 high-key) stays per-connector. The store is UNCONDITIONAL - two SELECTs to one ASSIGN target reach it with no SHARING clause. pb143_shared_visibility runs the row's exact demanded trace: Q deletes, P reads '23', P writes, Q reads it back, then the CLOSE-order-reversed durability legs. DeleteShared's missing LocksEffective consult was VERIFIED A NON-DEFECT and documented at the site: the siblings gate lock ACQUISITIONS, DELETE acquires none, and GR7's releases are correct by vacuity for a connector holding no locks.

subject: DELETE statement
notes: || REFUTED: overturned CONFORMS -> DIVERGES. GR6 --check OK. Its own text delegates: 'If the RETRY phrase is specified, additional attempts may be made to delete the record AS SPECIFIED IN THE RULES IN 14.7.9' and 'The I-O status is set IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE RULES FOR THE RETRY PHRASE'. The adjudicator cited 14.7.9 one level short and never read 14.7.9.3 GR4 a), which is where the divergence lives. 14.7.9.3 GR4 a) --check OK: 'If the RETRY phrase is not specified OR THE RESULT OF THE EVALUATION OF arithmetic-expression-1 OR arithmetic-expression-2 IS NEGATIVE OR ZERO, the statement is unsuccessful, the appropriate value is placed in the I-O status associated with the file connector according to the rules for 9.1.13'. DEFECT 1 (wrong I-O status on legal source): FileRegistry.RetryLoop is 'string s = attempt(); if (s == Success) return s; switch (kind) { case None: return s; case Times: for (int i = 0; i < amount && s != Success; i++) s = attempt(); return s; default: s = attempt(); return s == Success ? s : FileStatusCode.Deadlock; }'. The Seconds/Forever arm NEVER LOOKS AT amount, so 'DELETE F RECORD RETRY FOR 0 SECONDS' (or a negative/zero arithmetic-expression-2 computed at run time) reports '52' where GR4 a) requires the RETRY-not-specified outcome, i.e. the record operation conflict '51'. 9.1.13.8 --check OK on both: item 1 '51 ... currently locked by another file connector', item 2 '52 ... due to a deadlock'. The TIMES arm is correct for zero/negative (the loop body never runs, so the first attempt's '51' is returned) -- one arm fixed, the other not, the two-arm shape again. DEFECT 2 (same delegated sentence): 14.7.9.3 GR1 requires 'If arithmetic-expression-1 does not evaluate to an integer, the value of arithmetic-expression-1 is ROUNDED UP to the next whole number', but SequentialIoEmitter.RetryAmount renders '(int)(NumericRenderer.Align(num.Render(amount, ReceiverContext.None), 0))' and every arm of NumericRenderer.Align passes CobolRounding.Truncation, so 'RETRY WS-N TIMES' with WS-N = 1.5 makes ONE additional attempt where the rule requires two. Neither is rejected at bind time: StatementBinder.BindRetry does 'rp.SECONDS() is not null ? new RetrySpec(RetryKind.Seconds, Expr.BindExpr(...)) : new RetrySpec(RetryKind.Times, Expr.BindExpr(...))' with no range or integrality check. || UPHELD half (re-read, not inherited): the conflict detection and the a)/b)/c) consequences. KeyedIoEmitter.EmitDelete routes through SequentialIoEmitter.LockGoverned(file, BoundRecordLock.None, del.Retry) to FileRegistry.DeleteShared, which computes 'target = c.MutationTargetRecordId(image)' (RelativeConnector: LastReadRecordId in sequential access, else _pendingKey; IndexedConnector: LastReadRecordId else the prime-key slice) and, on a non-Success RetryLoop result, does 'c.SetStatus(conflict); return conflict;' BEFORE calling DeleteRecord -- a) the record is untouched, b) the status is stored (EmitStoreFileStatus), c) EmitInvalid/EmitUseHook see a non-'0' first character. Golden: file_sharing_mutate.out DELQ51=51 (no RETRY) and DELQRT=51 (RETRY 1 TIMES exhausts), with DELQ=00 after UNLOCK F-P proving GR6 a). The deadlock-bail for a POSITIVE seconds/forever value remains defensible latitude under 9.1.13.8 item 2 ('The implementor shall specify under what conditions a deadlock is detected'); GR4 a) removes that latitude only for zero/negative. || What would close the row: make RetryLoop honour the GR4 a) zero/negative gate for Seconds as it already does for Times, round the RETRY amount UP per GR1, and add a 2002 golden covering DELETE ... RETRY FOR 0 SECONDS -> 51, RETRY FOR n SECONDS -> 52, and a fractional TIMES count.

subject: DELETE statement
notes: || UPHELD as PARTIAL, but the adjudicator's BASIS is REFUTED and replaced. GR7 a) 1. --check OK ('A lock held by that file connector on the deleted record is released at the completion of the successful execution'). VERIFIED HALF -- the action, re-read: FileRegistry.DeleteShared ends 'if (status.Length > 0 && status[0] == '0' && target.Length > 0) PhysicalFileTable.ReleaseSingle(st, name, target);' -- gated on success ('0x') and applied to the deleted record's own id, exactly 'at the completion of the successful execution'. PhysicalFileTable.ReleaseSingle removes the entry only when the recorded owner is this connector, and State.RecordLocks is 'Dictionary<string,string>' recId -> ONE owner, which 9.1.16 licenses. || REFUTED -- the APPLY COMMIT mechanism the adjudicator asserted is WRONG, and its conclusion inverts. The claim was that 'COMMIT lexes as a facility IDENTIFIER' so 'APPLY COMMIT ON F' is absorbed by genericClause and silently dropped. It is not: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolLexer.g4 line 436 defines a dedicated token 'COMMIT : 'COMMIT' ;', and genericClause (CobolExpressions.g4) is 'IDENTIFIER (IDENTIFIER | literal)*' over the IDENTIFIER TOKEN -- not over cobolWord, which is the rule that lists COMMIT as a context-sensitive user word (CobolWords.g4). So in 'ioControlParagraph : I_O_CONTROL DOT (ioControlClause DOT?)*', genericClause consumes only 'APPLY' (no APPLY token exists, so it lexes as IDENTIFIER), the COMMIT token matches no alternative of ioControlClause, the loop exits and COMMIT is left unmatched -> a syntax error. 12.4.6.3.2's format is 'APPLY COMMIT ON [ [ file-name-1 ] [ identifier-1 ] ]...', so the clause is LOUDLY REJECTED, not silently swallowed. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW: no program this compiler accepts can be subject to an active APPLY COMMIT clause, so GR7's guard 'the file is not subject to an active APPLY COMMIT clause' is VACUOUSLY SATISFIED and the unconditional releases are correct for everything that compiles. The gap is a 12.4.6.3 NOT-IMPLEMENTED (consistent with StatementBinder routing the COMMIT and ROLLBACK STATEMENTS to BindUnsupportedFacility), not a GR7 divergence. || REMAINING UNVERIFIED HALF (why PARTIAL still stands): GR7's OTHER antecedent conjunct, 'If record locks are in effect', is never evaluated on this path. DeleteShared performs ReleaseAllExcept and ReleaseSingle without consulting LocksEffective, unlike its own siblings RewriteShared ('if (phrase == FileRecordLock.WithLock && LocksEffective(meta, st, name))') and WriteShared. It is benign TODAY only because LocksEffective's first line is 'if (meta.LockMode == FileLockMode.None) return false;' so a SHARING-only connector can hold no lock to release -- an accident of another method's guard, not a check on this one. And no test drives DELETE through DeleteShared with a lock held: tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/CobolFileLockTests.cs exercises ReleaseSingle/ReleaseAllForConnector as PRIMITIVES, and file_sharing_mutate never locks a record through the deleting connector. What would close the row: gate the GR7 releases on the same LocksEffective predicate the sibling verbs use, and add a 2002 golden that READs a record WITH LOCK, DELETEs it, and shows a second connector can then lock the same id.

notes: || UPHELD as PARTIAL, with the adjudicator's basis REFUTED and replaced (see GR-14.9.10.4-7 for the full refutation). This row is the flattened TAIL of 14.9.10.4 GR7's nested list (GR7 a) 2. and GR7 b)) -- the catalog-segmentation artifact tracked by PB39/PB55; both texts --check OK against 14.9.10.4. VERIFIED HALF -- the actions, re-read: GR7 a) 2. is FileRegistry.DeleteShared's FIRST act, 'if (!meta.Multiple) PhysicalFileTable.ReleaseAllExcept(st, name, target);', ahead of the GR6 conflict check and ahead of DeleteRecord -- 'at the beginning of the execution' and correctly NOT gated on success, unlike a) 1. and b). ReleaseAllExcept drops every lock owned by this connector whose key is not the target, so the deleted record's own lock survives to the completion rules. The '!meta.Multiple' guard is genuinely 'single record locking is specified': I traced meta.Multiple to SequentialIoEmitter.EmitSharingRegistration's 'bool multiple = file.LockMode?.Multiple ?? false;' passed into FileRegistry.RegisterSharing, i.e. the LOCK ON MULTIPLE RECORDS flag. COMMIT is a dedicated lexer token (CobolLexer.g4:436) and genericClause is 'IDENTIFIER (IDENTIFIER | literal)*' over the IDENTIFIER token, not over cobolWord, so 'APPLY COMMIT ON F' leaves COMMIT unmatched at the end of ioControlParagraph's clause loop and is a SYNTAX ERROR. The clause is loudly rejected, so GR7's 'not subject to an active APPLY COMMIT clause' guard is vacuously satisfied for every program that compiles and these releases are correct there; the missing feature belongs to 12.4.6.3. || REMAINING UNVERIFIED HALF (why PARTIAL stands): the multiple-record-locking branch is exercised by NOTHING. No fixture or unit test drives a DELETE through DeleteShared under LOCK ON MULTIPLE RECORDS, nor with a lock held on ANOTHER record so that ReleaseAllExcept has anything to drop (CobolFileLockTests exercises ReleaseSingle/ReleaseAllForConnector as primitives; file_sharing_mutate holds locks only through the NON-deleting connector, which is the GR6 path). Neither branch of the '!meta.Multiple' dispatch has ever been observed on a DELETE. What would close the row: a 2002 golden under LOCK MODE IS MANUAL WITH LOCK ON MULTIPLE RECORDS that locks two records, DELETEs one, and shows the other lock intact -- plus its single-locking twin showing the other lock gone at statement start.

subject: DELETE statement
notes: Derived the expected shape from 9.1.14 first: on the invalid key condition the status is a '2x' value and, if INVALID KEY is specified, exception processing is NOT executed and control goes to imperative-statement-1 (item 2); if INVALID KEY is NOT specified, the applicable exception processing statements DO run (item 3); when no invalid key condition exists, an unsuccessful non-invalid-key status still runs exception processing (not-exists item 1) and a successful status takes NOT INVALID KEY if present (not-exists item 2). Read the three implementing symbols. KeyedIoEmitter.EmitDelete emits, in order, EmitStoreFileStatus, then 'SeqIo.EmitUseHook(file, invalidKeyHandled: del.InvalidKey?.Invalid is not null)', then EmitInvalid. EmitInvalid renders 'if (st[0] == \'2\') { imp-1 } else if (st[0] == \'0\') { imp-2 }' when INVALID KEY is present, and the bare 'if (st[0] == \'0\') { imp-2 }' when only NOT INVALID KEY is written -- so imp-2 fires only on successful completion ('00' and '02' both begin '0'), matching not-exists item 2. The suppression is correctly SCOPED, not blanket: DispatchEmitter's generated __IoCheck body reads 'if (__invKey && __st[0] == \'2\') return;' -- so a '43' or '49' DELETE still runs the USE declarative even though an INVALID KEY phrase is written, which is exactly item 3 / not-exists item 1 and is the arm a blanket suppression would have gotten wrong. The EC-checked variant __IoCheckEc takes the same __invKey argument. NO qualifying test: no golden or negative fixture in tests/conformance writes DELETE ... INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY at all. Closing this row needs a golden on an indexed or relative file that (a) deletes a missing key and lands in INVALID KEY, (b) deletes a present key and lands in NOT INVALID KEY, and (c) proves a USE declarative is suppressed for the '23' but still fires for a '43'. || UPHELD: I re-derived 9.1.14 from the spec before reading these notes and all four arms match. I also verified the half the adjudicator did not name, which is where this rule usually breaks: 9.1.14 item 1 requires that 'if enabled, the EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY exception condition is set to exist' EVEN WHEN the INVALID KEY phrase suppresses the processing. EcEmitter.EmitIoCheckEc (EcEmitter.cs:427-454) emits 'if (__en) ExceptionState.SetIo(...)' BEFORE 'if (__invKey && __st[0] == \'2\') return -1;', so the condition is set and only the processing is suppressed -- had those two lines been in the other order, FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS after a handled INVALID KEY would have answered wrongly. DispatchEmitter.EmitIoCheck (DispatchEmitter.cs:220-226) returns on '0' first ('successful -- no declarative (ISO 14.9.49.4 GR6)'), so no declarative can interleave between EmitStoreFileStatus and EmitInvalid on the NOT INVALID KEY path. __invKey is 'del.InvalidKey?.Invalid is not null' -- keyed on the POSITIVE phrase only -- so a NOT-INVALID-KEY-only DELETE that lands on '23' still runs exception processing (item 3). HAZARD recorded but charged elsewhere: EmitInvalid branches on the runtime's RETURNED local __kstN while EmitStoreFileStatus and EmitUseHook read CobolFile.Status(name); the two channels agree on every reachable DELETE RECORD arm but diverge on FileRegistry.DeleteRecord's fall-through arms, which is why I downgraded GR-14.9.10.4-10 rather than this row. Verdict stays CONFORMS-but-untested, which ground rule 3 makes a legitimate outcome; the three closing goldens named above are the right ones.

The status reaches the program through 'c.SetStatus(status)' plus the emitter's SeqIo.EmitStoreFileStatus(df.File). This matches 9.1.13.7 item 1 ('I-O status = 41. An OPEN statement or a DELETE FILE statement that is attempted for a file connector in an open mode'). One reading note, not a defect: the RetryLoop sharing probe is evaluated eagerly before the IsOpen test, but OpenByAnotherConnector excludes the connector itself and the IsOpen arm wins the assignment, so the outcome is '41' regardless of a RETRY phrase. NO qualifying test: conformance:2023/delete_file_sharing exercises the OTHER-connector '62' path (DELETE FILE F-B while F-A holds the file open), never the same-connector '41'; delete_file and delete_file_absent both CLOSE or never open. Closing this row needs a golden doing OPEN OUTPUT F / DELETE FILE F / pin FILE STATUS = 41 and then proving the file still exists. || UPHELD: re-read FileRegistry.DeleteFile (FileRegistry.cs:367-387). 'if (c.IsOpen) status = FileStatusCode.FileAlreadyOpen;' is the first assignment and every later arm is in its else-chain, so the try block that calls File.Delete is never entered -- the file survives, which is the substance of 'shall not be open'. FileStatus.cs:35 gives FileAlreadyOpen = \"41\", and I validated the status independently (cite.py --check 9.1.13.7 -> 'OK 9.1.13.7 1) I-O status = 41. An OPEN statement or a DELETE FILE statement that is attempted for a file connector in an open mode.'). I re-examined the eager-RetryLoop ordering and agree it cannot change the ANSWER: RetryLoop (FileRegistry.cs:739-753) never sleeps and whatever it returns is discarded by the IsOpen arm -- a wasted probe, not a conformance defect (it IS worth fixing for the reason GR15 gives, since the same eager call is what produces '52' there). The success classification is load-bearing and is implemented: KeyedIoEmitter.EmitDeleteFile branches on 'st[0] != \'0\'' for ON EXCEPTION, so '05' takes the NOT ON EXCEPTION arm, and its comment states the rule ('\'05\' (absent file) is a SUCCESSFUL completion (GR14) and takes the NOT ON EXCEPTION path'). Two spec-derived goldens close it: tests/conformance/2023/delete_file_absent.cob deletes a never-created file with both phrases written and its .out is exactly 'NOEXC' + 'ST=05' -- proving both the value and the success classification; tests/conformance/2023/delete_file_sharing.cob re-deletes an already-deleted file and pins 'DEL05=05'. subject: DELETE statement
notes: Read FileRegistry.DeleteFile plus its helper OpenByAnotherConnector. The conflict probe is 'RetryLoop(() => OpenByAnotherConnector(name, c.HostPath) ? FileStatusCode.DeleteFileSharing : FileStatusCode.Success, retryKind, retryAmount)' with DeleteFileSharing = \"62\", and when it does not clear, 'status = sharing' is taken BEFORE the try block that calls File.Delete -- so sub-rule (a) 'the file is not deleted, and may be accessed' holds by construction, (b) the '62' value is produced, and (c) the statement is unsuccessful (st[0] != '0' routes to ON EXCEPTION / exception processing in KeyedIoEmitter.EmitDeleteFile). The RETRY half is routed through the same 14.7.9 RetryLoop the record-lock paths use, so 'additional attempts may be made ... as specified in the rules in 14.7.9' is honoured rather than re-implemented. conformance:2023/delete_file_sharing is spec-derived (header cites 9.1.13.9 item 2 / 14.9.10 GR15) and its .out pins DEL62=62 (no RETRY), DELRT=62 (RETRY 2 TIMES exhausts), DELFV=52 (RETRY FOREVER deadlock-bails per 9.1.13.8 item 2, whose detection conditions the standard leaves to the implementor), then DEL00=00 after the other connector closes -- which is also the direct proof of sub-rule (a), since the file was still there to delete. Two things the golden does NOT show and that I did not treat as closed: the ON EXCEPTION arm firing on a '62' (only the NOT ON EXCEPTION arm on '05' is covered, by delete_file_absent), and RETRY FOR n SECONDS, which is the documented single-run-unit residue (no external releaser exists in one process, so it bails rather than sleeps). Note the premise wording: GR15 gates on 'file locking is in effect ... locked by another file connector' while the code gates on open-by-another-connector; 9.1.13.9 item 2 defines '62' in exactly the code's terms, and COBOL.NET's implementor-defined default sharing mode is exclusive (14.9.27 GR23), so the two premises coincide here. The trailing NOTE about APPLY COMMIT is informative, not normative. || REFUTED: CONFORMS -> DIVERGES, and the test-ref is REMOVED because the golden PINS the divergent value. The no-RETRY and n-TIMES arms are right; the SECONDS and FOREVER arms place a status this rule forbids. FileRegistry.RetryLoop (FileRegistry.cs:739-753) carries a 'default:' arm for Seconds/Forever -- 's = attempt(); return s == FileStatusCode.Success ? s : FileStatusCode.Deadlock;' -- with FileStatus.cs:81 Deadlock = \"52\", and DeleteFile assigns it straight through ('else if (sharing != FileStatusCode.Success) status = sharing;'). GR15 sub-rule (b) is unconditional once the file sharing conflict condition exists; validated verbatim against the transcription (cite.py --check 14.9.10.4 'b) The valu62\' is placed into the I-O status associated with file-name-1 to indicate the file operation conflict condition.' -> OK 14.9.10.4 15); the OCR has eaten \"e '\" out of \"value '62'\", but the intended value is unambiguous and is confirmed from the other side by 9.1.13.9 2) (validated: 'I-O status = 62. A file sharing conflict condition exists because a DELETE FILE statement is attempted on a physical file and that physical file is currently open by another file connector.'). The condition still EXISTS on this arm -- the other connector never released the physical file, nothing cleared it -- so (b) applies. '52' is not a file-sharing status at all: 9.1.13.8 is titled 'Record operation conflict condition with unsuccessful completion' and its item 2 (validated: 'I-O status = 52. The input-output statement is unsuccessful due to a deadlock. The implementor shall specify under what conditions a deadlock is detected.') sits under the RECORD conflict condition. The latitude the standard grants there is over WHEN a deadlock is detected, not over answering a FILE-sharing conflict with a RECORD-conflict status. Two independent corroborations that '52' is out of bounds here: Annex E.3.3 item 35 enumerates the statuses the new DELETE FILE may set as '05', '37', '39', '41' and '62' -- '52' is absent (validated); and the project's own docs/COBOLNET_FILES_DESIGN.md:117 lists the DELETE FILE error paths as 41 / 62 / 37 with no 52, so the code also contradicts its own design SSOT. SECOND, narrower divergence in the same arm: 14.7.9.3 4) a) (validated: 'If the RETRY phrase is not specified or the result of the evaluation of arithmetic-expression-1 or arithmetic-expression-2 is negative or zero, the statement is unsuccessful, the appropriate value is placed in the I-O status ... according to the rules for 9.1.13') means RETRY FOR 0 SECONDS must behave exactly as the no-RETRY case, i.e. '62'. RetryLoop's Times arm honours it (the 'for (int i = 0; i < amount ...)' loop runs zero times and returns the first attempt's '62'), but the Seconds arm IGNORES the 'amount' parameter entirely and still bails to '52'. And 14.7.9.3 3) (validated: 'If the FOREVER phrase is specified, the mass storage control system shall attempt to gain access to a locked resource until the input-output operation has been completed') is not met by a single re-check. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS to a forbidden operand: FieldOperand binds a BoundFieldOperand, and at emit OperandText.FieldAsString falls through every arm of its final 'p.Item.Pic switch' (Alphanumeric / NumericEdited / National / Boolean / Numeric / float are enumerated; PicCategory.Pointer, PicCategory.ProgramPointer and PicCategory.ObjectReference are not) to the default arm '_ => $"{PlaceRenderer.Read(p)}.ToString()"'. So 'DISPLAY WS-PTR' over '01 WS-PTR USAGE POINTER.' compiles clean and prints ManagedPointer.ToString() -- a value with no COBOL meaning -- and 'DISPLAY WS-OBJ' over an OBJECT REFERENCE item prints the CLR object's ToString(). Both classes are fully modelled here (PicInfo.cs:296/302, carriers 'ManagedPointer' and the object-reference type; DataBinder.Ptr.cs / DataBinder.Oo.cs), so this is reachable from ordinary source, not theoretical. THE THIRD CLASS IS VACUOUS AND SHOULD NOT BE COUNTED AS PASSING: class message-tag has no Usage member at all (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:60-68 states the MCS facility is unmodelled and deliberately gets no dead enum member), so no message-tag operand can be constructed -- the rule's third arm is satisfied by absence, not by a check. I read OperandText.cs end to end and confirmed the fall-through: FieldAsString's terminal switch enumerates { IsUnsignedWideBinary }, { Numeric, IsFloat: false }, { Numeric } (float), and { Alphanumeric or NumericEdited or National or Boolean }, then '_ => $"{PlaceRenderer.Read(p)}.ToString()"'. subject: DISPLAY statement
notes: FORMAT 2 default rule and the twin of GR15: 'If the COLUMN phrase is not specified, the screen record starts in column 1.' The COLUMN/COL phrase is not in displayStatement (CobolParserCore.g4:1301). Interesting asymmetry checked while deriving this: COLUMN and COL ARE alternatives of cobolWord (CobolWords.g4 lines 24-27, present for report-writer / data-name use), so unlike AT and LINE they would lex as a data-name in the operand list -- 'DISPLAY SG COLUMN 5' does not draw a syntax error at the DISPLAY rule; it binds as a THREE-operand Format-1 device DISPLAY of SG, a name COLUMN, and the literal 5, and then fails (or stages loud) on the unresolved name. That is the shape to watch when Format 2 is added: the omission default must be driven by an absent PHRASE, not by an absent token, or the COLUMN-as-data-name path will silently satisfy it. As with GR15 this needs its own golden (a DISPLAY with LINE but no COLUMN). || UPHELD, and the asymmetry is confirmed by my own read of CobolWords.g4 (COL, COLS, COLUMN, COLUMNS all present as cobolWord alternatives; AT, LINE, EXCEPTION, NUMBER all absent). One refinement: because NUMBER is ALSO absent from cobolWord, the fully-spelled 'DISPLAY SG COLUMN NUMBER 5' IS a parse error while the optional-word-elided 'DISPLAY SG COLUMN 5' is not -- so the same source construct fails in two different ways depending on whether the programmer wrote an OPTIONAL word. That inconsistency is a symptom of the missing format, not a separate defect, but it is the concrete reason the eventual Format-2 grammar must add AT/LINE/NUMBER to the statement rule rather than lean on token absence.

subject: DISPLAY statement
notes: FORMAT 2 control flow on FAILURE, in three legs: (a) ON EXCEPTION present -> imperative-statement-1, then end of statement, NOT ON EXCEPTION ignored; (b) ON EXCEPTION absent -> the exception-checking PERFORM WHEN phrase, else an applicable USE declarative, control returning to the end of the statement with NOT ON EXCEPTION ignored; (c) neither phrase nor any exception-processing procedure -> straight to the end of the statement, NOT ON EXCEPTION ignored. NONE of it exists, and the reason is upstream of the control flow: there is no notion of an UNSUCCESSFUL DISPLAY at all. BoundDisplay (BoundTree.cs:552) carries only Operands / NoAdvancing / ToStdErr, and AcceptDisplayEmitter.EmitDisplay emits a bare Console.Write/WriteLine with no status, no exception set and no branch, so legs (b) and (c) -- which do not even need the phrases, only a failure signal to route -- are unreachable too. Grep confirms no site raises any EC-SCREEN-* (see GR19). Note leg (b) is the one that would remain missing even if only the phrases were added to the grammar: it needs a failure signal wired to the PERFORM/USE exception machinery, not just two imperative-statement slots. || UPHELD, and I checked the three-leg reading against the spec text myself (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:23500-23511): leg (b) is itself split into b)1 the exception-checking PERFORM WHEN phrase and b)2 the applicable USE declarative, and leg (c) is the no-procedure fall-through -- the adjudicator's summary is faithful. Re-read EmitDisplay: the emitted statement is a single Console.Write/WriteLine call with no try, no status variable and no branch, so there is no place a failure signal could even be observed. The 'upstream of the control flow' diagnosis is correct: the missing thing is the UNSUCCESSFUL determination (GR19), not the two imperative-statement slots.

subject: DIVIDE statement
notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.12.3 "Literal-1 and literal-2 shall be numeric literals"` -> OK, SR 3). DERIVED FIRST: every literal reachable in the DIVIDE literal slots must be rejected at compile time unless it is a numeric literal. The grammar makes the whole literal family reachable — `divideOperand : literal | functionCall | dataReference`, `literal : numericLiteral | nonNumericLiteral`, and `nonNumericLiteral : figurativeConstant | concatenationExpression | STRINGLIT | NATLIT | BOOLLIT | HEXLIT` (Core/CobolExpressions.g4) — and divideIntoOperand has its own `literal` alternative for the literal-2 slot. READ ExpressionBinder.NumLiteral arm by arm: a concatenationExpression -> COBOLNET0844 error; a NATLIT or BOOLLIT -> COBOLNET0844 error; a figurativeConstant -> BoundNumLiteral("0") for ZERO, else a bare `BoundExprError` with NO ctx.Edition.Error call; everything else -> `new BoundNumLiteral(CheckLiteral(lit.GetText()))`. ENFORCED HALF: national, boolean and concatenation literals are rejected with a COBOL diagnostic citing 8.8.1.1 (validated: `cite.py --check 8.8.1.1 "an identifier referencing a numeric data item"` OK — 'An arithmetic expression may be an identifier referencing a numeric data item, a numeric literal, the figurative constant ZERO'). UNENFORCED HALF, two shapes: (i) a plain alphanumeric STRINGLIT or a HEXLIT falls through to BoundNumLiteral carrying the RAW quoted text; NumericRenderer.LiteralNum -> EmitText.UnscaledLit -> IntLiteralX returns `"ABC"L` (mag.Length <= 18 branch), so `DIVIDE "ABC" INTO X GIVING Y` fails as a ROSLYN parse error on generated C#, never as a COBOL diagnostic — the exact wrong-stage shape landed kb/Work PB94 fixed for the VALUE clause, unfixed here; (ii) a non-ZERO figurative (`DIVIDE SPACE INTO X GIVING Y`) becomes a BoundExprError, which NumericRenderer.Visit(BoundExprError) renders as `NotImplemented.Value<long>(...)` — a runtime loud. NO TEST: I searched tests/conformance/negative for a DIVIDE fixture (`grep -rln DIVIDE tests/conformance/negative/*.cob`) — none exists, and no fixture covers an alphanumeric literal in any arithmetic operand slot. TO CLOSE: extend NumLiteral's rejection to STRINGLIT/HEXLIT and to a non-ZERO figurative with a COBOLNET0844-class diagnostic, plus negative fixtures in a DIVIDE operand position. || UPHELD (independent read of ExpressionBinder.cs:628-650 and :655-686): the four arms are exactly as described — the concatenation arm and the NATLIT/BOOLLIT arm call `ctx.Edition.Error("COBOLNET0844", …)`; the figurative arm returns `new BoundExprError(...)` with NO Error call for anything but ZERO; and the final `return new BoundNumLiteral(CheckLiteral(lit.GetText()));` is reached by STRINGLIT and HEXLIT. I followed CheckLiteral to its end (:655-686) to be sure nothing downstream rejects: it normalizes the decimal separator, has a floating-point-form branch, then `ctx.Edition.CheckDigitCapacity(text.Count(char.IsAsciiDigit), …)` — a DIGIT-COUNT check that a zero-digit literal like "ABC" passes silently. subject: DIVIDE statement
notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.12.3 "the composite of operands described in 14.7.7, Arithmetic statements, is determined by using all of the operands in the statement excluding the data item that follows the word REMAINDER"` -> OK, SR 4). DERIVED FIRST, and this rule has THREE testable edges: it applies only under NATIVE arithmetic; it counts ALL operands, which for DIVIDE INCLUDES the GIVING resultants (unlike ADD/SUBTRACT Format 2, whose own SR1b excludes them); and it EXCLUDES identifier-4 alone. READ: StatementValidation.CheckComposite opens with `if (data.Options.Arithmetic != ArithmeticMode.Native) return true;` — edge 1. Its signature is (verb, operands, receivers) and it superimposes both lists on their decimal points via Shape(digits, scale), applying 14.7.7 rule 2b's exclusion of binary-char/-short/-long/-double and float usages, then errors COBOLNET0805 past 31 digits. Checked all four DIVIDE call sites in ArithmeticBinder.BindDivide: Format 1 `CheckComposite("DIVIDE", [a], intoRecv)`; Format 2 `[dividendX, a], recv`; Format 3 `[a, divisorX], recv` — each passes the GIVING/INTO resultants as receivers, so they ARE superimposed (edge 2, and deliberately different from the ADD/SUBTRACT sites two methods above, which pass `[]` with an explicit 14.9.2.3 SR1b comment); Formats 4-5 `CheckComposite("DIVIDE", [dividend, divisor], quotients)` — the REMAINDER Place `r` is never passed to it (edge 3, exactly SR4's exclusion). All three edges match the rule text. NO TEST-REF: the only COBOLNET0805 assertion in the tree is StandardDecimalTests' 40-digit ADD, and tests/conformance/2023/ca4_giving_composite.cob covers the ADD/SUBTRACT exclusion — neither exercises DIVIDE, and nothing exercises the identifier-4 exclusion. || REFUTED — verdict CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The three edges the adjudicator tested are right; a FOURTH, which it did not derive, is wrong. SR4 says the composite uses ALL of the operands EXCLUDING only the data item after REMAINDER — and the explicit exclusion of identifier-4, itself a resultant, is what proves resultants ARE operands for this rule (otherwise the exclusion would be vacuous). But StatementValidation.cs:119-121 defines `static bool InComposite(PicInfo p) => p is { Category: PicCategory.Numeric, IsFloat: false } && p.Usage is not (BinaryChar or BinaryShort or BinaryLong or BinaryDouble);` and both the operand loop (:126) and the receiver loop (:137-139) gate on it, so a NUMERIC-EDITED identifier-3 — which SR2 expressly ADMITS (`cite.py --check 14.9.12.3 "Identifier-3 and identifier-4 shall reference an elementary data item of category numeric or numeric-edited"` -> OK) — is silently DROPPED from the superimposition. PicInfo carries Digits and Scale for a numeric-edited item (PictureAnalyzer.cs:341-343), so the data is present; only the category gate excludes it, and 14.7.7 rule 2b's exclusion list (validated by reading spec 21851-21869: intrinsic functions, binary-char/-short/-long/-double, float usages, floating-point literals) does NOT contain numeric-edited. Consequence: `DIVIDE A BY B GIVING E` where E is a numeric-edited mask with 25 digit positions and A/B contribute 10 more fraction digits has a 35-digit composite that SR4 makes nonconforming and CheckComposite passes clean — a violated syntax rule with no diagnostic, against the 4.2.2 duty that SR violations be flaggable. SECOND, opposite-direction defect in the same method: the `case BoundNumLiteral lit:` arm (:129-133) counts `t.Count(char.IsAsciiDigit)` for ANY numeric literal including a FLOATING-POINT one (ExpressionBinder.CheckLiteral :662-681 returns the float form as a BoundNumLiteral), yet 14.7.7 rule 2b excludes 'a floating-point literal' from the composite — so a literal like `1.234567890123456789E10` contributes 19 digits at scale 20 and can push a CONFORMING DIVIDE past 31 into a spurious COBOLNET0805. Note the method already honours rule 2b for float USAGES via `IsFloat: false`; the literal arm was never given the same treatment. TO CLOSE: admit numeric-edited receivers into InComposite (keeping the rule-2b usage exclusions), skip a floating-point-form literal in OfExpr, and add two goldens — a DIVIDE whose composite is legal only because identifier-4 is excluded, and a DIVIDE whose numeric-edited identifier-3 pushes the composite past 31 and must be rejected.

notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.12.4 "the remainder is the result of multiplying the subsidiary quotient and the divisor and subtracting the product from the dividend"` -> OK, GR 7). READ: EmitDivideRemainder builds `var product = new NumX($"({qt} * {divisor.Expr})", qs + divisor.Scale)` — qt is the GR6c subsidiary quotient at the quotient receiver's scale, and the NumX scale qs + divisor.Scale is the exact scale of the product so the subtraction aligns radix points without loss — then `NumX remainder = num.Combine(dividend, "-", product, rcv)`. That is GR7's expression literally, over the SAME snapshotted dividend/divisor GR2 defines (both materialized by Snapshot(num.FixedLane(...)) before the quotient store, so a quotient receiver aliasing a sender cannot poison it). Both arithmetic lanes are covered by that one Combine: native falls to CombineNative, and STANDARD/STANDARD-DECIMAL to `CobolDec.Sub(..., IntermediateMode)`, i.e. GR7's second sentence. subject: Offset time formats
notes: CITATION re-derived mechanically, all four normative sentences separately: cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.1 'A zero to indicate that offset from UTC was not available on the system on which the information was recorded' -> OK (marker '3)'); 'If the data contains a zero in that character position, the offset-hours and offset-minutes subfields of the data shall both contain zero' -> OK; 'If the values contained in offset-hours and offset-minutes subfields of data in a receiving field associated with an offset subformat are both zero, the position corresponding to the plus sign in the format shall contain a plus sign' -> OK; 'The colon character in the offset subformat of an extended offset time format appears in the data associated with the format' -> OK. This is a COMPOUND rule with FOUR normative obligations plus three informative NOTEs; I located and read the implementation of every one. (a) '0' IS A PERMITTED SIGN VALUE. CobolDate.cs#Analyze lines 510-516: 'if (s.Field == Fld.OffSign) { ... char c = data[pos]; if (c is not ('+' or '-')) { if (c == '0') offZero = true; else return pos + 1; } pos++; continue; }' -- exactly the three values rules 1-3 enumerate are admitted and every other character yields the 1-based error position §15.92.4 requires. (b) A '0' SIGN FORCES BOTH SUBFIELDS TO ZERO. Analyze line 531: 'if (offZero && s.Field is Fld.OffHour or Fld.OffMinute) hi = 0;' collapses the §15.3.3.6.2 ranges (0..23 hours, 0..59 minutes) to the single value 0 for both, and the offZero flag is set before either is read because §15.3.3.6.1 puts the sign first in the subformat. Traced the per-digit narrowing at lines 543-548 by hand: sign '0' with hours '05' errors at the SECOND hours digit (the leading '0' is still consistent with the only legal '00'), which is the earliest character at which the error is determinable -- the §15.92.4 contract, not an off-by-one. (c) THE RECEIVING-FIELD REQUIREMENT ('+' when both subfields are zero). CobolDate.cs#EmitFormatted line 363 'osign = offsetMinutes >= 0 ? '+' : '-'' can never produce '0' at all, and yields '+' at offsetMinutes == 0; lines 361-362 make oh/om zero only when offsetMinutes is exactly 0 (|offset| in 1..59 gives om != 0, >= 60 gives oh != 0), so the '-'-with-+0000 counterexample is unreachable. Verified by golden: conformance:2023/pb11_datetime_format_grammar 'OMIT-OFF=010000+0000' for FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss+hhmm" 3600) with argument-3 omitted (§15.41.3 r6 evaluates it as 0) -- literally NOTE 3's '+0000'. (d) THE COLON OF AN EXTENDED OFFSET SUBFORMAT APPEARS IN THE DATA. CobolDate.cs#Tokenize line 277 emits Seg(IsField:false, Sep:':', InData:true); EmitFormatted line 369 'if (!s.IsField) { if (s.InData) sb.Append(s.Sep); continue; }' writes it, and Analyze lines 504-508 REQUIRE it in the data ('if (pos >= data.Length || data[pos] != s.Sep) return pos + 1'). Verified by golden: pb11 'T-OFF=01:00:00+01:00'. The bind-time recognizer agrees on the subformat's two shapes -- DateTimeFormatGrammar.cs#ZoneOfWidth lines 119-122 accept the five-character '+hhmm' and six-character '+hh:mm' and require the offset's width to MATCH the common part's, so a basic/extended chimera never reaches the runtime. Also confirmed the FORMAT always carries '+' as the placeholder and never a '-': Tokenize's '-' arm (line 276) does not set afterOffSign, so a hyphen is only ever the extended-date separator -- the format/data asymmetry these three rules describe is modelled correctly rather than collapsed. HONEST RESIDUE (why this row stays test-needed even at CONFORMS): obligations (a) and (b) -- the SENDING-field permission to write '0' with zero magnitude, and its rejection when the magnitude is non-zero -- are verified by implementation reading ONLY. No golden in tests/conformance/ feeds a '0' into an offset sign position; pb23 exercises the consuming path with '+' ('19950215T05142781+0500', the D.31.5.8/D.31.5.9 examples) and pb11 pins the producing path, so the cited tests close (c) and (d) but not (a)/(b). A closing golden would be TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("hhmmss+hhmm", "01000000000") = 0 with the non-zero-magnitude mate asserting the error position. NOTE 2's cross-reference to CURRENT-DATE / WHEN-COMPILED is informative and lands outside this clause: CobolDate.cs#Format21 renders §15.21.3's separate 21-character layout, whose position 17 is '0' only when the system lacks the local-time-differential facility -- .NET's DateTimeOffset always has one, so '+'/'-' is always correct there. Editions rationale identical to GR-15.3.3.6.1-1. || REFUTED: verdict CONFIRMED at CONFORMS after an independent re-derivation and a hand-trace of every branch; the record is changed to record what the note over-claimed and what residue remains. (1) ALL FOUR CITATIONS RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY and all return OK on §15.3.3.6.1 marker '3)'. Reading the clause whole shows FIVE normative sentences, not four: the note folds the SENDING-field permission ('For offset-time values used as sending fields, the position ... may contain a zero provided that ...' -- --check OK) into obligation (a) rather than naming it. It is nonetheless implemented by the same Analyze line 514 arm, so the omission is a labelling one. (2) OBLIGATION (b) HAND-TRACED, NOT ACCEPTED: with sign '0' Analyze line 531 forces hi = 0 while lo stays 0 for both Fld.OffHour (0,23) and Fld.OffMinute (0,59), and the per-digit narrowing at 543-548 then admits '00' and rejects everything else at the earliest determinable character -- I walked '01000000000' (accepted, returns 0), '0'+hours '01' (error at the SECOND hours digit, data position 9) and '0'+minutes '10' (error at the FIRST minute digit, position 10), all of which match §15.92.4's 'first position at which the error can be determined'. subject: Intrinsic functions
notes: NOTE 1 item 2 - an EAE's result is implementor-defined if one or more of the ARGUMENTS are implementor-defined. Citation: cite.py --check 15.4.1 'One or more of the arguments are implementor-defined' -> OK (§15.4.1 rule 2; the near-identical L2.2 a) is disambiguated by its lettered marker, so this row is anchored on the NUMBERED item). This is a latitude/composition statement, not a behaviour requirement: nothing has to be enforced, and the only way to contradict it would be to over-define a result whose argument is implementor-defined. WHAT I READ. IntrinsicRenderer.Arg/RawArg/DecArg is the ONE argument intake for the numeric channel (every arm consumes Arg(...) or its raw/Dec twin - the class comment and the PB32/PB14 remarks on Landed make that the deliberate single seam), and it renders an argument through NumericRenderer.AsNum WITHOUT redefining its value, so an argument whose value is implementor-defined (a nested FUNCTION RANDOM - §15.75.3 r4 seed, §15.75.4 r3 domain subset; FUNCTION SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT - §15.80.3 r3 implementor-specified precision; FUNCTION FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE - §15.38.4 r2 accuracy) propagates its implementor-defined value into the enclosing EAE unchanged, and the compiler makes no claim to the contrary anywhere. The class of implementor-defined argument the compiler DOES take a documented position on is the floating-point carrier: docs/CONFORMANCE.md item 92 row 2 states 'when ANY argument renders as floating-point (COMP-1/COMP-2/FLOAT-SHORT/FLOAT-LONG/FLOAT-EXTENDED), the function's equivalent arithmetic expression is evaluated in IEEE binary64', and IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum's AnyRealArgument dispatch plus the RealMethod convention implement it. TEST-REF DELIBERATELY EMPTY - the row stays test-needed. conformance:2023/pb2_float_argument_exact_family is spec-derived and pins the float-ARGUMENT determination, but a COMP-2 item's VALUE is not implementor-defined (only its representation is), so it is corroboration, not a cover. A closing test would put a genuinely implementor-defined value in an argument position - e.g. FUNCTION INTEGER-PART(FUNCTION SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT) or FUNCTION MAX(FUNCTION RANDOM(1), 0) - and assert the enclosing function's result tracks the documented determination for that argument. EDITIONS: batch default; no edition delta in the item's text. || REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. TWO INDEPENDENT COSTS, both admitted inside the record itself. (1) ZERO INSTANCES OF THE RULE WERE ACTUALLY TRACED. The record names the rule's real instances (a nested RANDOM, SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT, FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE) and then verifies NONE of them; the single class it does verify - the floating-point carrier - it disqualifies in its own words ('a COMP-2 item's VALUE is not implementor-defined ... it is corroboration, not a cover'). A CONFORMS whose only positive evidence is conceded not to be an instance of the rule is an unverified edge under rule 5, and with an empty test-ref there is nothing else holding it up. (2) THE SINGLE-SEAM PREMISE IS FALSE, AND THE FILE SAYS SO. 'IntrinsicRenderer.Arg/RawArg/DecArg is the ONE argument intake for the numeric channel' is contradicted by the same file, which carries at least five argument intakes with DIFFERENT value semantics: Arg (IntrinsicRenderer.cs:457), RawArg (:511) / DecArg (:515) / DecOf (:522), Dbl (:712) / DblOf (:525) for the binary64 lane, IntArg -> AsInt (:716, :734) which RESCALES TO 0 WITH TRUNCATION for the integer positions, and RawArgPairs (:771) for the selection family - plus Str/StrArgList for the string channel. The record read one of them. Worse, `Arg` itself is `Landed(num.AsNum(...))`, and NumericRenderer.Landed (NumericRenderer.cs:647-654) is NOT the value-preserving pass-through the note describes: for an SDIDI-carried argument it emits `DecToUnscaledIntermediate(x.Expr, ws, CobolRounding.Truncation)` at `ws = rcv.WorkingScale(NumvalScaleFloor)` (ReceiverContext.cs:61 - the floor is 6). The renderer's own PB56 remark records the consequence in the same file: 'a fixed working scale truncated sub-microscale operands to zero'. So the note's load-bearing sentence - 'it renders an argument ... WITHOUT redefining its value' - is refuted at the exact line it cites. I did NOT find an over-definition of an implementor-defined argument's value (I traced FUNCTION INTEGER-PART(FUNCTION SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT), which keeps the §15.80.3 r3 scale-7 tick carrier through Landed's identity arm for exact Int128, and FUNCTION MAX over a mixed RANDOM/fixed list, which routes to the PB65 SDIDI selection arm), which is why this is PARTIAL and not DIVERGES. Verdict PARTIAL, code-location and empty test-ref kept: the row stays test-needed, and the closing test the record itself sketches is still the right one.

subject: Intrinsic functions
notes: NOTE 1 item 3 - an EAE's result is implementor-defined if one or more of the arithmetic expressions that COMPOSE it produces implementor-defined results. ⛔ Citation anchored on the wording that separates it from its sibling: --check 15.4.1 'produces implementor-defined results' -> OK at §15.4.1 rule 3), while --check 15.4.1 'produce implementor-defined results' -> OK at §15.4.1 rule 2) letter b) (the standard-mode twin, which is inside RV-15.4.1-L2.2's text). The composing-expression case this compiler actually meets is exponentiation with a non-integer exponent, which §8.8.1.5.4 rule 2 e) makes implementor-defined ('Otherwise, the equivalent arithmetic expression is defined by the implementor. Operands used in the development of that value shall be in SDIDI form' - --check 8.8.1.5.4 OK; the one-level-short §8.8.1.5 does not contain it). IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum's standard-mode arm renders FUNCTION EXP as RuntimeApi.DecPow(RuntimeApi.DecE, DecArg(ic,0)) and FUNCTION EXP10 as DecPow(DecFrom('10','0'), ...) - and NumericRenderer.Power (the `**` operator's renderer) emits RuntimeApi.DecPow(DecOperand(b), DecOperand(e)) under the same mode, i.e. the function and the spelled-out EAE reach the SAME CobolDec.Pow with the same operands, so the implementor-defined result the composing expression produces is ONE result, not two. RenderNum's own standard-mode arm holds the four constant/power rows the R18 work landed (E and PI as the exact 34-digit CobolDec.E/CobolDec.Pi of §15.27.3 r3 / §15.73.3 r3, EXP and EXP10 through the SAME CobolDec.Pow the `**` operator uses), so those EAEs agree with their spelled-out forms by construction. FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION's EAE is '(FUNCTION SQRT (FUNCTION VARIANCE (argument-list)))' (--check 15.86.4 -> OK, rule 1), and under standard-decimal the value of FUNCTION SQRT is fixed by §15.84.4 rule 2: 'the returned value is the absolute value of the exact square root of argument-1 rounded to 34 digits according to the rules for standard-decimal arithmetic' (--check 15.84.4 -> OK). Binary64 carries ~17 significant digits where the rule requires 34, and a 31-digit receiver can see the difference: VARIANCE(1,2,3) = 2/3, whose root to 34 digits is 0.8164965809277260327324280249019..., while the shipped path yields the binary64 0.816496580927726 and zeros beyond it. subject: CONCAT function
notes: 'StrArgList(ic) => string.Join(", ", ic.Args.Select(Str))' renders every argument in SOURCE ORDER into one 'Concat(params string[] parts) => string.Concat(parts)' call, a left-to-right fold — the iterated form §15.18.4 r4 prescribes (each concatenation's result becomes argument-1 of the next iteration). Concatenation is associative and no iteration truncates (the intermediate is not a fixed-size receiver anywhere in the model), so the flat n-ary call and the iterated model produce the identical value at every argument count. The TYPE consequence of the iteration was worked through explicitly and adds nothing beyond r2/r3: for every legal mix, the iterated result category (r3 applied per iteration with the intermediate as argument-1) equals the flat reading — e.g. CONCAT(alphabetic, alphabetic, alphanumeric) is alphanumeric both ways — so no r4-specific defect exists; the r2/r3 mislabelling is carried on those rows and is open there. Re-verified on the built CLI for this review: 'FUNCTION CONCAT("A", "B", "C", "D", "E")' → 'ABCDE'; 8 arguments → '1234567AB'; 'FUNCTION CONCAT("a" "b" "c")' → 'abc' and the explicitly nested 'FUNCTION CONCAT(FUNCTION CONCAT("a" "b") "c")' → the same 'abc'; and the §15.3 variable-repetition ALL subscript 'FUNCTION CONCAT(A TE(ALL))' over '05 TE PIC X(2) OCCURS 3' → 'AB P1P2P3', i.e. one implicit argument-2 per occurrence, left to right, which is r4's trigger reached through a single written argument. "+" : "-") + Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours).ToString("00") + Math.Abs(t.Offset.Minutes).ToString("00"). InvariantCulture pins the proleptic Gregorian calendar and ASCII digits (positions 1-4). DELIMITED BY SIZE contributes exactly 21 characters - so no receiver scale hides a layout defect. VERIFIED BY DIRECT EXECUTION OF THE SHIPPING METHOD (loaded src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/Cobol.Net.Runtime.dll and invoked CobolNet.Runtime.CobolDate.Format21 over fixed DateTimeOffsets, since TimeZoneInfo.Local reads the Windows registry and ignores TZ): +05:45 -> '2026073010331564+0545', -09:30 -> '...-0930', +12:45 -> '...+1245', 00:00 -> '...+0000', -12:00 -> '...-1200', +13:00 -> '...+1300'. So positions 20-21 (the prior pass's unverified edge (b)) are CORRECT for non-zero minute offsets, position 17 is correct on BOTH branches including the 'same as UTC' => '+' boundary, and the '-' branch of 18-19 cannot exceed 12 because no TimeZoneInfo zone is below -12:00. THE ONE OPEN POINT, now demonstrated rather than suspected: +14:00 -> '2026073010331564+1400'. 15.21.3 positions 18-19 state 'If character position 17 is '+', two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 13', and Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours) is UNCLAMPED, so a run on a host whose TimeZoneInfo.Local is 'Line Islands Standard Time' / Pacific-Kiritimati (UTC+14, a zone Windows and IANA both ship) returns '14' there. The reason this is NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION and not DIVERGES: the standard's table offers NO in-range value for a +14 host, so no behavior conforms - emitting 14 (today) is an out-of-range implementor extension, clamping to 13 misreports the offset, and returning '0'/'00'/'00' means 'the system has no facility to provide the local time differential factor', which is false. Nothing in CobolDate.cs, docs/CONFORMANCE.md or the design docs records a decision, and the same unclamped expression also feeds WHEN-COMPILED (15.99.3, identical table). notes: SUSTAINED; both halves of the rule independently re-verified. 'return d.Year * 1000L + d.DayOfYear;' places the Gregorian year in the YYYY positions and the ORDINAL day of that year in DDD — the §15.5.4 Julian date form ('The Julian date form is YYYYDDD, where YYYY represents the year and DDD represents the ordinal date within that year'). YYYY half: 1 -> 1601001 (epoch year), 3067671 -> 9999365 (terminal year), 143951 -> 1995046. DDD half, over the 62-value spec-computed sweep described in RV-15.24.4-1: the leap-day ordinal is counted (2000-02-29 -> 2000060) and 366-day years reach 366 (2000-12-31 -> 2000366), while the century non-leap years do not (1900-12-31 -> 1900365, 1700-03-01 -> 1700060 vs 2000-03-01 -> 2000061), so §15.5.1's Gregorian leap rule is honoured in the DDD positions and not merely in YYYY. notes: UPHELD after varying the RECEIVER as well as the argument. Repertoire appends exactly one character per input character (a substitution replaces, never expands or drops), so the returned string's length is always argument-1's character count, and under D-N1 one national position is one UTF-16 char and one usage-display position.
