Nothing in the tree computes 14114126198520207781233383725636853 / (2 ** 112); CobolIntrinsics.E() is the only body and is Math.E in every mode. WHAT THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED, and it is what makes this an owner DECISION rather than a bug: the standard itself classes this clause as processor-dependent. Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim - cite.py --check A.3 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' -> OK - and 4.5 NOTE, validated verbatim ('These factors can include the use of optional, processor-dependent, or implementor-defined language elements'), together mean a conforming implementation may fail to translate a compilation group that uses it without ceasing to conform. Annex F.2 additionally makes STANDARD-BINARY an obsolete feature, and the standard's own Annex E remark records that it 'has not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider'. The non-support is already recorded at docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 2 ('| 2 | ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1); the native/standard-decimal modes are provided |') - the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT shape, a verdict only the owner may set, hence NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION. BARE QUESTION: should 15.27.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by the existing documented non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY (Annex A.3 item 2 processor-dependence) rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? Identical to the already-adjudicated sibling RV-15.73.3-2 for PI; one decision should settle the whole 15.4.1 family. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY.' at --std 2002 draws COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014 (targeting COBOL-2002)', re-run by me), so the rule's precondition cannot arise at 85 or 2002. subject: FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: CONFIRMED NOT-IMPLEMENTED, independently re-verified. Citation re-validated: §15.40.3 r5 returns whole, including 'If argument-4 is specified, the magnitude of the value shall be less than or equal to 1439.' I re-ran the search rather than trusting the prior pass: `grep -rn 1439 src/ --include=*.cs | grep -v Generated/` returns NOTHING — not in the binder, not in the renderer, not in the runtime. Argument-4 flows `IntrinsicRenderer#RenderFormattedDatetime` -> `ArgInt(ic.Args[3])` -> `CobolDate.EmitFormatted`, which only ever computes `offMag = Math.Abs(offsetMinutes); oh = (int)(offMag / 60); om = (int)(offMag % 60)`. Consequences, both silent: 2000 minutes renders offset-hours 33, violating §15.3.3.6.2 ('The offset-hours subfield of the data associated with a basic or extended offset time format shall contain a value from 00 to 23 inclusive'); 9999 minutes renders 166, so `oh.ToString("00")` emits three characters and the returned value grows past the width the format describes. §15.3 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to be set to exist for an out-of-range argument even though the VALUE is implementor-defined; it is never set. Because argument-4 may be an identifier or an expression this cannot be a compile-time check in general, but it is a one-line runtime guard beside the existing integer-date guard in `CobolDate.FormattedDatetime`. NOT-IMPLEMENTED rather than DIVERGES because there is no implementation to diverge from. The identical rule text is §15.41.3 r4 for FORMATTED-TIME and is equally unimplemented (same sweep). TEST: none.

notes: CONFIRMED NOT-IMPLEMENTED. Citation re-validated: §15.40.3 r6 'Argument-4 shall not be specified if the time portion of the format in argument-1 is neither a UTC format nor an offset format.' NO CODE IMPLEMENTS THIS RULE. Re-read `BindIntrinsicCore`: its only FORMATTED-DATETIME-specific arm is the COBOLNET1517 literal check, and nothing correlates the argument COUNT with the SHAPE of the format literal. `EmitFormatted` does compute both predicates the rule needs — `isUtc` (a 'Z' segment) and the OffSign/OffHour/OffMinute fields — but at RUN time and only to drive emission, never to reject. `FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYMMDDThhmmss", 153569, 45296, 120)` compiles with zero diagnostics, prints 20210616T123456 and discards argument-4 (`hasTime && isUtc && hasOffset` is false and there is no offset field to render into). FULLY COMPILE-TIME DECIDABLE: r1 already forces argument-1 to be a literal, so the binder holds the format string and the argument count at the same point, immediately after the COBOLNET1517 arm, and the tokenizer is already reachable from the compiler through `RuntimeApi.DateFormatFractionDigits`. Note the predicate the fix needs must be the §15.3.1/§15.3.2 FORMAT RECOGNIZER called for under AR-15.40.3-2, not the present `isUtc` proxy — 'Z' anywhere in the string is not 'the time portion is a UTC format' (§15.3.3.5 says a UTC format is a common time format FOLLOWED BY 'Z'). §15.41.3 r5 is the same rule for FORMATTED-TIME and is equally unimplemented. TEST: none.

If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference."

THE VALIDATION ITSELF IS CORRECT and I re-read every leg: CobolDate#Analyze walks the tokenized format against the data, requiring each in-data separator ('-', ':', 'W', 'T', 'Z') to appear, rejecting a non-digit, a short field and any trailing character (`if (pos != data.Length) return pos + 1;`), and range-checking every subfield with per-digit narrowing - year 1601..9999 (§15.3.1.3/.5/.7, "greater than 1600 and less than or equal to 9999"), month 1..12, day-of-month against DaysInMonth, day-of-year against the leap year, week against LongIsoYear, weekday 1..7. I checked LongIsoYear against §15.3.1.7's OWN formulation (53 weeks "if the year subfield represents a common year and January 4 of that year falls on Sunday, or if the year subfield represents a leap year and January 4 of that year falls on a Saturday or Sunday") and derived that it is equivalent to ISO 8601's Jan-1-Thursday / leap-Wednesday rule, which is what ISOWeek.GetWeeksInYear implements - so the week cap is right. A nonzero result becomes ExceptionState#ArgumentError, which I read: it sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION fatal when checking is enabled and otherwise returns 0 - exactly §15.3 rule 14's disposition.

⛔ CORRECTION - THE WEEK-DATE CRASH WINDOW IS TWO DAYS WIDE, NOT ONE. The adjudicator cited only "9999W527". I recomputed .NET's ISOWeek.ToDateTime arithmetic by hand: 9999-01-04 is a MONDAY, so correction = 1 + 3 = 4 and ordinal = 52*7 + d - 4 = 360 + d, evaluated as `new DateTime(9999,1,1).AddDays(ordinal - 1)` against a 365-DAY year. d=5 gives 9999-12-31 (integer date 3,067,671, the §15.5.2 maximum - CORRECT and, usefully, the exact boundary the landed FORMATTED-DATE row pins as "9999W525"); d=6 gives 10000-01-01 and d=7 gives 10000-01-02, BOTH past DateTime.MaxValue, and BOTH throw System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Every §15.3.1.7 subfield rule passes for both: 9999 > 1600 and <= 9999; 9999 is a 52-week ISO year so week 52 is inside 01..52; day-of-week 6 and 7 are inside 1..7. So "YYYYWwwD"/"9999W526" AND "YYYYWwwD"/"9999W527" are both PERMISSIBLE DATA that abort the run unit with a raw CLR stack trace - neither a COBOL value nor a COBOL exception condition, where §15.3 rule 14 fixes the disposition as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result. The extended forms "YYYY-Www-D"/"9999-W52-6" and "9999-W52-7" fault identically (same Analyze leg).

CORROBORATION, NOT INHERITANCE: the landed AR-15.79.3-5 RAN this input against the sibling and its own sweep records `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` as verified crashing identically. notes: VERDICT UPHELD, on stronger evidence than the original, with one citation corrected. CITATION FIX: the original note said '§8.8.4.2.2 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value'; §8.8.4.2.2 is 'General format' and --check FAILS on that text. The clause is §8.8.4.2.4 (--check OK: 'For operands whose class is numeric, a comparison is made with respect to the algebraic value of the operands regardless of the manner in which their usage is described ... Zero is considered a unique value regardless of the sign'). WHY THIS SURVIVES THE ATTACK AT IMPLEMENTATION LEVEL RATHER THAN BY SAMPLING: leftmost-wins is a property of ExtremeIndex ALONE - `for (int i = 1; i < xs.Length; i++) { int c = cmp(xs[i], xs[k]); if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0) k = i; }` - and is independent of the comparator passed in, so it holds identically for all six MaxString/MinString overloads (native pad-compare, the ushort[] alphanumeric-PCS weights, and the NationalCollation variant) and for OrdMaxString/OrdMinString, which is the whole family in one place. The original evidence only exhibited SAME-CONTENT / DIFFERENT-LENGTH ties, which cannot distinguish leftmost-wins from a stable comparator; the refuter added a tie between DIFFERENT CONTENTS of EQUAL VALUE, which is what the rule is actually about, and it passes on the weights overload. The NUMERIC/INDEX half remains vacuous rather than unverified, and the argument is sound: §8.8.4.2.4 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value (and makes signed and unsigned zero one value), §15.59.4 r3 confines the SIZE question to alphanumeric and national, and under standard arithmetic §15.4.1 puts the returned value in a mode-defined intermediate data item whose characteristics come from the mode rather than from the selected argument - so two tied numeric or index arguments have no observable difference in content to choose between. CONTINGENCY WORTH RECORDING: this rule governs which of the TIED arguments is returned; whether the tie is real is RV-15.59.4-1's question, and at the boundaries documented there the 'greatest value' premise is itself wrong. EDITION WINDOW as in AR-15.59.3-1, from Annex E only. EVIDENCE: PROBED, --std 2023. REFUTER'S DECISIVE CASE - an equal-value tie between DIFFERENT contents, on the non-identity-PCS weights overload: E:/Temp/rfmax/tiew.cob (RFMAXTIEW) `OBJECT-COMPUTER. XX PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE AL.` / `SPECIAL-NAMES. subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: A combined WEEK-date-and-time format whose argument-2 is VALID per §15.3.1.7 aborts the run unit with an unhandled .NET exception instead of returning a value. `MOVE FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("YYYYWwwDThhmmss", "9999W527T235959") TO WS-F.` at --std 2014 → 'Unhandled exception. System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException … at System.Globalization.ISOWeek.ToDateTime … at CobolNet.Runtime.CobolDate.Analyze'. Every subfield satisfies §15.3.1.7: year 9999 is >1600 and <=9999; Jan 4 9999 is a Monday so 9999 is a 52-week ISO year and week 52 is inside the permitted 01..52; day-of-week 7 is inside 1..7. The expected result is +86399.00 — D.31.5.9 makes the date VALIDATED BUT DISCARDED for this function, so the integer date form is never needed here at all; Analyze computes it unconditionally at its `else if (hasWeek) integerDate = ISOWeek.ToDateTime(...)` leg, and ISO-9999-W52-7 falls on 10000-01-02, outside DateTime.MaxValue. Even on the most conservative reading (that the denoted date is out of range and r5 is therefore violated), §15.3 fixes the disposition as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result — never a raw CLR stack trace, which is neither a COBOL value nor a COBOL exception condition. Sibling sweep (same Analyze line, both verified crashing identically): `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` and `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` — the latter is the worse one, since §15.92 defines TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME as the VALIDATOR that returns an error position and can therefore never legitimately fault. Fix shape: bound-check the week-date reconstruction (and hand SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME a path that does not build integerDate at all). The rest of r5 is correct and was verified: the mandatory 'T' is required in the data (§15.3.3.7); the D.31.5.9 worked example `("YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm", "19950215T05142781+0500")` → +18867.81 with the offset correctly excluded; Feb-31 in the same format → the §15.3 default 0; the calendar boundary "99991231T235959" → +86399.00. test-needed. ⚙ FIXED AND CLOSED 2026-08-05 (fix-queue PB23). This row's ONLY divergence was the shared week-date reconstruction, and the row itself said so ("ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX"). CobolDate#Analyze no longer calls ISOWeek.ToDateTime: §15.3.1.7 fixes week 1 as "the week that includes January 4", so that week's Monday is computed directly and every later day is a plain integer offset from it — the arithmetic CANNOT overflow, which is the point, because the input is VALID and no tightening of the per-subfield range table could have prevented the fault. The result is then range-checked against §15.5.2's ceiling ("shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to ... 3,067,671"), and ONLY the caller that must PRODUCE an integer date form reacts: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION through ExceptionState#ArgumentError per §15.3 rule 14's "incorrect value ... FOR THE RETURNED VALUE" arm (implementor-defined result 0 when checking is off), while TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME still answers 0 — §15.92.4 requires any non-zero answer to be "the ordinal character position at which the first error ... was detected", and no CHARACTER of "9999W526" is in error (the identical '6' in "2009W526" is valid) — and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME still returns its seconds (§15.79.4 reads only the time subfields). THE TWO-DAY WINDOW THIS ROW RECORDS (d=6 AND d=7) IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not re-derived on paper: 9999-12-31 is ISO 9999-W52-5. The new arithmetic is proven EQUIVALENT to ISOWeek over >200,000 week dates spanning 1601-9999 by unit:CobolDateIntegerDateRangeTests.TheIntegerWeekArithmetic_AgreesWithISOWeek_Everywhere, which asserts its own population so it cannot pass vacuously. ⛔ THE TEST GAP THIS ROW NAMED IS ALSO CLOSED: the golden carries Annex D.31.5.8's and D.31.5.9's OWN worked examples — "YYYYMMDD"/"19950215" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" both -> 143951, and "hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and its combined form both -> 18867.81 — so the §15.48.4 / §15.79.4 NOTE that the other half "does not impact the returned value" is now verified by TEST rather than by code reading.

notes: §15.5.5: a standard numeric time form value is 'a numeric value representing seconds past midnight', and with LEAP-SECOND OFF in effect (the only supported mode; §7.3.17.4 GR1 implies OFF when unspecified) it 'shall be greater than or equal to zero and less than 86,400'. subject: SIN function
notes: Citation validated: cite.py --check 15.82.4 'The returned value is the approximation of the sine of argument-1 and is greater than or equal to' -> OK (rule 1). Implementation: CobolIntrinsics.Sin(double x) => Math.Sin(x), reached through RenderFloat (the catalog row is Float:true). Both halves of the rule verified: (a) approximation - Math.Sin is the binary64 sine with full argument reduction, and S15.82.4 specifies no equivalent arithmetic expression, so per S15.4.1 the approximation is implementor-defined in EVERY arithmetic mode (native: 'the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor'; the standard-mode returned-value-shall-equal-the-EAE requirement applies only 'when ... an equivalent arithmetic expression is specified', which is why SIN is correctly absent from the ArithmeticStandardIntrinsic loud-stage list); (b) range - Math.Sin returns a value in [-1,+1] for every finite double argument. Receiver handling preserves the bound: a FLOAT or receiverless context keeps the binary64 value through RealResult (NaN - reachable only from a non-finite COMP-2 argument - is screened to the S15.3 EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION default 0 or the raise under checking); a FIXED-POINT receiver quantizes through the one FromDouble at FloatWorkingScale >= 9, and rounding a |v| <= 1 value at scale >= 9 can produce at most exactly +/-1.0, still within the rule's bounds. Untested by a spec-derived test: IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests (GnuCOBOL differential) and NIST IF135A pin values but are regression nets - CONFORMS-but-untested.

subject: SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: Citation validated: cite.py --check 15.83.4 'The value returned is equal to the positive algebraic value of smallest finite magnitude that may be used to increment argument-1' -> OK (rule 2), with the NOTE table read from specs/ISO_COBOL.md 33280-33291. Code READ: BindAlgebraicFold -- 'if (sig.Name == SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC) return new BoundNumLiteral(Decimalize(BigInteger.One, pic.Scale, negative: false));' -- a compile-time fold to 10^(-scale) taken BEFORE the HIGHEST/LOWEST capacity branches, so it is independent of digit count, sign and container, which is exactly what r2 says (the smallest INCREMENT, not the smallest representable magnitude of the item's range). Decimalize delegates to CobolNet.Runtime.CobolNum.FormatFunctionText, the same renderer the runtime uses for a computed intrinsic's text, so a NEGATIVE scale (trailing P) appends |scale| zeros and a positive scale inserts the point -- one rule, one place. Every row of the r2 NOTE table checked against a golden or a spec test rather than sampled: S999 -> 1, 99V9(3) -> 0.001 and S9PP -> 100 by SmallestAlgebraic_PictureIncrement_Spec (DISPLAY-exact) and by golden 2023/intrinsics_smallest_algebraic; S9(4) BINARY -> +1 by golden 2023/smallest_algebraic (MOVE to PIC +99999.999 gives '+00001.000'); BINARY-CHAR UNSIGNED -> 1 by golden 2023/intrinsics_smallest_algebraic (a usage-only item carries Scale 0). BINARY-CHAR SIGNED is the only NOTE row without its own case, and it cannot differ: the fold reads pic.Scale and never pic.Signed or the container width. The counter registers fold to 1 via CounterRegisterFold (unsigned integers per 8.4.3.14.4 GR1 / 8.4.3.15.4 GR1), golden 2023/algebraic_counter_registers. Result type is separately correct (IntrinsicResultRule.IntegerFollowsArgument1, the 15.83.1 two-row table). RECORDED LIMIT, charged elsewhere so as not to double-count: a floating-point argument-1 yields NO value at all in ANY arithmetic mode -- licensed by r4 under native, NOT licensed under the two standard modes -- but that is an ADMISSION defect and it is charged on AR-15.83.3-4; for every argument-1 the argument rules admit, the value this rule demands is produced and is exactly right. || REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Citation re-derived (cite.py --check 15.83.4 with the full rule-2 sentence -> OK rule 2). THE FIXED-POINT HALF IS VERIFIED and I strengthened it: the adjudicator asserted the BINARY-CHAR SIGNED row 'cannot differ' without reading the factory, so I read PicInfo.cs:318-328 -- PicInfo.BinaryItem(usage, signed) constructs 'Scale: 0' unconditionally, the 'signed' argument affecting only Digits (BinaryDouble 19 vs 20) and the Signed flag -- so the claim is now evidenced rather than assumed; likewise CobolNum.FormatFunctionText (CobolNum.cs:608-628) was read and its scale<0 arm ('digits + new string(0, -scale)') and scale>0 arm (PadLeft then insert the point) give exactly 100 for S9PP and 0.001 for 99V9(3). THE FLOATING-POINT HALF IS NOT IMPLEMENTED AT ALL, and the adjudicator's own defence of the CONFORMS is contradicted by its own AR-15.83.3-4 finding. Its closing sentence reads 'for every argument-1 the argument rules admit, the value this rule demands is produced'; that is FALSE under OPTIONS ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL or STANDARD-BINARY, where a USAGE FLOAT-LONG item is admitted by r1 (8.5.2.12 item 2 names float-long, read in full), is outside r2 (3.166 = FLOAT-BINARY-* only) and r3 (3.167 = FLOAT-DECIMAL-* only), and is outside r4's native-only licence -- yet BindAlgebraicFold produces no value for it. This is NOT double-counting AR-15.83.3-4: independently of admission, there is no returned-value rule for a floating-point argument-1 anywhere in this method -- the fold is 'Decimalize(One, pic.Scale)', a PICTURE-scale expression that has no meaning for an IEEE float, and the adjudicator's own AR-15.83.3-4 note concedes 'a float lane would need ... a returned value'. So the moment the admission defect is repaired this rule has a hole with nothing to fill it, which is the definition of an unverified half. Rule 5: 'a rule with two halves where one was verified => PARTIAL, always.' Test-refs kept -- all three are spec-derived and all three pin the fixed-point half; none reaches the float half.

subject: SQRT function
notes: CONFORMS. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.84.3 "The value of argument-1 shall be zero or positive"` -> OK §15.84.3 2). THIS IS A VALUE CONSTRAINT, SO THE DISPOSITION THE STANDARD ASKS FOR IS A RUN-TIME EC, NOT A COMPILE-TIME REJECT — §15.3 closing paragraph, read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:29561: 'The rules for a function may place constraints on the permissible values for arguments... If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist... If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference.' So no COBOLNET diagnostic is owed even for the literal FUNCTION SQRT(-4). READ: CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Sqrt (line 28) is `Math.Sqrt(x)`, which is NaN for every x < 0, and the NaN is screened on ALL THREE arms IntrinsicRenderer.cs#RenderFloat can emit — I checked each rather than the one: (a) the fixed-receiver arm quantizes through CobolIntrinsics.cs#FromDouble, whose first line is `if (double.IsNaN(d)) return Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError(...)`; (b) the float-receiver / receiver-less arm (line 431) returns CobolIntrinsics.cs#RealResult(call), which is `double.IsNaN(d) ? ArgumentError(...) : d`; (c) the standard-decimal arm (line 441) wraps the SAME RealResult before CobolDec.FromDouble, so the conversion never sees a NaN either. Arm (b)/(c)'s screen exists precisely because PB13 moved the raise site out from under the unquantized render and a refuter caught it. ExceptionState.cs#ArgumentError (line 248) carries BOTH dispositions the standard names: with ArgumentFunctionChecking set it does Set("EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION", fatal: true) and throws CobolFatalException (§14.6.13.1, Table 13 Fatal); with checking clear it returns 0, the §15.3 implementor-defined default. NO SPURIOUS RAISE AT THE BOUNDARY: -0.0 satisfies 'zero or positive' and Math.Sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0, not NaN, so the screen does not fire on it. GOLDEN: conformance:2023/pb13_domain_raise_receiver_shape line 38 asserts SQRT-NEG=DEFAULT for FUNCTION SQRT(-1) written as a RECEIVER-LESS relation operand — the exact arm that had no screen before PB13 — and its header derives the disposition from §15.3/§15.4. WHAT NO TEST COVERS, verified by reading only: the checking-ENABLED throw for SQRT specifically (no fixture turns EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking on over SQRT — ExceptionState.cs#ArgumentError is the single raise site for the whole family, so this is one branch of one method, not an unaudited path), and the with-receiver COMPUTE arm for SQRT (pb13 pins that arm for ACOS, which shares FromDouble byte-for-byte). REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Citation re-derived independently, not inherited: `cite.py --check 15.84.3 "The value of argument-1 shall be zero or positive"` -> OK §15.84.3 2); the §15.3 disposition paragraph the adjudicator leans on also re-derives (`--check 15.3 "the implementor defines the result of the function reference"` -> OK §15.3 item 14), and §14.6.13.1.1 NOTE 3 (read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:21334ff, "An exception condition is set to exist only if checking for that condition is enabled") confirms that NOT recording the condition with checking off is correct. So the disposition MODEL is right. WHAT IS NOT RIGHT IS THE DETECTOR, and it is invisible to every arm the adjudicator checked because he checked the RENDER arms and not the ARGUMENT CHANNEL. THE CONSTRAINT IS TESTED ON A NARROWED VALUE, NOT ON argument-1. There is no domain guard on the SQRT body at all: CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs:28 is a bare `Math.Sqrt(x)` and the whole family's detection is the NaN artifact. That is sound only while the double the body receives has the same SIGN as argument-1 — and it does not. IntrinsicRenderer.Dbl -> NumericRenderer.Real (NumericRenderer.cs:697) converts an SDIDI operand as `(expr).ToDouble()`, and CobolDec.cs:310 is `(double)Sig * Math.Pow(10, Exp)`. For Exp <= -324 `Math.Pow(10, Exp)` underflows to +0.0, so a NEGATIVE SDIDI becomes -0.0 (verified at the IEEE level: (-1.0)*pow(10,-400) = -0.0, signbit -1), and Math.Sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0 — NOT NaN. Nothing downstream can recover it: RealResult and FromDouble screen `double.IsNaN` ONLY. CONCRETE, LEGAL SOURCE: under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL with `01 A PIC S9V9(30) VALUE -0.000000000000000000000000000001` (= -1E-30, 31 digit positions, legal per §13.18.40.3 SR14), `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SQRT(A * A * A * A * A * A * A * A * A * A * A)` hands the function the exact SDIDI -1E-330 — comfortably inside decimal128's exponent range, so CobolDec carries it — whose value is NEGATIVE and therefore violates §15.84.3 r2. The compiler returns 0 and sets NOTHING: no EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION with checking off (where §15.3's implementor-defined result would at least be defensible), and NO RAISE EVEN WITH CHECKING ON, which §14.6.13.1.1 requires. The rule's ordinary half (a plainly negative argument) IS enforced; its underflow half is not — two halves, one verified, so PARTIAL per rule 5. THE SIBLING IN THE SAME FILE IS THE PROOF THIS IS A MISS AND NOT A DESIGN: CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs:32-33 give LOG and LOG10 an EXPLICIT `x <= 0` guard that names §15.55.3 r2 / §15.56.3 r2 at the BODY, precisely so the domain verdict does not ride on a NaN artifact. SQRT's rule has the same shape and got no guard — and its own in-code comment misnames the clause it is honouring ("argument ≥ 0 (rule 1)"; r1 is the CLASS rule, r2 is the value rule). The fix is a body guard `x < 0 -> ArgumentError("§15.84.3 r2")` beside LOG's, which also closes the -0.0 case by construction. TEST-REF UNCHANGED BUT IT DOES NOT CLOSE THE ROW: pb13_domain_raise_receiver_shape line 38 is `IF FUNCTION SQRT(-1) = 0` — the checking-OFF receiver-less arm only. Nothing anywhere turns EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking on over SQRT (the adjudicator concedes this), and nothing exercises a standard-decimal argument at all. test-needed.

notes: NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION — the same shape already adjudicated for the two siblings RV-15.27.3-2 (FUNCTION E) and RV-15.73.3-2 (FUNCTION PI), both carried at NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION in the inventory today. THE RULE'S PRECONDITION CANNOT HOLD IN THIS COMPILER: DataBinder.cs#BindDeclarations lines 318-320 reject the mode outright — Edition.Error("COBOLNET0806", "ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is an obsolete feature (ISO §8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 / Annex F) and is not supported; use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL") — and the defence is double, because NumericRenderer.cs#StandardDecimal (line 394) is `Arithmetic is ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal or ArithmeticMode.Standard`, which excludes StandardBinary: even if the bind error were downgraded, the render lane taken would be the NATIVE binary64 one, not a 113-bit one. Nothing in the tree can compute a binary128 square root: there is no 113-bit carrier and `grep Sqrt src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Numeric/*.cs` is empty. WHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT A DEFECT: the standard itself classes the enabling clause as processor-dependent — Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim by me, `cite.py --check A.3 "The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor"` -> OK §A.3 2) — and Annex F.2 makes it an obsolete feature; the non-support is already recorded at docs/CONFORMANCE.md line 45, '| 2 | ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1); the native/standard-decimal modes are provided |'. That is the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT shape, a verdict only the owner may set (D13), which is why I record NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION rather than NOT-IMPLEMENTED. BARE QUESTION: should §15.84.4 rule 3 be recorded as discharged by the existing Annex A.3 item-2 documented non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? One decision settles E, PI and SQRT together. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH ITS OWN SIBLING: the standard-DECIMAL rule §15.84.4 r2 is NOT discharged by any such licence — that mode is supported and its rule is DIVERGES (see RV-15.84.4-2), so answering this question does not close §15.84.4. EDITIONS DERIVED FROM THE CONSTRUCT REGISTRY, NOT FROM IntrinsicCatalog: ConstructRegistry.g.cs row 'arithmetic-standard-binary-2014' — introduced 2014, obsolete 2023 — so the rule cannot apply at 85 or 2002. TEST-REF DELIBERATELY EMPTY: the existing StandardDecimalTests coverage exercises the MODE rejection and never references SQRT or any returned value, so per the sibling's struck-test precedent it does not cover this rule; a test pinning that FUNCTION SQRT under STANDARD-BINARY is refused by name would be the honest cover. test-needed.

subject: SQRT function
notes: CONFORMS. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.84.4 "the returned value is the absolute value of the approximation of the square root of argument-1"` -> OK §15.84.4 4). The rule leaves 'the approximation' undefined, and §15.4.1 supplies the latitude for native mode, read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:29777: 'When native arithmetic is in effect, the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor.' READ: CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Sqrt line 28 is `Math.Sqrt(x)`; IEC 60559 requires sqrt to be correctly rounded, so this is the best binary64 approximation available, not merely a plausible one. ALL THREE RENDER ARMS CHECKED at IntrinsicRenderer.cs#RenderFloat rather than the one: (a) a float receiver or a receiver-less context (line 431) returns CobolIntrinsics.cs#RealResult(call) UNQUANTIZED, so FUNCTION SQRT(2) and a COMP-2 item holding that value are the same number — the §15.4 receiver-independence PB13 restored; (b) a fixed-point receiver (line 452) quantizes through CobolIntrinsics.cs#FromDouble at ReceiverContext.FloatWorkingScale (>=9, capped at the receiver's Int128 headroom so the PB5/PB13 9.2e9 saturation cannot reach a declarable receiver), rounding rather than truncating at the quantization point — an approximation landed at the receiver's own scale, which is what §15.4.1 leaves to the implementor; (c) SQRT's catalog row carries Codomain.None, and that is CORRECT rather than an omission — §15.84.4 states no bound on the returned value, so the FromDoubleBounded clamp (which exists for RANDOM's open [0,1) and ASIN/ACOS/ATAN's irrational pi bounds) must not apply here. THE 'ABSOLUTE VALUE' HALF IS VACUOUS BUT I CHECKED IT RATHER THAN ASSUMED IT: §15.84.3 r2 confines argument-1 to zero-or-positive, and Math.Sqrt(x) >= 0 for every x >= 0 (Math.Sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0, which is zero, not negative), so no sign correction is owed and none is missing; a negative argument is an AR-15.84.3-2 violation that takes the NaN -> EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION path instead of yielding a value at all, so it never reaches this rule. GOLDENS: conformance:2002/float_intrinsic pins SQRT=1.4142135623730951 into a COMP-2 — the correctly-rounded double of sqrt(2), whose exact value is 1.41421356237309504880… — proving the unquantized arm keeps full binary64; conformance:2023/pb52_intrinsic_argument_stage pins the quantized arm, SQRT(4)=2.00 and SQRT(NI)=2.00 into PIC 9(6)V99. EDITIONS: SQRT and its native returned-value rule are unchanged across the four editions; batch default, not read off IntrinsicCatalog's IntroducedIn. REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Citation re-derived: `cite.py --check 15.84.4 "the returned value is the absolute value of the approximation of the square root of argument-1"` -> OK §15.84.4 4), and §15.4.1's native latitude re-derives too (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:29777). The APPROXIMATION half is CONFORMING and I re-verified it independently — CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs:28 `Math.Sqrt(x)` is IEC 60559 correctly-rounded, and all four RenderFloat exits are accounted for (line 431 RealResult unquantized for a float/receiver-less context; line 441 the standard-decimal DecFromDouble; the Codomain arm which SQRT's Codomain.None correctly skips; line 452 FromDouble at ReceiverContext.FloatWorkingScale, whose cap I re-derived at ReceiverContext.cs#WorkingScale as min(max(Scale,9), 38-IntegerDigits) and which cannot fall below a legal picture's own scale). THE ABSOLUTE-VALUE HALF WAS DECLARED VACUOUS AND IS NOT, AND IT WAS DECLARED VACUOUS BY THE ONE ARGUMENT THAT FAILS. The adjudicator wrote 'Math.Sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0, which is zero, not negative, so no sign correction is owed and none is missing'. The rule does not say 'made non-negative when negative'; it says the returned value IS THE ABSOLUTE VALUE of the approximation, and IEEE abs clears the sign bit: |-0.0| = +0.0 while sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0 (verified: signbit -1 vs +1). IEC 60559 mandates sqrt(-0) = -0 exactly SO THAT sqrt is not the absolute value there — -0.0 is the unique input on which §15.84.4 r4's 'absolute value' phrase does work, and it is the input the code gets wrong. -0.0 is a LEGAL argument-1: §15.84.3 r2 admits zero, and a COMP-1/COMP-2 item reaches -0.0 by ordinary native underflow (e.g. a product of a negative and a positive tiny float). READ, AND THE READING IS THE FINDING: `grep Abs src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Intrinsics/CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs` returns NOTHING — there is no Math.Abs anywhere on the SQRT path, in the body or in any of the four render arms, so the rule's second half is not implemented, merely unreachable-by-argument. OBSERVABILITY WAS NEVER MEASURED, WHICH IS ITSELF THE PARTIAL: the receiver-less/float arm keeps the value unquantized and the text channel renders it through CobolFloat.cs:25 `Display(double v) => v.ToString(InvariantCulture)`, which on .NET Core 3.0+ is IEEE-faithful and therefore renders a negative zero with its sign — so `DISPLAY FUNCTION SQRT(<a COMP-2 holding -0.0>)` is the candidate wrong output, and a COMP-2 receiver stores the signed zero bit-for-bit. I did not RUN it (read-only), so I report the unverified edge at its honest cost rather than claiming DIVERGES. TEST-REF WEAKENED, NOT STRUCK: conformance:2002/float_intrinsic is a D16-REVIEW golden — its header says 'D16 review', it derives no §15.84.4 clause, and it pins one positive argument — so under rule 3 it is evidence about the binary64 pipeline, not a spec-derived close of r4; pb52_intrinsic_argument_stage likewise derives §15.14.3/§15.50.3 and merely happens to contain SQRT. Both retained as the partial evidence they are. The closing test is one pinning SQRT over a negative-zero float operand. test-needed.

notes: Citation re-derived: `cite.py --check 15.86.3 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric."` -> OK, §15.86.3 1). Read the whole enforcement path end to end. subject: SUM function
notes:
Citation re-derived mechanically: `cite.py --check 15.88.3 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric"` => OK, §15.88.3 rule 1 (Argument rule). READ: IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#Verified row `["SUM"] = Uniform('n', "§15.88.3 r1")` (line 693, in the 'statistical trio' block beside STANDARD-DEVIATION and VARIANCE); IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#Uniform builds an ArgSchema with EMPTY positional kinds and a TAIL rule, so `schema.At(i)` yields the 'n' rule for EVERY argument position — which is what §15.88.2's repeated `{ argument-1 }` needs, since every written argument IS argument-1. Enforcement: IntrinsicBinder.cs#CheckArgumentClasses (line 1652) is called on the generic path at line 587, AFTER arity and BEFORE every per-function arm; it loops all positions and calls IntrinsicArgumentRules.Violation. For kind 'n', Violation reads CandidateClasses(op) and Admissible('n') = [CobolClass.Numeric] — so a numeric-EDITED item (Table 2 class alphanumeric, mapped to CobolClass.NumericEditedDeEditing) is rejected too, which the arm's comment derives from §8.8.1.1 ("an identifier referencing a NUMERIC DATA ITEM"). VERIFIED EDGES: (a) a GROUP argument — ClassOfPlace returns Alphanumeric for `Item.IsGroup` (National/Boolean for an as-if-pic group), so `FUNCTION SUM(grp)` is rejected; (b) an INDEX item — the usage-keyed arm returns CobolClass.Index before the category table, so it cannot pass as numeric; (c) a table(ALL) argument — TableAllPlace is a `PlaceDecorator(Element)` (Place.cs:158), so `p.Item` is the ELEMENT and the element's class is screened, i.e. `SUM(alphaTable(ALL))` is rejected, not failed open; (d) the figurative ZERO is admissible here by §8.3.3.6.4 GR4 (CandidateClasses gives it Numeric among four), correct behavior per the batch's rule 8. FAIL-OPEN residue, deliberate and documented at the Violation head: an operand whose class is not statically decidable (candidates empty) is not screened — that can only miss a rejection, never invent one. TESTS: tests/conformance/negative/pb58-sum-alpha.cob (`COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SUM(N9 X3)`, header cites "ISO 15.88.3 r1", reject-at 2002 2014 2023, expected diagnostic COBOLNET1627 in the .err, registered in tests/conformance/negative/manifest.json:192) and the positive twin tests/conformance/2023/pb58_argument_predicates_legal.cob line 75 (`FUNCTION SUM(N9 I2 3.5)` — registered in tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json:124). Nothing missing for this rule.

REFUTER (verdict SUSTAINED after independent attack): citation re-derived independently — `cite.py --check 15.88.3 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric"` => OK, §15.88.3 rule 1; spec text re-read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33501-33504. Attacked on four axes and each held. (1) TWO-ARM DISPATCH (the shape that has recurred five times in this repo): both `functionCall` alternatives that can spell SUM — the FUNCTION-keyword arm (IntrinsicBinder.cs:89) and the reserved-word keyword-omitted arm `SUM(…)` (IntrinsicBinder.cs:78, CobolExpressions.g4#reservedIntrinsicArgFn) — converge on the SAME BindIntrinsicCore (line 438), whose generic path calls CheckArgumentClasses; there is no unscreened second route, and KeywordOmittedFunction cannot reach SUM at all because a reserved word never arrives in the cobolWord name slot. (2) ArgSchema.At(i) (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:172) returns the Tail rule for EVERY i when Positions is empty, so Uniform('n') genuinely screens all n positions of the repeated argument-1, not just position 1. (3) The two classifier holes I probed are closed: a ref-modified numeric item resolves through RefModPlace.Category (Place.cs:292ff), which implements §8.4.3.3.4 GR6 c) — numeric under display usage is considered class alphanumeric — so `FUNCTION SUM(N9(1:2))` is rejected; and a nested USER-DEFINED function result does NOT fall into the fail-open `BoundComputedOperand => CobolClass.Numeric` catch-all, because UdfBinder.UdfBindCall returns `new BoundNumRef(tempPlace)` over a temp cloned from the RETURNING item's description (§8.4.3.2.4 GR1), so it reaches the screen as a BoundFieldOperand carrying the real category and an alphanumeric-returning UDF is rejected. (4) EDITIONS: CheckArgumentClasses is gated only on `ctx.Edition.Permissive`, never on the edition, so the screen fires at --std 85 as well; the negative fixture's `reject-at: 2002 2014 2023` omits 85 only because that same fixture declares `01 TDEF TYPEDEF STRONG` and `01 NAT PIC N(2)`, both COBOL-2002+ constructs that would make an 85 run reject for the wrong reason — not because the rule is edition-gated. Verdict held at CONFORMS.

subject: SUM function
notes:
Citation re-derived: `cite.py --check 15.88.4 "The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows"` => OK, §15.88.4 rule 1 (Returned value rule); spec lines 33507-33521 carry a/b/c, i.e. the n-ary left-to-right sum. §15.4.1 (read at spec line 29768ff) governs how an EAE is realized per arithmetic mode. ALL THREE LANES READ in IntrinsicRenderer.cs#RenderNum, the ONE dispatcher: (a) STANDARD-DECIMAL / STANDARD — RenderDec's `alwaysDec` list (line 645) names "SumScaled" unconditionally, so SUM ALWAYS evaluates on the SDIDI carrier under a standard mode, emitting CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs#SumDec (`s = xs[0]; for i>0 s = CobolDec.Add(s, xs[i], mode)`) — the EAE evaluated left to right in the standard intermediate data item, exactly §15.4.1's "the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression". (b) NATIVE, fixed-point — `case "SumScaled" or "RangeScaled"` (line 193) takes AlignedArgs (line 756), which aligns every argument to the list's MAXIMUM scale via NumericRenderer.Align and calls CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SumScaled (`Int128 s = 0; foreach (x) s += x`) with the result NumX carried at that common scale; the alignment is escape-checked (CobolNum.RescaleEscape), so an argument that cannot be represented in the Int128 intermediate raises the size-error condition instead of wrapping — §15.4.1 makes the native value an implementor-defined approximation, and the loud boundary is the documented D16/PB32 choice. (c) NATIVE with a floating argument — line 138 routes to RenderFloat(RealMethod("SumScaled")) => CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs#SumReal (`double t = 0; foreach t += x`), again the same left-to-right EAE. The n=1 case falls out of every body unchanged (`(argument-1)`); the n>2 case is the same loop. The ARGUMENT COUNT for the EAE's "n occurrences" comes from the §15.3 ALL enumeration (TryBindAllArgument builds ONE TableAllPlace the backend enumerates over the fixed OCCURS count / the ODO object / the dynamic capacity), so a runtime-ranged list still sums exactly the occurrences the standard specifies. §15.88.1's companion TYPE table is also honored (not this row, but it is the same returned value): IntrinsicCatalog row Result: IntrinsicResultRule.IntegerFollowsAllArguments, resolved in IntrinsicResultType.cs#Resolve as Integer only when every argument is known integer, else Numeric. TESTS: tests/conformance/2023/pb62_standard_decimal_summing_family.cob (header cites 15.88.4; `FUNCTION SUM(10^30, 2)` under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL with ON SIZE ERROR present and not taken) whose golden reads SUM=1000000000000000000000000000002 — the exact EAE value the native Int128 alignment could not hold; tests/conformance/2023/pb62_all_subscript_runtime_ranges.cob goldens SUM=0015000{ over an ODO ALL, MIXED=0039000{ (7+8+9+1+5+9), DYN3=0060000{ (dynamic capacity 3), ALLALL=0021000{ (two-level ALL ALL = 1..6); pb58_argument_predicates_legal.cob goldens SUM=        10.50 for the native mixed integer/scaled list 5+2+3.5. RESIDUE, disclosed: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY — which §15.4.1 also binds to the exact-EAE requirement — is not routed to the SDIDI lane (NumericRenderer.StandardDecimal is true only for StandardDecimal/Standard); it is not a silent divergence, because DataBinder.cs line 318 rejects the clause outright with COBOLNET0806 as a documented obsolete non-support at every edition, so no SUM can be compiled under it. That disposition belongs to §8.8.1.4.1, not to §15.88.4, and is left as an owner-level item rather than counted against this row.

REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. THE ADJUDICATOR'S EVIDENCE FOR THE NATIVE FIXED-POINT LANE IS THE RENDERER'S COMMENT, NOT THE RUNTIME BODY. IntrinsicRenderer.cs:191-192 asserts "SUM/RANGE genuinely ADD, so they keep aligned arguments — now escape-CHECKED (Align emits RescaleEscape): an alignment past the Int128 intermediate is the size-error condition, never a wrap", and the adjudicator's clause "the alignment is escape-checked … so an argument that cannot be represented in the Int128 intermediate raises the size-error condition instead of wrapping" is that comment restated. The guard is real but it is on the PER-ARGUMENT RESCALE ONLY: NumericRenderer.Align (line 526) emits CobolNum.RescaleEscape, whose test is `Int128.Abs(value) > Int128.MaxValue / Pow10Wide(toScale - fromScale)` — it bounds each ALIGNED ARGUMENT, and says nothing about their sum. THE ACCUMULATION IS UNGUARDED: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Intrinsics/CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SumScaled is verbatim `Int128 s = 0; foreach (var x in xs) s += x; return s;` — plain Int128.op_Addition, and neither Directory.Build.props nor src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Cobol.Net.Runtime.csproj sets CheckForOverflowUnderflow, so the context is unchecked and the add WRAPS silently. The same file proves this is a two-arm miss and not a design choice: twenty lines below, MedianScaled and MidrangeScaled route every add through AddForHalving (`try { return checked(a + b); } catch (OverflowException) { throw new CobolSizeError(… "EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW"); }`) and every scale bump through ScaleForHalving, and the PB32 remark introducing them states the policy in terms that cover SUM exactly: "A wrap is never a conforming answer — §15.4.1 asks at worst for 'an implementor-defined approximation', and a value 3.2x out with its top thirty digits wrong approximates nothing." PB32's own note asserts "the ×5/×10 … costs a decimal digit of Int128 headroom that MAX/MIN/SUM/RANGE never spend" — true of the MULTIPLY, and the reason SUM was never swept; the ALIGNMENT spends that headroom just as freely, and the accumulator behind it was never guarded. REACHABLE INSIDE THE COMPILER'S OWN 31-DIGIT CAP (EditionContext.CheckDigitCapacity / MaxDigits): with `P PIC S9(31) VALUE ALL '9'` (9.999999999999999999999999999999e30) beside `Q PIC SV9(7)`, AlignedArgsEx sets the common scale to 7; Align(P,7) = 99999999999999999999999999999990000000, which PASSES RescaleEscape because the bound is Int128.MaxValue / 10^7 = 17014118346046923173168730371588 and |P| is below it. `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SUM(P P P Q)` therefore accumulates 299999999999999999999999999999970000000, which exceeds Int128.MaxValue (170141183460469231731687303715884105727) and wraps to -40282366920938463463374607431798211456, i.e. the VALUE -4.0282366920938463e30 at scale 7. Stored into a `PIC S9(31)` receiver WITH an ON SIZE ERROR phrase: the true value 2.9999999999999999999999999999997e31 needs 32 digits and would raise the size-error condition, while the wrapped value fits the receiver — so the phrase is NOT taken and a wrong, sign-flipped answer is stored silently. That is the identical measured shape PB32 recorded for MIDRANGE ("with an ON SIZE ERROR phrase present and NOT taken") and PB65 for MIN ("a silent Int128 wrap on widening handed MIN a negative result over two positive arguments"), on the one member of the family neither sweep reached. §15.4.1's native latitude is "an implementor-defined approximation of the value of that expression"; a value of the wrong sign and the wrong order of magnitude is not an approximation of it. NATIVE IS THE DEFAULT MODE (OptionsModel.cs:22, cited to §11.9.5.2 r4 — "Default ArithmeticMode.Native when absent"), so this is the lane an ordinary COMPUTE takes, and the lane structure was re-confirmed independently: RenderNum:88 `if (num.StandardDecimal)` -> RenderDec (SumScaled is in the alwaysDec list at line 645) -> SumDec; else RenderNum:107 `AnyDecRaw` -> RenderDec; else RenderNum:135 `AnyRealArgument` -> SumReal; else RenderNum:193 -> the unchecked SumScaled. The Dec lane and the float lane ARE correct as adjudicated; the fourth and default lane is not. notes: cite.py --check 15.89.4 "The returned value is the approximation of the tangent of argument-1." => OK §15.89.4 1) (Returned value rule). BODY: CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs:27 `public static double Tan(double x) => Math.Tan(x);   // §15.89`. Math.Tan takes RADIANS, which is what §15.89.1 requires ("the tangent of an angle or arc, expressed in radians, that is specified by argument-1") — the units half of the rule, checked rather than assumed. §15.89.4 states a PROSE approximation, not an equivalent arithmetic expression, so §15.4.1's last paragraph makes the value implementor-defined in every arithmetic mode and a binary64 Math.Tan satisfies it. ALL THREE RECEIVER LANES READ, NOT SAMPLED (IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat, lines 390–452; TAN routes here because the catalog row's Float flag is true — dispatched at line 109 `if (sig.Float) return RenderFloat(ic, sig.RuntimeMethod)`). (a) Float or receiver-less: `RealResult(Tan(…))` — stays binary64 at full precision, and RealResult is retained precisely so the NaN => EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION raise site is not skipped when the value is not quantized. (b) STANDARD-DECIMAL: `CobolDec.FromDouble(RealResult(Tan(…)))` — the approximation enters as an SDIDI operand per §8.8.1.5.1 and lands ONCE, rather than truncating at a receiver-derived working scale first (PB56). (c) Fixed receiver: `CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble(Tan(…), ws)` with ws = ReceiverContext.FloatWorkingScale. THE CODOMAIN COLUMN IS CORRECTLY EMPTY: the row omits Codomain, so IntrinsicCodomain.None and RenderFloat line 449 takes the unclamped FromDouble arm — right, because the tangent is UNBOUNDED and IntrinsicCodomain exists only for a §15.x.4 rule that STATES a bound (RANDOM's open [0,1), ASIN/ATAN's ±π/2, ACOS's π). Clamping TAN would be the defect here, not the fix. QUANTIZER CHECKED FOR THE SATURATION SHAPE the batch's rule 5 names: I read ReceiverContext.WorkingScale (ReceiverContext.cs:110–116, ws = clamp(max(Scale, 9)) capped at IntermediateDigits − IntegerDigits) and CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble (CobolIntrinsics.cs:211–226). The cap's stated invariant — a value that fits the receiver never saturates, and a value that does not always descales to a sentinel above the receiver's capacity — is what matters for TAN, whose values near π/2 are legitimately huge (Math.Tan(Math.PI/2) ≈ 1.633e16; at ws 9 that is 1.633e25, far inside Int128's 1.7e38, and a receiver too small for it raises the size error per §14.7.5 case 5 rather than silently storing low-order digits). No 9.2e9-class long-carrier saturation exists on this path. ARGUMENT CONVERSION CHECKED: IntrinsicRenderer.Dbl (line 712) => NumericRenderer.Real (NumericRenderer.cs:697–700), which divides the unscaled carrier by 10^scale, with Pow10D handling a NEGATIVE scale (a PICTURE-P trailing-scaled operand), so a scaled argument such as TAN(.001) reaches Math.Tan as 0.001 and not as 1. ONE EDGE NOTED, NOT A DOWNGRADE: an infinite argument (only reachable from a float item holding ±∞, which is outside the standard's data model) makes Math.Tan return NaN, which FromDouble reports as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION "argument out of domain" — arguably over-attributed, since §15.89.3 states no value restriction, but the input is unrepresentable in conforming COBOL so no conforming program can observe it. MISSING: no spec-derived test. Row stays test-needed. Editions: batch default; §15.89.4's wording is unchanged across the four editions and TAN dates from the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment. || REFUTED: CONFORMS => PARTIAL. THE STANDARD-DECIMAL HALF OF THE RETURNED-VALUE DELIVERY IS IMPLEMENTED FOR ONE RECEIVER SHAPE ONLY, AND THE ADJUDICATOR'S LANE (b) IS PRE-EMPTED FOR THE OTHERS. The three arms inside RenderFloat are tested in this order (IntrinsicRenderer.cs, RenderFloat tail): `if (num.Receiver.Real || num.Receiver.Receiverless) return RealResult(call) [Real:true];` THEN `if (num.StandardDecimal) return DecFromDouble(RealResult(call)) [Dec:true];` THEN the FromDouble/FromDoubleBounded quantizer. TAN is exactly the function that reaches those magnitudes (unbounded codomain, values near π/2), so this is not a corner the function cannot occupy. subject: TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD function
notes: CITATION RE-DERIVED: cite.py --check 15.91.4 "the number of days in the year determined by FUNCTION INTEGER" -> OK, 15.91.4 1) b) Returned value rule (the b) leg anchors the marker; a) and c) read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 15.91.4). READ CobolDate.cs#TestDayYyyyddd in full: 'if (day is < 1601000 or > 9999999) return 1; long ddd = day % 1000; if (ddd < 1 || ddd > (DateTime.IsLeapYear((int)(day / 1000)) ? 366 : 365)) return 2; return 0;'. Leg-by-leg against the rule text: (a) the window is literally 1 601 000..9 999 999 and it is tested FIRST, so a negative or short argument answers 1; (b) FUNCTION MOD(argument-1 1000) == day % 1000 because control only reaches it with day >= 1601000 > 0 (C# % and the 15.68-style MOD agree on positives), and FUNCTION INTEGER(argument-1 / 1000) == day / 1000 because integer division IS floor for positives, giving a year in 1601..9999 so DateTime.IsLeapYear can never throw and applies the proleptic Gregorian rule 15.91.1 names; (c) 0 otherwise. No spurious code 3 (D.31.3.9 --checked: zero / 1 / 2 only). TEST: tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_test_validators.cob J1-J6 with golden .out J1=00 (2024366, leap, valid), J2=02 (2023366, common year), J3=02 (1900366, century non-leap), J4=00 (2000366, /400 leap), J5=01 (1600100, below the year window), J6=02 (2024000, day 0) - all three legs exercised, spec-derived (values hand-derived from 15.91.4, registered in 2002/manifest.json). WHY PARTIAL - LEG (a)'s UPPER HALF IS DEFEATED ABOVE 2^63: CodeGen/Emit/IntrinsicRenderer.cs case "TestDateYyyymmdd" or "TestDayYyyyddd" renders RuntimeApi.DateFn(method, IntArg(ic,0)); IntArg -> AsInt -> RuntimeApi.IntegerArg -> CobolIntrinsics.cs#IntegerArg(Int128), which for a value outside long range does NOT call the function at all but calls ExceptionState.ArgumentError, i.e. throws EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION when checking is on and RETURNS 0 when it is off (ExceptionState.cs#ArgumentError: 'return 0, the 15.3 default-result convention'). 0 is TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD's 'the date is valid' answer, so FUNCTION TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD(P) with 01 P PIC 9(19) VALUE 9999999999999999999 reports a VALID date where 15.91.4 r1 a) requires 1 - and the operand really does arrive as Int128, since PicInfo.cs:371 types a field 'Digits > 18 ? "Int128" : "long"'. If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist') does NOT authorise this: 15.91 places no constraint on argument-1's VALUE at all - every integer has a defined answer, and classifying an out-of-window value is the function's whole purpose - so the PB22 landing ('a value the receiving body cannot represent is an incorrect argument'), correct for INTEGER-OF-DAY and its range-guarded siblings, is the wrong shape for the two TEST-* date validators, which should saturate to their r1 a) verdict instead of erroring. kb/Work/PB22.md names neither TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD nor TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD, so this is residue of a landed fix, not a re-report; TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD (RV-15.90.4-1) shares the identical renderer arm and has the identical hole. subject: TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes:
CITATION RE-VALIDATED BY ME: cite.py --check 15.92.3 "Argument-1 shall be a national or alphanumeric literal" -> OK (§15.92.3 1)). I also --check'ed the sibling to be sure I was adjudicating r1 and not the already-landed r2 row: cite.py --check 15.92.3 "The content of argument-1 shall be either a date format, a time format" -> OK (§15.92.3 2)).

THE RULE HAS TWO HALVES AND I READ BOTH IN ONE METHOD. BindIntrinsicCore is the single arm that runs them, which is why it is the code-location rather than either half's helper.
(a) LITERAL. BindIntrinsicCore builds `bool formatFn = sig.Name is "FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE" or ... or "TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME"` and emits COBOLNET1517 when `args.Count > 0 && args[0] is not BoundStringLiteral && formatFn`. I traced the non-literal shapes through ExpressionBinder: a data item binds to BoundFieldOperand, an expression to BoundComputedOperand, a numeric literal to BoundNumericLiteral — none is a BoundStringLiteral, so all are rejected. §8.3.3.6.3 SR1's figurative admission is honoured one line ABOVE the screen: a BoundAllLiteral (`ALL "YYYYMMDD"`) is re-bound to the equivalent BoundStringLiteral, carrying its category, before the test runs (kb/Work PB58 — it used to be a false COBOLNET1517).
(b) NATIONAL OR ALPHANUMERIC. The same method calls CheckArgumentClasses (IntrinsicBinder.cs:1652), which is a no-op for a function absent from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified — so I confirmed the row IS present: ["TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME"] = Schema("§15.92.3 r1/r2", ['s','s'], cross: CrossArgRule.MatchArgument1, crossClause: "§15.92.3 r2"). Position 0's kind 's' resolves through IntrinsicArgumentRules#Admissible to {Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National}. I then traced EVERY literal shape through CandidateClasses -> ClassOf1 -> ClassOfCategory rather than trusting the kind letter: "..." -> Alphanumeric (admitted); N"..." -> National (admitted — ExpressionBinder#NationalLiteralOperand yields a BoundStringLiteral with Category National, so half (a) does NOT reject a national format literal, which is precisely the over-rejection this rule's second word invites); B"..." -> Boolean (also a BoundStringLiteral, so it survives half (a) and is rejected HERE — the two halves genuinely cover different shapes and neither is redundant); a numeric literal -> Numeric (rejected by both). The 's' set's third member NumericEditedDeEditing is unreachable at this position because there is no numeric-edited LITERAL, so the INTERSECTION of the two halves is exactly "national or alphanumeric literal" — no over- and no under-rejection.

THE ONE READING THAT COULD OVERTURN THIS, PRE-EMPTED. §8.3.3.6.3 SR1 ("A figurative constant may be used whenever 'literal' appears in a format or when a rule allows it") means a BARE figurative — SPACE, ZERO — technically satisfies "literal" here, and BindIntrinsicCore's half (a) rejects it with COBOLNET1517 because a BoundFigurative is not a BoundStringLiteral (only the ALL form is pre-converted). That is NOT an over-rejection of legal source: §15.92.3 r2 requires argument-1's CONTENT to be a date, time or combined format, and no figurative constant's value is one, so every such program is illegal on r2 regardless. The only consequence is the diagnostic CODE (COBOLNET1517 rather than the DateTimeFormatKindMismatch r2 arm), never the accept/reject answer. Recorded because a refuter reaching for SR1 will land here.

EDITIONS derived from the standard, NOT from IntrinsicCatalog's row: I grepped every occurrence of the name in specs/ISO_COBOL.md (TOC, the §8.11 name list, Table 21 at :29997, §15.92, Annex D.31.5.10, the index) and ANNEX E — the 2014->2023 change record — carries none, so the rule is unchanged at 2023; the already-landed sibling row AR-15.92.3-2 on this same clause records the same 2014,2023 window, and IntrinsicCatalog's IntroducedIn 2014 is corroboration I did not derive the answer from.

TEST EVIDENCE, AND ITS LIMIT. conformance:2014/formatted_datetime is spec-derived and exercises the ADMISSION side — three TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME references with alphanumeric literal formats, all accepted (golden TF1/TF2/FCD) — so the screen provably does not turn legal source away. ⚠ THE REJECTION SIDE HAS NO TEST UNDER THIS FUNCTION'S NAME: I grepped tests/ for COBOLNET1517 and the only spec-derived negative is conformance-test:IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.FormattedDate_NonLiteralFormat_1517, which drives the IDENTICAL shared formatFn arm under FORMATTED-DATE's name; and nothing anywhere feeds this function a boolean or numeric argument-1, so the class half is unexercised for it. The verdict rests on the implementation reading above, not on that test.

REFUTED: verdict AFFIRMED (CONFORMS), TEST-REF STRIPPED TO "" — the listed golden does not close a RESTRICTION rule.
I re-derived the citation myself: cite.py --check 15.92.3 "Argument-1 shall be a national or alphanumeric literal" -> OK (§15.92.3 1)).
I RE-READ BOTH HALVES INDEPENDENTLY AND THE INTERSECTION IS EXACTLY THE RULE. Half (b): IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs Verified carries ["TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME"] = Schema("§15.92.3 r1/r2", ['s','s'], cross: MatchArgument1); Admissible('s') = [Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National] (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs, the kind table); ClassOf1 maps a BoundStringLiteral through ClassOfCategory(sl.Category), so N"…" -> National (admitted) and B"…" -> Boolean (rejected). Violation's `candidates.Length == 0 => return null` fail-open cannot open a hole at this position, because a BoundStringLiteral never yields an empty candidate set. Half (a) therefore rejects every non-literal and half (b) rejects exactly the boolean literal — the adjudicator's reading is correct and I confirm it.
ONE SHAPE THE ADJUDICATOR'S ENUMERATION MISSED, AND IT STRENGTHENS THE VERDICT RATHER THAN BREAKING IT: a CONSTANT-NAME. IntrinsicBinder.BindArgOperand has an arm ahead of the numeric-expression path — `if (SoleDataReference(a) is { } cref && ctx.Data.ConstantOf(cref) is { Category: not PicCategory.Numeric } k) return new BoundStringLiteral(k.Text) { Category = k.Category };` (kb/Work R01, landed) — so `01 K-FMT CONSTANT AS "YYYYMMDD".` used as argument-1 is a BoundStringLiteral carrying the constant's own category. §13.10.4 GR1 ("the effect of specifying constant-name-1 in other than this entry is as if literal-1 … were written where constant-name-1 is written", spec line 14724) makes that the required answer, and BOTH halves screen it correctly. I probed this expecting an over-rejection and found the arm already there.
⛔ WHY THE TEST-REF GOES. `conformance:2014/formatted_datetime` writes three TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME references (TF1/TF2/FCD), every one of them with a plain uppercase ALPHANUMERIC literal format. DELETE BOTH HALVES OF THE SCREEN — the COBOLNET1517 arm and the Verified row — and that golden still passes byte-for-byte, because nothing in it is on the rejection side. A green gate that never looked at what the rule does is not evidence it holds (feedback_green_gates_arent_evidence). I grepped tests/ for the rejection side myself and confirm the adjudicator's own admission: the ONLY spec-derived COBOLNET1517 negative is IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.FormattedDate_NonLiteralFormat_1517, whose body compiles `FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATE(FMT, 153569)` and whose comment cites §15.39.3 r1 — a DIFFERENT rule row under a DIFFERENT function's name, which rule 3 does not let stand as this row's closing test; and NOTHING anywhere feeds this function a boolean or a numeric argument-1, so the class half is unexercised at every edition. Per rule 3 the honest test-ref is empty and the row stays test-needed. The verdict is unchanged because rule 5 costs verification, not coverage, and I verified both halves in the implementation.

subject: TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes:
CITATION RE-VALIDATED BY ME: cite.py --check 15.92.4 "the value returned is the ordinal character position at which the first error in argument-2 was detected" -> OK (§15.92.4 1)).

BOTH HALVES READ IN THE IMPLEMENTATION, NEVER SAMPLED. CobolDate#TestFormattedDatetime is a one-line pass-through (`=> Analyze(format, data, out _, out _, out _, out _, leapSecond)`), so CobolDate#Analyze IS this rule and is the code-location.
(a) ZERO. Analyze returns 0 only after every format segment has been consumed AND `pos == data.Length`; every other exit is non-zero.
(b) THE ORDINAL POSITION. Every failure arm returns `pos + 1`, the 1-BASED index of the character under examination: a separator segment whose character does not appear (`data[pos] != s.Sep`), an offset-sign character that is not '+'/'-'/'0', data exhausted mid-field, a non-digit in a digit subfield, a subfield provably out of range, and the first TRAILING character (`if (pos != data.Length) return pos + 1`).

⛔ THE LOAD-BEARING PART IS "THE FIRST ERROR ... DETECTED", AND IT IS IMPLEMENTED AS PER-DIGIT RANGE NARROWING RATHER THAN A PER-FIELD CHECK — a per-field check would have reported the START of the offending field and failed the NOTE. After consuming digit k of a width-w subfield, Analyze widens the partial value into [mn, mx] by appending the w-1-k digits still to come (`mn *= 10; mx = mx*10 + 9`) and returns pos+1 the moment `mx < lo || mn > hi`. I HAND-TRACED BOTH OF THE NOTE'S OWN EXAMPLES through that loop:
 · "yyyymmdd"/"20051314": the month subfield is [1,12]; at its first digit '1' the interval is [10,19], which straddles 12, so nothing is provable yet; at '3' it is [13,13] and 13 > 12, so the return is pos+1 = 6. That is the NOTE's 6 AND the NOTE's reason ("the character '3' occupies the first position in which it can be determined that an error has occurred").
 · "yyyymmdd"/"15990316": the year subfield is [1601,9999] (§15.3.1.3's "greater than 1600"); at '1' the interval is [1000,1999], which straddles 1601; at '5' it is [1500,1599] and 1599 < 1601, so the return is 2 — the NOTE's 2, for the NOTE's reason.
I checked the subfield bounds against the spec text rather than the comments: §15.3.3.3 verbatim gives hours "00 to 23", minutes "00 to 59", seconds "< 60" with LEAP-SECOND OFF and "< 61" with ON; Analyze uses (0,23), (0,59) and (0, leapSecond ? 60 : 59). Month is [1,12], day-of-month is bounded by DateTime.DaysInMonth of the already-parsed year/month, day-of-year by the leap year, week by LongIsoYear, weekday [1,7]. The Fraction subfield is deliberately EXEMPT from narrowing, which is right — §15.3.3.2 puts no range on it.

DELIBERATE, AND CORRECT UNDER THIS RULE: `dateRepresentable` is ignored here. REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Three findings; the first is a two-arm bound where only one arm was checked, on the very method that IS this rule.
Citation re-derived by me: cite.py --check 15.92.4 "the value returned is the ordinal character position at which the first error in argument-2 was detected" -> OK (§15.92.4 1)).
⛔ (1) THE OFFSET SUBFIELD BOUNDS WERE VERIFIED AGAINST THE WRONG CLAUSE. The adjudication states it checked the subfield bounds against the spec text and names §15.3.3.3 — "hours '00 to 23', minutes '00 to 59'" — then lists "Analyze uses (0,23), (0,59)". But those two switch arms are SHARED: `Fld.Hour => (0, 23)` is joined by `Fld.OffHour => (0, 23)`, and the minutes arm is written `Fld.Minute or Fld.OffMinute => (0, 59)` — ONE expression serving TWO subfields. §15.3.3.3 governs only one of them, by its own words: cite.py --check 15.3.3.3 "The minutes subfield of the data (corresponding to mm in a common time format) shall contain a value from 00 to 59 inclusive" -> OK, and the offset subformat is NOT part of the common time format — §15.3.3.6.1 defines the offset-hours and offset-minutes subfields separately (cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.1 "two lowercase 'h' characters representing the hours portion of the offset from UTC" -> OK). The clause that actually governs them is §15.3.3.6.2, which the adjudication never located: "The offset-hours subfield of the data associated with a basic or extended offset time format shall contain a value from 00 to 23 inclusive" / "… offset-minutes … from 00 to 59 inclusive" (specs/ISO_COBOL.md :29747, :29749). I ran that clause down expecting an invented range and the VALUES turn out right — but a bound justified by a clause that does not cover it is an unverified bound, and §15.92.4's answer is conditioned on exactly "format problems or RANGE problems". Neither `Fld.OffHour` nor `Fld.OffMinute` carries a citation in the source, while every neighbouring bound does. Rule 5: an edge unverified => PARTIAL.
⛔ (2) THE SHORT-ARGUMENT-2 ANSWER IS OUTSIDE THE RULE'S CODOMAIN, AND ITS DEFENCE IS A CLAUSE ABOUT A DIFFERENT FUNCTION. When argument-2 is shorter than the format, Analyze's `if (pos >= data.Length) return pos + 1;` yields data.Length + 1 — a position that does not exist in argument-2 — where §15.92.4 admits only "the ordinal character position at which the first error IN ARGUMENT-2 was detected". The input is REACHABLE: §15.92.3 places no size rule on argument-2 and the compiler applies none — I read the row, `Schema("§15.92.3 r1/r2", ['s','s'], cross: MatchArgument1)`, and it carries no ArgPredicate width at either position (contrast TRIM's `.WithPredicate(1, ArgPredicate.ExactWidth(1, …))` five rows above it). The adjudication defends the answer with §15.93.4 r1 c)'s `(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1)` — a real, --check-able clause that legislates TEST-NUMVAL's returned value, not this function's; that is the a_real_clause_can_answer_a_different_question shape, and it is the whole of the evidence offered. No test covers the shape and docs/CONFORMANCE.md carries no determination for it (its only §15.92 entry is item 112, the LEAP-SECOND one).
⛔ (3) THE "BOTH NOTE EXAMPLES" CLAIM IS NOT WHAT THE CODE DOES. §15.92.4's NOTE writes `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME ("yyyymmdd", A-DATE)` in LOWERCASE. Both recognisers are case-SENSITIVE: CobolDate.Tokenize's switch matches 'Y'/'M'/'D' uppercase only (lowercase falls to `default` -> `return null`, and Analyze then answers 1), and DateTimeFormatGrammar.BasicDates holds the literal strings ["YYYYMMDD", "YYYYDDD", "YYYYWwwD"], so bind-time Classify returns null and the reference is rejected with DateTimeFormatKindMismatch. The NOTE's own program does not compile. That is DEFENSIBLE — §15.3.1.2 normatively requires "four uppercase 'Y' characters … two uppercase 'M' characters", and a NOTE is not normative — but the adjudication asserts "I HAND-TRACED BOTH OF THE NOTE'S OWN EXAMPLES" and every test silently substitutes uppercase (grep for "yyyymmdd" across tests/ returns nothing). The traced program is not the NOTE's program, and the substitution was never recorded.
WHAT I RE-VERIFIED AND CONFIRM, so the PARTIAL is not mistaken for a wider doubt: CobolDate#Analyze is the only body (grep of src/ for TestFormattedDatetime finds IntrinsicCatalog, IntrinsicRenderer and CobolDate alone); the RenderDec lane does NOT double-dispatch it (RenderDec's `alwaysDec` list excludes it and AnyDecOrRealRaw is false for two string arguments, so it returns null and the single native arm at IntrinsicRenderer `case "TestFormattedDatetime"` renders it at scale 0 — I checked for the two-arm shape and it is absent here); the per-digit narrowing reproduces 6 and 2 for the NOTE's DATA values under an uppercased format; §15.3.1.7's long-ISO-year condition (53 weeks iff Jan 4 is Sunday, or a leap year and Jan 4 is Saturday or Sunday) is equivalent to ISOWeek.GetWeeksInYear's rule, so LongIsoYear is right; §15.3.3.6.1 rule 3's zero-sign-implies-zero-magnitude narrowing is present and correct; Tokenize's `extended` flag (a ':' or '-' anywhere in the format) is sound because no basic §15.3 format contains either character, so §15.3.3.2's phantom decimal separator is placed correctly; and a NATIONAL argument-1/argument-2 pair survives end-to-end (NationalLiteralOperand returns a BoundStringLiteral, StrArgVisitor's `Visit(BoundStringLiteral) => EmitText.CsLiteral(n.Value)` is category-blind, so positions count one per national character).

notes:

READ, not sampled: CobolIntrinsics.TestNumval (Exact.cs:539) is a pure projection — NvScan(text, commaMode, "", false, digitCap, allowGroup:false).ErrPos — of the SAME scan the NUMVAL value path rides (Exact.cs:308), so the validator and the value function cannot disagree about what conforms. NvScan (Exact.cs:586-639) is a positional recognizer of §15.67.3 r1's TWO alternative formats, walked over the ORIGINAL string with no pre-normalization (that is what makes the reported position ordinal): leading SPACE-only run (r2's ignorable character is the space, not .NET IsWhiteSpace); format-A leading sign; spaces; digit groups with at most one decimal separator; then, only when NO leading sign was taken, a format-B trailing +/-/CR/DB in any case; then a trailing space run. ALL THREE LEGS verified. Leg a (0): every conforming shape returns new(0,...) — pinned N1 "123.45"=0, N2 " + 12 "=0 (r2's before-the-first-digit spaces), N3 "123cr"=0 (mixed-case CR), N4 "5."=0 (the 'digit [ . [digit] ]' branch), and ".5" takes the '. digit' branch. r5 (the DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA separator swap) is the commaMode parameter, fed by IntrinsicRenderer.CommaFlag (ctx.Data.DecimalPointIsComma) and unit-pinned: TestNumval("1,5", commaMode:true)=0, ("1.5", commaMode:true)=2. (1) DECISIVE — LEG (a) INCORPORATES AN ARGUMENT RULE THIS COMPILER DOES NOT IMPLEMENT. If standard-decimal arithmetic is in effect, the total number of digits in argument-1 shall not exceed 34." -> OK (§15.67.3 rule 4) — and the standard-binary half (35) is ABSENT FROM THE TREE: IntrinsicRenderer.DigitCapFlag (line 800) is two-valued, `num.StandardDecimal ? ", digitCap: 34" : ""`, so NvScan's digitCap is only ever 31 or 34 and the renderer's own comment at line 263 records the omission ("standard-binary's 35 rides the P12/P13 STANDARD-BINARY wave"). Rule 5 of this batch is explicit: a rule with two halves where one was verified => PARTIAL, always. The adjudicator routed the whole of §15.67.3 r4 to the L2.3 sibling row and left leg (a) clean; leg (a) cites the rule and so carries the gap too, and cannot read CONFORMS while its incorporated half is an open owner question.
(2) THE EVIDENCE FOR LEG (c) OVER A DATA ITEM IS OUTPUT-SHAPED AND CANNOT DISCRIMINATE. The note closes leg (c)'s "n is text.Length ... the item's FULL FIXED-WIDTH image" claim with "golden N10 uses W40 PIC X(40) VALUE ALL '1'". notes:
Citation re-derived: cite.py --check 15.93.4 "the returned value is the position of the 32nd digit if no prior error is found" -> OK (§15.93.4 rule 1, sub-note 2); its premise re-derived too — cite.py --check 15.67.3 "If native arithmetic is in effect, the total number of digits in argument-1 shall not exceed 31." -> OK (§15.67.3 rule 3). READ: NvScan line 609, `if (++digits > digitCap) return new(i + 1, true, false, 0, 0)`, with digitCap defaulting to 31 on the TestNumval signature (Exact.cs:539) and IntrinsicRenderer.DigitCapFlag (line 800) emitting NOTHING under native arithmetic, so the native call takes that default. Three things checked. (1) The reported position is the 32nd DIGIT's own character position (i is the index of the digit that pushed the count past the cap), not the count and not the string end. (2) "the total number of digits" is counted across BOTH sides of the decimal separator — the counter is incremented in the single digit arm that serves the integer and fraction parts alike. (3) "if no prior error is found" holds structurally: the cap test lives inside the digit loop, so any earlier malformation has already broken the loop or returned, and any LATER malformation is at a higher position than the digit that trips the cap — so the reported position is still the FIRST character in error under leg b. The cap is tested BEFORE the accumulator multiplies, so the value projection cannot saturate into a plausible number (the PB33/PB34 defect this ordering was written for). TESTS: intrinsics_test_validators N10 = 32 over W40 (PIC X(40) VALUE ALL "1" — the 32nd digit is at position 32); pb33_numval_family_digit_cap TEST-34 = 33 over "1234567890123456789012345.678901234", where the 32nd digit sits at character position 33 because of the decimal point — I recomputed that position independently rather than trusting the fixture's prose header, which loosely says "-> 32" while the .out's overpunched "00000003C" is 33; unit DigitCap_FollowsArithmeticMode asserts TestNumval(40 x '1') == 32. Both the boundary (31 digits = 0) and the first failing case are covered.

notes:
Citation re-derived: cite.py --check 15.93.4 "If standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, and the argument has more than 35 digits, the returned value is the position of the 36th digit" -> OK (§15.93.4 rule 1, sub-note 3). THE RULE'S PRECONDITION CAN NEVER HOLD IN THIS COMPILER. READ: DataBinder.BindDeclarations (DataBinder.cs:318-320) — `if (Options.Arithmetic == ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary) Edition.Error("COBOLNET0806", "ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is an obsolete feature (ISO §8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 / Annex F) and is not supported; use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL")` — a hard compile error, so no object program can ever run with standard-binary in effect. Correspondingly the 35-digit cap is NOWHERE in the tree: IntrinsicRenderer.DigitCapFlag (line 800) is a two-valued property, `num.StandardDecimal ?
