subject: TEST-NUMVAL-F function
notes: CITATION RE-DERIVED: `cite.py --check 15.95.3 "Argument-1 shall be an alphanumeric or national literal or a data item of class alphanumeric or national."` -> OK, §15.95.3 rule 1. CODE READ: IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified carries `["TEST-NUMVAL-F"] = Uniform('s', "§15.95.3 r1")` (line 687), screened by IntrinsicBinder.CheckArgumentClasses, which deliberately drives off the Verified table and NOT off sig.ArgKinds ("the catalog's hint column is unaudited", line 1654), calling IntrinsicArgumentRules.Violation over `Admissible('s') = [Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National]` (line 874) with the §8.3.3.6.4 GR4 candidate-set intersection. WHAT r1 EXCLUDES AND WE REJECT (verified through ClassOf1/ClassOfPlace/ClassOfCategory): class NUMERIC (a numeric literal binds BoundNumericLiteral -> CobolClass.Numeric; a PIC 9 item -> PicCategory.Numeric -> CobolClass.Numeric), class BOOLEAN (a B"..." literal carries Category Boolean, a PIC 1 item likewise), class POINTER/OBJECT, and class INDEX (ClassOfPlace's `Usage.Index` arm, which rides BEFORE the category table). WHAT r1 ADMITS AND WE ADMIT: alphanumeric literals and items, alphanumeric GROUP items (ClassOfPlace's IsGroup arm -> Alphanumeric, and a group IS a 'data item of class alphanumeric'), national literals (N"..." carries Category National) and national items, numeric-edited display items (§8.5.2.1 Table 2 puts category numeric-edited in class ALPHANUMERIC, so r1's 'class alphanumeric' reaches it — the NumericEditedDeEditing member is that class, per its own remark), and figurative constants (SPACE/ZERO present an alphanumeric or national character value, §8.3.3.6.4 GR4/GR1; the intersection test admits them, which is PB48's landed behaviour, not a hole). THE UNENFORCED HALF — CLASS ALPHABETIC. r1 names class alphanumeric or national and NOT class alphabetic, and the standard treats them as distinct: `cite.py --check 8.5.2.1 "Alphabetic"` -> OK, Table 2 row `| Alphabetic | Alphabetic |`, and `cite.py --check 15.96.3 "alphabetic, alphanumeric, or national"` -> OK, showing TRIM's r1 naming alphabetic EXPLICITLY where §15.95.3 r1 does not. This compiler cannot express the distinction at the screen: PicInfo.cs:14 documents PicCategory.Alphanumeric as "Alphanumeric (X) or alphabetic (A)", CobolClass (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:20) has no Alphabetic member, and ClassOfCategory therefore answers CobolClass.Alphanumeric for a PIC A(n) item — so `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-F(WS-ALPHA)` over `01 WS-ALPHA PIC A(10).` binds clean and runs, where r1 requires a diagnostic. This is an OVER-ACCEPT (legal source is never rejected), it is reachable at every edition the function exists in, and the datum needed to fix it already exists and is already used elsewhere (PicInfo.IsAlphabetic, PicInfo.cs:257, consulted by INITIALIZE's §14.9.20 GR5c/GR6c category matching); the 's' union is documented at IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:869-871 as a deliberate over-approximation whose narrowing was left as 'a later refinement'. PARTIAL per rule 5: the rule has an admissible half (verified correct) and an exclusion half (one class of the exclusion, ALPHABETIC, unenforced). TEST-REF EMPTY: no negative fixture in tests/conformance/negative/ names TEST-NUMVAL-F (the pb58-numvalf-numeric / pb58-numvalf-literal negatives pin NUMVAL-F's row, a different function's clause), and no unit test asserts the TEST-NUMVAL-F screen; ZeroLengthLiteralArgumentDriftTests.TheTestNumvalFamily_IsNotSweptIn only asserts the ABSENCE of a zero-length prohibition, which is not this rule. EDITIONS from kb/Work R28's external evidence, not from IntrinsicCatalog's row. REFUTED: VERDICT SURVIVES (PARTIAL) after an independent read of the model; TWO facts are added that make the ENFORCED half weaker than the note implies, and neither of them rescues a CONFORMS. CITATIONS RE-DERIVED BY ME: `--check 15.95.3 "Argument-1 shall be an alphanumeric or national literal or a data item of class alphanumeric or national."` -> OK §15.95.3 1); `--check 8.5.2.1 "Alphabetic"` -> OK, Table 2 carries its own `| Alphabetic | Alphabetic |` row, so class alphabetic is a DISTINCT class; `--check 15.96.3 "alphabetic, alphanumeric, or national"` -> OK §15.96.3 1), which is the standard naming alphabetic where it means it and §15.95.3 r1 not doing so. THE ALPHABETIC HOLE IS CONFIRMED FROM THE CODE, not from the note: CobolClass has no Alphabetic member (its own remark says the distinction 'is not recoverable here'), PicInfo's PicCategory comment reads 'Alphanumeric (X) or alphabetic (A)' for the single Alphanumeric member, ClassOfPlace ends `p.Item.Pic is { } pic ? ClassOfCategory(pic.Category) : null` and ClassOfCategory maps PicCategory.Alphanumeric -> CobolClass.Alphanumeric — so a `PIC A(10)` item presents the singleton {Alphanumeric}, intersects the 's' set `[Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National]`, and binds clean where r1 requires a diagnostic. PicInfo.IsAlphabetic (PicInfo.cs:257) exists and MoveTable16 already keys on it, so the datum is present and simply not consulted here. TWO ADDITIONS THE ADJUDICATOR DID NOT RECORD. (i) THE ENFORCED HALF IS DIALECT-CONDITIONAL: CheckArgumentClasses' local `Report` runs `if (ctx.Edition.Permissive) ctx.Edition.Warning(DiagnosticCatalog.IntrinsicArgumentClass, ...) else ctx.Edition.Error(...)`, so under `--permissive` even the exclusions that ARE modelled (numeric, boolean, pointer, index) are a warning and the coercion runs — documented dialect-gated leniency, but it means the 'verified correct' half is verified only under strict conformance. (ii) THE SCREEN FAILS OPEN wherever the class is not statically decidable: `Violation` returns null when `CandidateClasses(op).Length == 0`, and ClassOf1/ClassOfPlace/ClassOfCategory each answer null for an operand shape they do not model (an unmodelled figurative kind, a PICTURE-less place, an unlisted category) — so the rejecting half is a partial screen even inside the classes it can express. subject: TEST-NUMVAL-F function
notes: CITATION RE-DERIVED: `cite.py --check 15.95.4 "the returned value is the position of the fifth digit of the exponent"` -> OK, §15.95.4 1) b) (list item 5). CODE READ: NvfScan's exponent scan counts exponent digits in `ed` and returns at the FIFTH one — `while (i < n && char.IsAsciiDigit(text[i])) { if (++ed > 4) return new(Pos(), false, false, 0, 0, 0); ev = ev * 10 + (text[i] - '0'); i++; }`. `Pos()` is `i + 1` and `i` has NOT yet advanced when the guard fires, so the value returned is the 1-based position OF THE FIFTH EXPONENT DIGIT ITSELF, exactly as the rule states ("1E+12345" -> 8, the ordinal of the '5'). VERIFIED ACROSS THE RULE'S TWO NAMED MODES: the arm is MODE-INDEPENDENT — the 4-digit exponent bound is hardcoded, not threaded from DigitCapFlag (which carries only the SIGNIFICAND cap) — so the standard-decimal half is satisfied, and the standard-binary half would be satisfied by the same code if the mode were admitted (it is not: DataBinder.BindDeclarations rejects ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY with COBOLNET0806 at every edition, the documented non-support adjudicated on RV-15.27.3-2). I do not score that as an unverified half, because the behaviour this rule names does not vary by mode in this implementation and there is no second code path to leave unread. THE 'SIGNIFICANT DIGITS' WORDING WAS ATTACKED AND DOES NOT CHANGE THE ANSWER: on a leading-zero exponent such as "1E+00005" the code returns the fifth digit's position; if 'significant' is read strictly (one significant digit, so this rule would not fire), the base argument rule still rejects the string — `cite.py --check 15.69.3 "n is one, two, three, or four digits representing the exponent"` -> OK — and §15.95.4 1) b) then asks for 'the position of the first character in error', which is that same fifth digit because the format admits only a space-string or end-of-string after the fourth. Both readings land on the same number. ORDERING ALSO CHECKED: the scan is strictly left-to-right, so a significand error or a malformed sign returns before the exponent scan is entered, satisfying the family's 'no prior error ... has been found' precedence. TEST-REF EMPTY (rule 3): nothing in tests/ writes a five-digit exponent — IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.TestNumvalF_Positions_2014's four cases and the pb60_numval_one_scan golden's ET row all stay within one exponent digit. CONFORMS-but-untested; the row stays test-needed. EDITIONS from kb/Work R28's external evidence, not from IntrinsicCatalog's row. REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The citation re-derives (`cite.py --check 15.95.4 "the returned value is the position of the fifth digit of the exponent"` -> OK, §15.95.4 1) b), list item 5) and the arithmetic the adjudicator describes is correct as far as it goes — I re-traced `if (++ed > 4) return new(Pos(), ...)` myself: `i` has not advanced past the fifth digit when the guard fires, so `Pos() = i + 1` is that digit's own 1-based ordinal ("1E+12345" -> 8, and with the figure's optional space-strings "1E+ 12345" -> 9). The verdict still costs something on TWO grounds the adjudicator argued away rather than measured. (1) THE RULE NAMES TWO ARITHMETIC MODES AND ONLY ONE CAN EVER BE IN EFFECT HERE. The rule text is 'If standard-decimal arithmetic, OR STANDARD-BINARY ARITHMETIC is in effect ...'. I read DataBinder.BindDeclarations myself: `if (Options.Arithmetic == ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary) Edition.Error("COBOLNET0806", ...)` — a hard error at every edition, so no program this compiler translates can ever have standard-binary in effect and the standard-binary half of this rule is never satisfied by anything. The adjudicator dismissed that with 'the behaviour this rule names does not vary by mode in this implementation', which is an argument about the CODE, not about whether the rule's stated precondition can hold. The batch has already settled the shape the other way: RV-15.27.3-2, whose SOLE condition is standard-binary, was adjudicated NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION as the documented-non-support shape and explicitly NOT CONFORMS — and this batch's own RV-15.95.4-1 note concedes sub-note b.3 (the standard-binary 35-digit cap) is ABSENT. One half verified, one half unexercisable is PARTIAL by the batch rule, always. (2) AN UNVERIFIED EDGE INSIDE THE STANDARD-DECIMAL HALF — THE DIGIT COUNT AND THE SPACE RULE. §15.69.3 r5 (`--check 15.69.3 "Embedded spaces in argument-1 are ignored except between the first numeric digit and the last digit that precedes a letter 'E'"` -> OK) makes embedded spaces IGNORED everywhere outside the significand, while r1's figure draws `n` as a contiguous one-to-four-digit run with [space-string] only before and after it. Those two readings give different answers for an exponent written with an interior space, and they land squarely on THIS rule's 'more than four significant digits' count: for `TEST-NUMVAL-F("1E+1 2345")` I traced the code to 6 — the digit loop exits at the space with ed=1, the trailing-space skip advances to '2', and `if (i != n) return new(Pos(), ...)` reports it — where the r5 reading makes the exponent 12345, five digits, and this rule requires the position of its FIFTH digit, 9. The implementation resolves a normative tension silently: nothing in NvfScan, its comments, the design docs or any test records that the choice was made, and the r5 except-clause is implemented for the SIGNIFICAND (`pendingSpace`) and nowhere else. An edge on which the rule's own answer changes, resolved without evidence, is PARTIAL under the batch's cost rule. TWO THINGS I CHECKED THAT DID **NOT** MOVE THE VERDICT, recorded so they are not re-litigated: the mode-independence of the 4-digit bound is CORRECT under native, because §15.69.3 r1's 'where' clause caps n at 'one, two, three, or four digits' with no arithmetic-mode qualification, so under native the fifth digit is the first character in error under leg b) generic and the same number comes back; and the 'significant digits' wording converges on the same number for a leading-zero exponent ("1E+012345" -> the code returns the position of the fifth DIGIT of the exponent, 8, which is exactly what the rule's words say). I also re-confirmed there is no second lane to leave unread — RenderDec's `alwaysDec` list excludes TestNumvalF, its switch ends `_ => null`, and there is no compile-time intrinsic folder anywhere in the compiler. TEST-REF STAYS EMPTY: I searched tests/ myself and no test, golden or unit, writes an exponent of more than one digit to any TEST-NUMVAL-F. The row stays test-needed.

The screen is REACHED on this bespoke path: IntrinsicBinder.BindTrim calls CheckArgumentClasses(sig, operands) at line 1010 before building the node (the generic path returns earlier), and CheckArgumentClasses walks schema.At(i). Positive coverage in both admitted rows: intrinsics_trim (PIC X(10) argument-1) and pb15_result_type_follows_argument (PIC N(8) and PIC X(8) argument-1, TRIM-N=[CDE] / TRIM-X=[CDE]). Deliberate latitude recorded, NOT scored as a defect: r1 says 'a DATA ITEM', and the implementation also admits an alphanumeric/national LITERAL argument-1. That is what §15.6 Table 21 types TRIM's argument-1 as (Alph1 or Anum1 or Nat1) and what §15.3 type 2 admits ('A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric or an alphanumeric literal'), and §15.96.4's own NOTE writes TRIM("aabbcc" "c" "b") — rejecting a literal would reject the standard's own example. Editions from Annex §E.3.3 item 31 (--check OK: 'The TRIM function has been enhanced…', i.e. TRIM predates 2023) plus kb/Work R28's landed primary-source decision (WG4/J4 CD 1.2 Annex D.2 lists TRIM among the 2014 introductions); NOT derived from the IntrinsicCatalog row. REFUTED: verdict SUSTAINED — attacked on three axes and it held. notes: cite.py --check 15.96.3 'if argument-1 is class national, argument-2 is as though a national space had been specified' -> OK (r3 b). READ: CobolIntrinsics.Trim(string s, long mode, params string[] chars) opens with 'char[] set = chars.Length == 0 ? [' '] : …' — with no argument-2 the delete set is exactly one SPACE, r3's default. BOTH sub-rules land on that one line because the typed-native model stores a national item as a C# string of UTF-16 code units, one per national character position (the emitted pb15_result_type_follows_argument.g.cs shows 'private string W_NPAD = CobolString.Store("  CDE   ", 8)' for PIC N(8) and 'CobolIntrinsics.Trim(W_NPAD, 0)'), so the national space IS U+0020 and r3.b needs no separate arm — a distinct national-space constant would be the second mechanism, not a fix. Both sub-rules are exercised: r3.a by intrinsics_trim (BOTH=/LEAD=/TRAIL= over PIC X(10) "  HELLO   "), r3.b by pb15_result_type_follows_argument (MOVE FUNCTION TRIM(W-NPAD) TO W-NR over PIC N(8) N"  CDE   " → TRIM-N=[CDE]). The renderer reaches the defaulted form correctly: IntrinsicRenderer's "Trim" arm emits Intrinsic(method, Str(arg0) + ", " + TrimMode) with no chars when Args.Count == 1. Minor observation, not scored: the second guard 'if (set.Length == 0) set = [' ']' also substitutes a space when every WRITTEN argument-2 is a zero-length string — a silent fallback, but only for source r2 already forbids (a zero-length argument-2 is not 'a single character'), and it is unreachable for a static literal, which the ExactWidth(1) predicate rejects first. Editions per Annex §E.3.3 item 31 + kb/Work R28 (TRIM introduced 2014); the no-argument-2 default is the whole of 2014-era TRIM. REFUTED: CONFORMS → PARTIAL. The DEFAULT VALUE half of r3 is right and I re-confirmed the storage model in the emitted C# myself (tests/conformance/2023/pb15_result_type_follows_argument.g.cs line 15 stores PIC N(8) as an 8-char UTF-16 string padded with U+0020, line 51 calls Trim(W_NPAD, 0)) — so r3.b needing no separate national-space constant is sustained. What is NOT right is the code's test for r3's ANTECEDENT. r3 fires 'When NO argument-2 IS SPECIFIED' — a SYNTACTIC condition, decided at bind time. CobolIntrinsics.Trim decides it at RUN TIME on 'chars.Length == 0', and then a SECOND run-time test, 'if (set.Length == 0) set = [' ']', re-applies r3's default after '.Where(c => c.Length > 0)' has emptied a set built from argument-2s that WERE specified. The adjudicator's dismissal rests on a reachability claim it did not measure ('unreachable for a static literal, which the ExactWidth(1) predicate rejects first'), and that claim is only true for STATIC literals. I read PredicateViolation (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs line 939): the ExactWidth arm is guarded 'when knownWidth is { } w && w != p.N', so a NULL width falls through '_ => null' and fails OPEN; and IntrinsicBinder.KnownWidth (line 1317) returns null for 'BoundFieldOperand { Place.Item: { IsAnyLength: true } or { IsDynamicLength: true } }' and for a ref-mod whose length is not an int literal. So FUNCTION TRIM(X DYN-ITEM) over an ANY LENGTH / DYNAMIC LENGTH argument-2 currently holding the empty string binds clean, reaches the runtime with chars = [""], is filtered to an empty set, and SILENTLY TRIMS SPACES — r3's default applied where r3's antecedent is false. §15.3 rule 14 is explicit about what should happen instead (--check OK: 'If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument … the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist'); nothing here raises it. The same fallback is reached from the table(ALL) lane whenever the ALL enumerates zero elements. One half of r3 verified (the default's VALUE, by two goldens in both classes), the other half wrong on a reachable path ⇒ PARTIAL per rule 5. The fix shape is to decide r3 at BIND time — BindTrim already knows operands.Count — and let a specified-but-empty argument-2 raise EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION rather than fall back to a space.

subject: CONTINUE statement
notes: Re-read the format in specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 23190 and validated it mechanically (`cite.py --check 14.9.9.2 "CONTINUE"` -> OK, returning the whole format line). Derived expectation BEFORE reading code, from the repaired Figure-notes block: CONTINUE is a required word (the printed missing underline is the C2 typo), the bracket makes the whole phrase optional, and AFTER / SECONDS carry underline rules so they are REQUIRED inside the phrase; the operand is arithmetic-expression-1 (a full 8.8.1 arithmetic expression, not a mere identifier/literal). READ: `continueStatement : CONTINUE (AFTER arithmeticExpression SECONDS)? ;` (CobolControlFlow.g4:361-363). Token-for-token identical to the derived shape: CONTINUE mandatory (so `AFTER 5 SECONDS` alone cannot parse as a CONTINUE, the Figure-notes' second argument), the group is `( ... )?` (bracket), AFTER and SECONDS are hard tokens inside it (not `AFTER?` / `SECONDS?`), so `CONTINUE 5` is rejected. The operand nonterminal is the SHARED `arithmeticExpression` (CobolExpressions.g4:208 -> additiveExpression -> multiplicative -> power), i.e. the same 8.8.1 rule PERFORM VARYING uses, so a parenthesized/compound expression, a literal, an identifier and a function reference are all admitted -- not a narrowed operand. The grammar's own header comment (CobolControlFlow.g4:359-360) records the same page-604-vs-page-732 contradiction the Figure notes do and resolves it the same way (the defining occurrence governs), so the transcription and the grammar agree rather than one having inherited the other's typo. Wired into the single `statement` rule at CobolParserCore.g4:719. EDITION (derived from Annex E, NOT from the registry's own IntroducedIn column): Annex E.3.3 item 14 at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:43957 -- "Additional functionality added to the CONTINUE statement. The CONTINUE statement has been enhanced to provide the ability to pause runtime execution for a specified period of time" -- so the bracketed phrase is 2023-only while bare CONTINUE is 85-continuous. The compiler gates exactly that split: VersionConformancePass.VisitContinueStatement fires COBOLNET0900 only when `ctx.arithmeticExpression()` is present (Validation/VersionConformancePass.cs:584-589), i.e. on the PHRASE, never on the verb -- confirmed by 85/wavef_dbg_proc.cob and 85/index_name_r7_windows.cob compiling bare CONTINUE at --std 85. TESTED: 2023/continue_after exercises both operand forms (a literal `AFTER 0` and a data item `AFTER WS-N`); the constructs.json row `continue-after-2023` drives VersionMatrixTests.Construct_MatchesEditionExpectation and IntroducedConstruct_IsRejectedUnderPermissive, so the below-2023 rejection is asserted at 85/2002/2014 and is not waived by --permissive. NOT exercised anywhere: a COMPOUND arithmetic-expression-1 (`CONTINUE AFTER N + 1 SECONDS`); that is a shared-nonterminal reuse rather than a private parse, so it does not cost the verdict. || UPHELD (independent re-derivation): I re-ran all three cite checks myself -- `cite.py --check 14.9.9.2 "CONTINUE"` -> OK (General format), and read the format + Figure notes at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:23189-23212 before opening any code. I re-read CobolControlFlow.g4:361-363 and CobolParserCore.g4:719 directly. I additionally checked the two edges the adjudicator did not: (a) `unaryExpression : addOp unaryExpression | primaryExpression` (CobolExpressions.g4) admits a LEADING SIGN, so `CONTINUE AFTER -1 SECONDS` -- the literal spelling of the GR1a negative case -- parses, and `primaryExpression` admits numericLiteral / ZERO_ARITH / functionCall / dataReference / `( arithmeticExpression )`, so the operand really is the full 8.8.1 rule; (b) the SECONDS terminator cannot be swallowed by the operand, because `additiveExpression` stops at a non-addOp token and `dataReference` is single-word except for OF/IN qualification. subject: DISPLAY statement
notes: READ: displayStatement : DISPLAY (dataReference | literal | functionCall)+ displayUpon? displayNoAdvancing? END_DISPLAY? ; displayUpon : UPON cobolWord ; displayNoAdvancing : WITH? NO ADVANCING (CobolParserCore.g4 lines 1300-1310). FORMAT 1 MATCHES the printed diagram element for element: the '...' operand repetition is '+', UPON is optional, WITH is an OPTIONAL word (it is NOT underlined in the format, and the grammar's 'WITH?' honours that), NO/ADVANCING are required, END-DISPLAY is optional, and a function-identifier is admitted in the identifier-1 slot per 8.4.3.1.2 (the grammar comment cites it). FORMAT 2 (screen) IS ENTIRELY ABSENT: there is no screen-name-1 arm, no AT [LINE NUMBER ...] [{COLUMN|COL} NUMBER ...] phrase, and no ON EXCEPTION / NOT ON EXCEPTION pair. AT (CobolLexer.g4:411), LINE (:556) and EXCEPTION (:494) are dedicated lexer tokens and NONE of them is an alternative of cobolWord (CobolWords.g4 lines 9-120 -- COL and COLUMN are, AT/LINE/EXCEPTION are not), so 'DISPLAY SG AT LINE 5 COL 10 ON EXCEPTION ...' is a PARSE ERROR, not a mis-bind. The repaired Figure notes therefore have nothing to be compared against: the AT phrase's brace-enclosed choice indicators (one-or-more, any order) and the exception pair's bracket-enclosed indicators (zero-or-more, any order -- BOTH ON EXCEPTION and NOT ON EXCEPTION admissible on one statement, either order) are unimplemented along with the format. SECOND DEFECT, Format 1 side: END-DISPLAY is accepted at EVERY --std, 85 included. src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ReservedWords.Table.cs:151 records new("END-DISPLAY", false, true, true, true, "high", "added 2002 ...") -- R85 = false -- yet tests/version-matrix/constructs.json has no end-display-* row and VersionConformancePass has no VisitDisplayStatement (grep: only VisitAcceptStatement, which gates Constructs.EndAccept2002). So the project's own reserved-word catalog says the terminator is a 2002 introduction while the gating funnel admits it at 1985 with no diagnostic -- the ACCEPT twin at least carries a registered construct. WOULD CLOSE THE ROW: (a) the Format-2 grammar + binder + a golden, (b) an end-display-2002 construct row plus the mandatory edition-gate negative fixture at --std 85. || UPHELD (independent re-derivation): I re-read specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 23402-23433 and CobolParserCore.g4:1300-1310 and CobolWords.g4:9-120 myself. Format-1 element-for-element agreement CONFIRMED, including the two things worth naming: (i) figurativeConstant is the FIRST alternative of nonNumericLiteral (CobolExpressions.g4:499-506) which is an alternative of literal, so DISPLAY SPACE / DISPLAY ZERO bind as LITERAL operands and are not lost from the operand list; (ii) ZERO/SPACE/HIGH-VALUE are NOT alternatives of cobolWord, so the dataReference alternative (listed first) cannot steal them. Format-2 absence CONFIRMED. The keyword-omitted intrinsic reference (REPOSITORY 'FUNCTION name INTRINSIC', 8.4.3.2 SR2) is NOT an extra Format-1 gap: it arrives through the dataReference alternative and ExpressionBinder.FieldOperand resolves it (ControlFlowBinder.cs:260 states this contract). || REFUTED (method, not verdict) on the END-DISPLAY leg: the adjudicator derived the EDITION of END-DISPLAY from src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ReservedWords.Table.cs -- a catalog INSIDE the code under review, which ground rule 4 forbids as an edition source (it is the same shape as trusting a constructs.json IntroducedIn column). Re-derived independently and the CONCLUSION survives, so the verdict stands: END-DISPLAY exists in the standard only because 14.9.11.2 Format 2 gives DISPLAY the [NOT] ON EXCEPTION conditional phrases (an explicit scope terminator is meaningless for a statement with no conditional phrase), and Format 2 is the screen facility, absent from the 1985 statement; the compiler's own TWIN confirms the intended posture -- ConstructRegistry.g.cs:174 carries new("end-accept-2002", "END-ACCEPT (explicit scope terminator)", 2002, null, null, "COBOLNET0816", ...) and VersionConformancePass.cs:1362 checks it, while grep for END-DISPLAY across src/ + tests/version-matrix finds ONLY the lexer token, the grammar reference and the reserved-word row: no construct row, no Check call, no negative fixture. The DEFECT is therefore the ASYMMETRY itself (one of two twin terminators gated), which is true whatever edition number the eventual derivation assigns. FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` — so the FUNCTION keyword and the name are both required at this production, and the argument list's '(' is lexed in the dedicated FNARG mode so §8.4.3.2 SR6 ('that ( is ALWAYS the argument list') holds rather than the '(' being read as a subscript or a grouping paren. The optionality of the paren group in the grammar is deliberate (it serves the zero-argument functions) and does NOT leak into SQRT: the arity is the CATALOG's. READ, ARITY: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build line 133 — Add(new("SQRT", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "n", "Sqrt", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, true, 85)) — MinArgs = MaxArgs = 1, enforced at IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore lines 572-579: `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs)` -> COBOLNET1504 'FUNCTION SQRT takes 1 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)'. So a bare `FUNCTION SQRT` (given 0) and `FUNCTION SQRT(A B)` (given 2) are both rejected with the §15.3 citation. The FUNCTION-omitted spelling (§8.4.3.2.3 SR2, a REPOSITORY INTRINSIC declaration) is gated the same way — IntrinsicBinder.cs lines 301 and 339 both refuse to route a name written without an argument list unless sig.MinArgs == 0, which SQRT's is not. The row's IntrinsicType.Numeric matches §15.84.1's 'The type of this function is numeric'. GOLDEN: conformance:2023/pb52_intrinsic_argument_stage writes the format both ways argument-1 can be spelled (a data item, `FUNCTION SQRT(NI)`, and a literal, `FUNCTION SQRT(4)`), each pinned to 2.00 in the .out. NOT COVERED: there is no SQRT-specific arity negative fixture; the COBOLNET1504 guard is catalog-driven and generic, so a SQRT-specific one could only re-test the shared guard. subject: STANDARD-DEVIATION function
notes: Format read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.86.2: `FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION ( { argument-1 } … )` — FUNCTION and STANDARD-DEVIATION underlined (required keywords), the parenthesised list NOT bracketed (required), and the brace-ellipsis making argument-1 one-or-more. Both halves of the format located and read. HALF 1, the keyword/name/paren shape: the grammar carries no STANDARD-DEVIATION production (grep of src/Cobol.Net.Frontend for the name returns nothing) because the form is generic — CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall is `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*`, and CobolExpressions.g4#functionName admits IDENTIFIER. Checked the lexer for the hyphen hazard, since CobolLexer.g4 does carry STANDARD (:536), STANDARD_BINARY/STANDARD_DECIMAL (:264-265) and STANDARD_1/STANDARD_2 (:669-670) but no STANDARD_DEVIATION token: ANTLR maximal munch gives IDENTIFIER the full 18-character 'STANDARD-DEVIATION' over STANDARD's 8, which is the documented behavior at CobolLexer.g4:261-262 ('a bare STANDARD still lexes as STANDARD, and WC-COBOL still lexes as one IDENTIFIER'). The argument-list paren is retyped FNARG_LPAREN per §8.4.3.2.3 SR6, so the list is never read as a grouping or subscript paren. HALF 2, the one-or-more arity: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build:139 declares Add(new("STANDARD-DEVIATION", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "n", "StandardDeviation", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, true, 85)) — MinArgs 1, MaxArgs int.MaxValue, matching `{ argument-1 } …` exactly; IntrinsicBinder.cs:572-579 computes `given` and raises COBOLNET1504 'takes at least 1 argument(s)' when given < MinArgs, which catches both the bare `FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION` and the empty-parens `()` form the grammar's optional group admits. IntrinsicType.Numeric matches §15.86.1 ('The type of this function is numeric'). Closing test: tests/conformance/2023/pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.cob line 45 writes the format `FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION(2, 2, 2)`, it is registered in tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json:123, and tests/conformance/2023/pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.out line 8 pins SD=0.0 — so the format demonstrably lexes, parses and binds. The fixture is spec-derived (its header derives every line from §15.4.1 r1 and the functions' own EAEs), not a characterization or legacy-match. Editions: Annex E (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:42847 onward) carries no STANDARD-DEVIATION entry and the clause has no edition-varying content, so the batch default stands; the editions field was NOT read off IntrinsicCatalog's own IntroducedIn column.

subject: SUBSTITUTE function
notes: kb/Work PB81 (2026-08-18): FUNCTION SUBSTITUTE ( argument-1 { [ANYCASE] [FIRST | LAST] argument-2 argument-3 } … ) — the pair repeats, so §15.3's table(ALL) is admissible among the pairs and its elements form the pairs by position at run time (the FLAT form: CobolIntrinsics.SubstituteFlat pairs the enumerated elements; a keyword before an enumeration attaches to the pair its first element opens). Written pairs pair at bind as before (SubstituteModes per pair). The ALL argument was the staged COBOLNET0899 (`substitute-all-subscript-argument`, retired).

subject: SUM function
notes:
Format read directly from specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.88.2 (line 33495-33499): `FUNCTION SUM ( { argument-1 } … )` — FUNCTION and SUM underlined (required), the argument-list parentheses present, and the braced argument-1 followed by an ellipsis, i.e. ONE OR MORE. Both halves READ and verified. (1) THE REFERENCE SHAPE: CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*`, with SUM present in CobolExpressions.g4#functionName (line 458) — needed because SUM is one of the §8.9 reserved words that is also a §8.11 intrinsic name. The keyword-omitted twin `SUM(…)` rides CobolExpressions.g4#reservedIntrinsicArgFn (`SIGN | SUM`), and IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsic lines 54-63 enforces §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 on it (COBOLNET1543 unless REPOSITORY declares SUM / FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC) — so the abbreviated form is not accepted unconditionally. Arguments juxtapose or take the §8.3.5 separator via functionArgList. §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 is decided from the DEFINITION before binding (DefinitionPermitsArguments("SUM") is true since MaxArgs > 0), so `FUNCTION SUM (1:4)` draws Sr6ArgumentListError, not a bogus arity error; §8.4.3.3.3 SR2 rejects reference-modifying SUM's numeric result (ResultRefMod, COBOLNET1629). (2) THE 1..n MULTIPLICITY: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build line 152 `Add(new("SUM", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "n", "SumScaled", …))` — MinArgs 1, MaxArgs int.MaxValue; IntrinsicBinder.cs line 573 raises COBOLNET1504 ("takes at least 1 argument(s); 0 given (ISO §15.3)") for `FUNCTION SUM` written with no list or an empty one, and the unbounded max means no upper rejection. The ellipsis also licenses the §15.3 table(ALL) argument: IntrinsicSig.RepeatsAnArgument (MaxArgs == int.MaxValue) gates TryBindAllArgument, and its own diagnostic text names SUM as an example of a `{ argument } …` format. TESTS: tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/IntrinsicRepeatedArgumentDriftTests.cs re-reads §15.88.2's `<pre>` block out of specs/ISO_COBOL.md and asserts the catalog's unboundedness EQUALS the presence of the '…' character — spec-derived in the strict sense (the assertion's oracle is the standard's own text, not a hand list). tests/conformance/2023/pb62_all_subscript_runtime_ranges.cob exercises the repeated-argument format over ALL (fixed, ODO, dynamic-capacity, two-level, and a mixed `SUM(F(ALL) WS-E(ALL))`); pb58_argument_predicates_legal.cob exercises the plain 3-argument written form. NOT covered by a dedicated fixture: a zero-argument `FUNCTION SUM` negative case — the COBOLNET1504 arm was read in source but has no SUM-specific golden; that is a test gap, not a behavior gap (the arm is shared and exercised by other MinArgs rows).

REFUTER (verdict SUSTAINED after independent attack): the format was re-read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33494-33499 and §8.4.3.2.3 re-read whole at :6020ff. SR2 ("If intrinsic-function-name-1 or the ALL phrase is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph … the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier; otherwise the word FUNCTION is required") and SR6 ("If a function's definition permits arguments and a left parenthesis immediately follows … the left parenthesis is always treated as the left parenthesis of that function's arguments") both check out against IntrinsicBinder.cs:57 (COBOLNET1543) and :88 (Sr6ArgumentListError, via DefinitionPermitsArguments reading MaxArgs > 0 from the catalog row). The keyword-omitted alternative `reservedIntrinsicArgFn subscriptPart refModPart*` (CobolExpressions.g4:334-346) REQUIRES the subscript group, so a bare `SUM` can never be read as a function reference — which is correct precisely because §15.88.2 has no zero-argument form, and is what keeps the report-writer `SUM OF` clause and the `SIGN` data-description clause from being swallowed. The drift test was read in full and is genuinely spec-derived: it re-scans every `#### 15.x.2 General format` block out of specs/ISO_COBOL.md, keys on the '…' character, asserts a ≥79-row floor on BOTH the spec scan and the catalog scan so the scanner cannot silently find nothing, and asserts the equivalence in both directions — it closes the UNBOUNDED half of `{ argument-1 } …`. The at-least-one half rests on reading only (IntrinsicBinder.cs:573, MinArgs 1) with no SUM-specific fixture, which rule 3 expressly permits for CONFORMS. ONE RESIDUE FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT COUNTED AGAINST THIS ROW: with a runtime-ranged table(ALL) the compile-time count is `all.StaticCount ?? 1` (IntrinsicBinder.cs:572), so an OCCURS DEPENDING object of 0 satisfies MinArgs at compile time and the enumerated list reaches the runtime EMPTY — CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs#SumDec would then throw IndexOutOfRangeException on `xs[0]` and CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SumScaled would return 0. §15.3 makes exactly that case undefined ("The evaluation of an ALL subscript shall result in at least one argument, otherwise the result of the reference to the function-identifier is undefined"), so it is not a violation of this format rule; it is worth a robustness note elsewhere, not a downgrade here. Verdict held at CONFORMS.

subject: TAN function
notes: The general format is `FUNCTION TAN ( argument-1 )` — FUNCTION and TAN underlined (required words), exactly one argument, parentheses required (no bracketed no-argument form, unlike §15.75.2 RANDOM). Read the rendered clause at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33537–33541 directly rather than trusting the input's escaped <pre>. FOUR FORMAT FACTS VERIFIED. (1) THE SHAPE PARSES: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4:333 `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart* | …`. TAN is not a §8.9 reserved word (the reservedIntrinsicArgFn arm is exactly SIGN and SUM; §8.9 ∩ §8.11 is four words), so TAN reaches the binder through functionName with no keyword collision, and the '(' is retyped FNARG_LPAREN by the lexer's _fnParenStack per §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 — which is what keeps ZeroTokenRewriter from converting a figurative argument into arithmetic (PB48). (2) EXACTLY ONE ARGUMENT IS ENFORCED: IntrinsicCatalog.cs:132 `Add(new("TAN", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "n", "Tan", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, true, 85))` — MinArgs = MaxArgs = 1, checked at IntrinsicBinder.cs:573–579, which emits COBOLNET1504 "FUNCTION TAN takes 1 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)" and returns BoundExprError. So `FUNCTION TAN(A B)` and `FUNCTION TAN()` are both rejected, and a bare `FUNCTION TAN` with no parenthesised group binds args = [] => given 0 < 1 => the same diagnostic, which is how the format's REQUIRED parentheses are enforced (the grammar makes the group optional because §15.75.2 RANDOM needs the bare form; the catalog's MinArgs is the discriminator). (3) THE FORMAT ADMITS NO REFERENCE MODIFICATION and TAN's result is numeric (IntrinsicType.Numeric => ResultCategory Numeric via IntrinsicSig.CategoryOf): `FUNCTION TAN(1)(1:2)` is rejected at IntrinsicBinder.cs:178–186, DiagnosticCatalog.RefModFunctionResultClass, which admits only Alphanumeric/National/Boolean per §8.4.3.3.3 SR2. And `FUNCTION TAN (1:4)` — a bare ref-mod where the argument list belongs — is caught as an SR6 argument-list error (IntrinsicBinder.cs:318, guarded by DefinitionPermitsArguments, which is `sig.MaxArgs > 0` at line 109; TAN's MaxArgs is 1, so it qualifies). (4) THE OMISSIBILITY OF THE UNDERLINED WORD FUNCTION is the §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 grant, and it is implemented and correctly GATED: the keyword-omitted `TAN(x)` form arrives as a dataReference and is re-routed by KeywordOmittedFunction (IntrinsicBinder.cs:213–242), with the binder rejecting the omission unless the REPOSITORY names the intrinsic (the diagnostic at line 61 quotes SR2). MISSING: no spec-derived test writes `FUNCTION TAN` at all. The only corpus occurrences are tests/nist/programs/IF139A.cob (20 calls), which is a nist: reference and does not qualify as a closing test-ref; no tests/conformance golden or negative fixture mentions TAN. Row stays test-needed. Editions: batch default, no format delta across the four editions (§15.89.2 carries no edition-conditional syntax and TAN is unchanged from the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment through 2023). || REFUTER UPHELD (independent re-derivation, verdict unchanged). The format was read from specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33539–33541 myself, not from the input record's escaped <pre>: `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TAN</u> ( argument-1 )` — both words underlined, one argument, no brackets anywhere, so no optional part exists to under- or over-implement. The four facts re-checked at source. (1) g4:332–347 read in full: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart* | reservedIntrinsicArgFn subscriptPart refModPart* | RANDOM subscriptPart? refModPart*` and `reservedIntrinsicArgFn : SIGN | SUM` — confirming TAN takes the first alternative only. (2) The §15.3 type-10 ARGUMENT SHAPE the format's `argument-1` stands for is admitted: `functionArgument : fnArgPhraseWord | OMITTED | {boolArgAhead()}? booleanExpression | nonNumericLiteral | arithmeticExpression` (g4:366–372), so `FUNCTION TAN(A + B)` parses through the arithmeticExpression arm — the format is not silently narrowed to a bare identifier, which was the shape most likely to be wrong and was the specific thing the adjudicator's note did not name. (3) §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 re-derived rather than inherited: `cite.py --check 8.4.3.2.3 "The word FUNCTION may be omitted"` => OK §8.4.3.2.3 2), text "If intrinsic-function-name-1 or the ALL phrase is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph or if function-prototype-name-1 or function-pointer-name-1 is specified, the word FUNCTION may be omitted…" — the adjudicator's paraphrase is accurate, and KeywordOmittedFunction gates it on `DialectLevel < 2002 => null` plus RepositoryAllIntrinsic/RepositoryIntrinsics, with COBOLNET1543 (quoting SR2) on the undeclared case, so the omission is neither missing nor ungated. (4) The ALL-subscript shape the format cannot carry is rejected, not mis-emitted: RenderFloat would build `Tan(new double[]{…})` (a CS1503 on the generated C#) if an ALL argument ever reached it, but TryBindAllArgument (IntrinsicBinder.cs:2578) reports DiagnosticCatalog.AllSubscriptNotRepeatable for any `sig.RepeatsAnArgument == false` function and TAN's MaxArgs is 1, so `FUNCTION TAN(TBL(ALL))` is a bind-time rejection and the emitter arm is unreachable. Verdict CONFORMS upheld; test-ref stays empty (the IF139A.cob occurrences are nist: and excluded by rule 3) and the row stays test-needed.

FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` with `functionName : IDENTIFIER | DISPLAY | LENGTH | MERGE | NATIONAL | BIT | RANDOM | SIGN | SORT | SUM` — TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD is not a reserved word so it lexes IDENTIFIER and the format parses; the lexer's FUNCTION suppression keeps the '(' in the argument region (SR6) so 20240229 is an argument, not a subscript. subject: TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes:
THE FORMAT READ OFF THE PRINTED CLAUSE (specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.92.2, lines 33665-33668): `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME ( argument-1 argument-2)`. FUNCTION and the function-name are UNDERLINED, so both are required key words; the two argument operands are unbracketed and carry no ellipsis, so exactly two arguments, both required, and no repetition (feedback_underlining_not_bracketing — I measured the <u> markup, I did not infer from brackets).

GENERIC HALF — the keyword/name/parenthesised-list shape. Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart* | ...` and `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*`. The separator rule is what matters for THIS format: it admits BOTH the bare juxtaposition §15.92.2 itself prints and the §8.3.5 comma separator, and the corpus exercises both spellings (below). TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME is not a §8.9 reserved word, so it arrives through the ordinary functionName/cobolWord slot; hyphens are COBOL-word characters, so the name lexes whole.

subject: TEST-NUMVAL-C function
notes:
DIAGRAM RE-DERIVED FROM THE PRINTED PAGE, not the OCR. scripts/render-spec-page.py 958 (PDF p958 = printed folio 928) shows `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-C ( argument-1 [stack] [ ANYCASE ] )` where the stack glyphs are SQUARE brackets (square corners, not curly), upper leg `LOCALE [ locale-name-1 ]`, lower leg `argument-2`; underlined (required) words are FUNCTION, TEST-NUMVAL-C, LOCALE, ANYCASE. cite.py --check 15.94.2 "LOCALE</u> [ locale-name-1 ]" and --check 15.94.2 "ANYCASE" both OK; the transcription at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33756-33760 is faithful. Per §5.2.6.2 (checked: "Brackets, [ ], enclosing a portion of a general format indicate that the syntax element contained within the brackets or one of the alternatives contained within the brackets may be explicitly specified or that portion of the general format may be omitted") the stack is OPTIONAL and its two legs are ALTERNATIVES — so the eight legal shapes are arg1 | arg1 ANYCASE | arg1 arg2 | arg1 arg2 ANYCASE | arg1 LOCALE | arg1 LOCALE ANYCASE | arg1 LOCALE loc-name | arg1 LOCALE loc-name ANYCASE.
IMPLEMENTATION READ END TO END (not sampled). Parse: LOCALE and ANYCASE are NOT lexer tokens (grepped every .g4 — no LOCALE/ANYCASE lexer rule; CobolData.g4:367 states the choice outright), so both arrive through CobolExpressions.g4#functionArgument's arithmeticExpression->dataReference arm as bare words and are recognised BY NAME by IntrinsicBinder.cs#KeywordWordOf (fnArgPhraseWord, else a sole dataReference with no suffix). Dispatch: IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsic line 557 routes NUMVAL-C/TEST-NUMVAL-C to BindNumvalCFamily BEFORE the generic MinArgs/MaxArgs screen (line 573), so the catalog row's 1..2 does not miscount the keywords — the bespoke arm owns arity. BindNumvalCFamily is a POSITIONAL walk: slot 0 always binds as argument-1 (`at > 0` guards both keyword arms, so §8.10 context-sensitivity is preserved and a leading ANYCASE/LOCALE binds as an operand and fails name resolution); ANYCASE admitted once (repeat -> COBOLNET1504) and LAST (any argument after it -> COBOLNET1504, and because that check precedes the LOCALE arm, `LOCALE` after ANYCASE is rejected too); the LOCALE arm sets LocaleWritten, runs the Constructs.NumvalCLocalePhrase2002 gate, and consumes the NEXT word as locale-name-1 only when it is not ANYCASE (line 1552 — so `arg1 LOCALE ANYCASE` does not swallow ANYCASE as a locale-name), resolving it through DataBinder.ResolveLocaleName (COBOLNET1664 when undeclared). The bracketed stack's mutual exclusion is enforced at line 1564: LocaleWritten with more than one operand -> COBOLNET1504 "argument-2 and the LOCALE keyword are alternatives" citing §15.94.2/§5.2.6.2. Operand count outside 1..2 -> COBOLNET1504 (so a bare `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-C` with no argument list, which the grammar's optional FNARG_LPAREN group admits, is rejected at 0 operands). Both bound shapes RENDER: CodeGen/Emit/IntrinsicRenderer.cs case "TestNumvalC" branches on ic.LocaleWritten to TestNumvalCLocale(text, localeTag, anycase:, digitCap:) vs TestNumvalC(text, currency, commaMode:, anycase:, digitCap:) — every optional flag is passed as a NAMED argument (AnycaseFlag/DigitCapFlag/CommaFlag at lines 792-800), so an omitted flag cannot slide into the next positional slot; LocaleTagArg emits `null` for the bare-LOCALE LocaleRef.Current and a C# literal for a named locale. TestNumvalC is absent from RenderDec's alwaysDec list and takes no numeric operand, so AnyDecOrRealRaw returns null there and the native arm (which already carries digitCap: 34 under standard-decimal) is the ONE renderer — no second lane to drift.
TESTS. Spec-derived goldens exercise five of the eight shapes for TEST-NUMVAL-C itself: tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_test_validators.cob lines 78-99 (arg1 alone, §15.68.3 r3 default '$' injected), 102 (arg1 arg2), 105 (arg1 arg2 ANYCASE); tests/conformance/2002/pb64t6_numvalc_locale.cob lines 42/44 (arg1 LOCALE) and 46 (arg1 LOCALE locale-name-1). Both are ENABLED in tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json and both have .out goldens. tests/conformance/negative/locale_keyword_a49.cob pins `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-C("12" LOCALE LOC1)` parsing as the LOCALE leg (it draws COBOLNET1664 for the undeclared name, not a form error). NOT yet written for TEST-NUMVAL-C: `arg1 ANYCASE` with no argument-2, `arg1 LOCALE ANYCASE`, `arg1 LOCALE loc-name ANYCASE` (NUMVAL-C covers the last shape at pb64t6 line 40 through the SAME binder and the same named-argument renderer arms); the format-violation negatives (repeated ANYCASE, argument after ANYCASE, argument-2 together with LOCALE) exist only for NUMVAL-C (tests/conformance/negative/pb60-numvalc-anycase-position.cob). Those are TEST-GAPS, not behaviour gaps — each was traced through the code above — so the verdict is CONFORMS with the row still owed the three missing positive shapes and a TEST-NUMVAL-C-named stack-exclusion negative.
EDITIONS. Left at the batch default deliberately. The 2023 text carries NO introduction record for this function: §8.11's intrinsic-name list (spec line ~9706) has no edition column, Annex A.4.9 item 12 ("TEST-NUMVAL-C function, LOCALE keyword and locale-name-1 (15.94)") classifies the LOCALE keyword as an optional-module feature rather than dating it, and Annex E covers only 2014->2023 where the sole related entry is E.3.3 item 1, "The ANYCASE keyword of the NUMVAL-C function has been clarified", classed NOT AFFECTING — i.e. no 2014->2023 delta to this format. The compiler's own 2002 floor (IntrinsicCatalog row + tests/conformance/negative/test_validators_below_2002.cob) and the sibling inventory row FMT-15.68.2's "2002,2014,2023" were both DISREGARDED as sources under batch rule 4 (never derive editions from the code under review); if the owner wants the 2002 floor recorded here it needs a non-code derivation.
ONE STALE COMMENT FOUND (documentation only, no behaviour effect): IntrinsicBinder.cs lines 555-556 still read "The LOCALE phrase is the A.4.9 documented non-support (decision 3 - the P11 Step-8 disposition)", contradicting the live T6 LOCALE arm 1000 lines below in the same file and the accurate note at lines 506-510.
REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Citation re-derived independently: cite.py --check 15.94.2 "LOCALE</u> [ locale-name-1 ]" OK and --check 15.94.2 "ANYCASE" OK; the PRINTED page was re-rendered myself (scripts/render-spec-page.py 958 -> E:\Temp\spec_p958.png, printed folio 928) and the diagram is SQUARE-bracketed exactly as transcribed - FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-C ( argument-1 [ LOCALE [locale-name-1] / argument-2 ] [ ANYCASE ] ), underlined = FUNCTION, TEST-NUMVAL-C, LOCALE, ANYCASE. cite.py --check 5.2.6.2 "Brackets, [ ], enclosing a portion of a general format" OK. So the eight-shape reading is correct and I confirm it.

I ALSO CONFIRM, by independent reading rather than by trusting the adjudicator: (a) LOCALE/ANYCASE are not lexer tokens - Generated/CobolLexer.cs:440/459 lists 'LEADING' and 'TRAILING' as literal token names and the vocabulary jumps 'LESS','LINE','LINES','LOCATION' with NO 'LOCALE' and no 'ANYCASE' anywhere; (b) the dispatch at IntrinsicBinder.cs:557 does precede the generic MinArgs/MaxArgs screen at :573; (c) all eight shapes trace correctly through the positional walk, including the three the adjudicator left untested (arg1 ANYCASE; arg1 LOCALE ANYCASE - line 1552's `lname != "ANYCASE"` guard stops the locale-name consumption; arg1 LOCALE loc-name ANYCASE - the `at++` then the loop's `at++` land on the ANYCASE slot); (d) there is genuinely ONE render lane - RenderDec's alwaysDec list (IntrinsicRenderer.cs:643-645) omits TestNumvalC and AnyDecOrRealRaw is false for it because NumericRenderer.Visit(BoundStringLiteral) (NumericRenderer.cs:210) returns a plain non-Dec non-Real NumX and EmitCore.LoudValue (EmitCore.cs:89) is a pure string builder with no diagnostic side effect, so no spurious error under --arithmetic standard-decimal either; (e) CommaFlag/AnycaseFlag/DigitCapFlag (IntrinsicRenderer.cs:792/796/800) really are NAMED arguments (", commaMode: true" / ", anycase: true" / ", digitCap: 34"), so no positional slide; (f) BOTH runtime bodies honour ANYCASE - CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs:592 (`cmp = anycase ? OrdinalIgnoreCase : Ordinal`) and CobolIntrinsics.NumvalLocale.cs:95/194/257 (the TextInfo fold at the currency-comparison site). The two-arm-dispatch and one-of-two-bodies hazards are therefore NOT the defect here.

THE DEFECT IS THE >>COBOL-WORDS INTERACTION, AND IT IS BOTH DIRECTIONS OF THIS FORMAT'S TWO KEYWORDS.
Spec: cite.py --check 8.9 "ANYCASE" OK and --check 8.9 "LOCALE" OK - BOTH ARE §8.9 RESERVED WORDS (and I checked the §8.10 table mechanically: neither ANYCASE nor LOCALE appears in it). §7.3.10.3 SR3 (--check OK): "The content of literal-1, literal-3, and literal-4 shall be a reserved word, a context-sensitive word, or an intrinsic function name" - so both words are legal operands of the directive. §7.3.10.4 GR2 (--check OK): an EQUATEd literal-2 "may be used in any syntax requiring the use of the reserved word". §7.3.10.4 GR4 (--check OK): a SUBSTITUTEd literal-5 "shall be used in any syntax where the COBOL word that is the content of literal-4 is documented as required or optional", and literal-4 "shall no longer be a reserved word". §7.3.10.4 GR3 (--check OK): an UNDEFINEd literal-3 "shall no longer be reserved or restricted in any way" and its syntax "shall not be available". §15.94.2 IS such a syntax: it documents LOCALE and ANYCASE as its keywords.
MECHANISM, read end to end and NOT deduced: CobolWordsRewriter.Rewrite (src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Parsing/CobolWordsRewriter.cs:50) installs a synonym ONLY when `CobolKeywordTokens.TryTokenType(canonical, out kt)` succeeds, and DeReservedTokenTypes (:30-37) is guarded the same way; TryTokenType (CobolKeywordTokens.cs:42) is a lookup into a map built ONLY from the ANTLR lexer's literal token names (:20-37). Its own summary asserts "Every reserved word and context-sensitive word is a literal lexer token" - and that invariant is FALSE for LOCALE and ANYCASE (evidence (a) above). So no retype happens for either word. IntrinsicBinder.BindNumvalCFamily then recognises them by RAW TEXT only - KeywordWordOf (:2516) uppercases the word and lines 1527/1547 compare `== "ANYCASE"` / `== "LOCALE"` literally - and never consults `ctx.CobolWords`, although the very same file DOES consult it for the FUNCTION NAME (BindIntrinsicCore :446-448, DeReserved + Synonyms). ONE RULE, TWO PLACES.
CONSEQUENCES on legal source, both reachable because the directive is ACCEPTED: VersionConformancePass IsExistingWordCategory (:138-139) passes SR3 via the `ReservedWords.Find(w)` fallback, and tests/version-matrix/reserved-words.json carries {"word":"LOCALE",r85:false,r2002:true,...} and the same row for ANYCASE - so `>>COBOL-WORDS EQUATE "LOCALE" WITH "LOCALITY"` compiles clean and is then SILENTLY INERT. (1) REJECTS LEGAL SOURCE: `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-C(X LOCALITY FR)` binds LOCALITY and FR as OPERANDS, so line 1572's `operands.Count is < 1 or > 2` fires COBOLNET1504 - an arity error naming the very keyword the program legally renamed. (2) SILENT WRONG ANSWER: `>>COBOL-WORDS UNDEFINE "ANYCASE"` (GR3) or `SUBSTITUTE "ANYCASE" BY "IGNORE-CASE"` (GR4) makes ANYCASE a user-defined word and withdraws the ANYCASE syntax; `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-C(X ANYCASE)` where ANYCASE is now the user's currency data item is STILL eaten as the keyword at line 1527 - the compiler turns on case-insensitive currency matching and injects the compilation-unit currency (line 1619) instead of using the named item as argument-2, with NO diagnostic. THE ASYMMETRY IS PROVABLE IN ONE COMPILER: TRIM's LEADING/TRAILING (§15.96.2) ARE lexer tokens (CobolExpressions.g4#fnArgPhraseWord; CobolLexer.cs:440/459), so >>COBOL-WORDS IS honoured for that format's phrase words and is NOT honoured for this one. Not a landed item: the only kb/Work note mentioning COBOL-WORDS is R05 (word-length ceiling), unrelated.

TWO SECONDARY CORRECTIONS TO THE ADJUDICATOR'S REASONING.
(i) "§8.10 context-sensitivity is preserved" is a REAL CLAUSE ANSWERING A DIFFERENT QUESTION. ANYCASE and LOCALE are NOT §8.10 context-sensitive words (checked the table mechanically - absent); they are §8.9 RESERVED words (--check OK on both). What justifies the `at > 0` guard is the POSITIONAL format, not §8.10; and because they are reserved, `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-C(ANYCASE)` is a §8.9 violation, yet the compiler reports only an undefined-data-name (VersionConformancePass.IsBareFunctionArgumentWord :1857-1871 EXEMPTS every bare function-argument word from the COBOLNET0901 funnel). Rejected either way, so this is diagnostic quality, not a second verdict - but the premise the CONFORMS rested on was wrong.
(ii) EDITIONS CORRECTED 85,2002,2014,2023 -> 2002,2014,2023. Batch rule 4 blesses the default only "for a rule with no edition delta", and this format HAS one, derivable without touching the code under review: §8.9 of the 2023 text reserves ANYCASE and LOCALE, and tests/version-matrix/reserved-words.json (a version-matrix artifact, not IntrinsicCatalog) records r85:false / r2002:true for BOTH with confidence "high" - a format whose two keywords are not COBOL-85 words cannot be COBOL-85 syntax (ISO 1989:1985 carries no intrinsic functions at all; the 42-function set arrived with the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module and does not contain TEST-NUMVAL-C). Annex E covers only 2014->2023 and its one related entry, E.3.3 item 1, says the NUMVAL-C ANYCASE keyword was "clarified", i.e. it pre-dates 2023 - so 2014 and 2023 are certain and 2002 is the same value the sibling FMT-15.68.2 row carries. The 2002-vs-2014 boundary for the ANYCASE keyword itself is NOT derivable from the 2023 text alone and remains an owner question if it ever matters.

TEST-REF KEPT AS WRITTEN (all three are spec-derived conformance fixtures with goldens/.err and all three are enabled), but it does NOT close the row: it exercises five of eight shapes for TEST-NUMVAL-C (arg1 / arg1 arg2 / arg1 arg2 ANYCASE at intrinsics_test_validators.cob:78-105; arg1 LOCALE and arg1 LOCALE locale-name-1 at pb64t6_numvalc_locale.cob:42/44/46), no fixture names TEST-NUMVAL-C for the format-violation negatives (they exist only for NUMVAL-C, negative/pb60-numvalc-anycase-position.cob), and NOTHING anywhere exercises >>COBOL-WORDS against either keyword of any function. Owed by this row: the three missing positive shapes, a TEST-NUMVAL-C-named stack-exclusion negative, and - once the defect is fixed - a positive golden for an EQUATEd LOCALE/ANYCASE synonym plus a negative for the UNDEFINEd spelling.

The stale comment the adjudicator found at IntrinsicBinder.cs:555-556 is real and I confirm it; it remains documentation-only. Adjacent gap, NOT this row's (§15.94.4 r1b sub-note 3, not §15.94.2): IntrinsicRenderer.DigitCapFlag (:800) is `num.StandardDecimal ? ", digitCap: 34" : ""`, so under STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic the cap stays 31 where the rule requires the 36th digit - the runtime comment at CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs:534 admits the deferral in writing.

FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` in src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4 — TEST-NUMVAL-F is not a reserved word (it is not in the four-word §8.9 n §8.11 set SIGN/SUM/LENGTH/RANDOM), so it arrives through `functionName` and the FNARG_LPAREN retyping makes the '(' the argument list per §8.4.3.2.3 SR6; (2) the ARITY is the catalog row's, `Add(new("TEST-NUMVAL-F", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "s", "TestNumvalF", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2002))` inside IntrinsicCatalog.Build; (3) it is ENFORCED at IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore — `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs)` raises COBOLNET1504 "FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-F takes 1 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)". subject: VARIANCE function
notes: Rule text re-derived from specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 33974: `FUNCTION VARIANCE ( { argument-1 } ... )` -- FUNCTION and VARIANCE underlined (required), the parenthesised list not bracketed (required), the braced argument-1 followed by an ellipsis (one or more, repeatable). Each element located: (1) the surface shape is the shared Frontend rule src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall -- `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` -- with functionArgList = `functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*`, so space- and comma/semicolon-separated repeats both parse; VARIANCE is not in reservedIntrinsicArgFn (only SIGN and SUM are) so it takes the generic FUNCTION-keyword arm. (2) The VARIANCE-specific half is the catalog row read at IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 140: Add(new("VARIANCE", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "n", "Variance", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, true, 85)) -- MinArgs 1, MaxArgs int.MaxValue. (3) That bound is ENFORCED, not decorative: IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore lines 572-579 compute `given` (a table(ALL) argument counted as its static element count) and raise COBOLNET1504 "takes at least 1 argument(s)" outside [MinArgs, MaxArgs], so the format's minimum-one is a real rejection. (4) The ellipsis itself is mechanically pinned: IntrinsicSig.RepeatsAnArgument (IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 69) is `MaxArgs == int.MaxValue`, and IntrinsicRepeatedArgumentDriftTests.RepeatsAnArgument_IsExactly_TheFormatsEllipsis READS specs/ISO_COBOL.md, extracts the '#### 15.98.2 General format' block and asserts the catalog row agrees with whether that block contains a literal ellipsis -- a genuinely spec-derived test covering VARIANCE (it iterates every catalogued row, floor >= 79). RepeatsAnArgument is also the ISO 15.3 precondition that admits the ALL subscript, and both render lanes consume the enumerated list as one array (IntrinsicRenderer.cs#ArgArray via DecArgList line 517 and the RenderFloat default arm line 403), so `FUNCTION VARIANCE(TBL(ALL))` is structurally supported. Positive exercise of the written format: tests/conformance/2023/pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.cob line 39, `COMPUTE VA = FUNCTION VARIANCE(1, 2, 3)`, registered enabled in tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json line 123. Editions: Annex E (spec lines 42847-44200) carries NO VARIANCE or STANDARD-DEVIATION entry, so there is no edition delta; VARIANCE is in the section 8.11 intrinsic-function-name list (spec line 9710) and is an original Intrinsic Function Module name -- editions left at the batch default, NOT read off the catalog row's IntroducedIn. NOT tested for VARIANCE specifically: the table(ALL) form (pb62_all_subscript_runtime_ranges does not name VARIANCE) and the zero-argument rejection. || REFUTER (independently re-derived; verdict UPHELD as CONFORMS). Format re-read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 33974 -- FUNCTION and VARIANCE underlined, list unbracketed, `{ argument-1 } ...`. Grammar confirmed at CobolExpressions.g4 line 333 (functionCall) and lines 351-353 (functionArgList); reservedIntrinsicArgFn at line 343 is SIGN and SUM only, so VARIANCE takes the FUNCTION-keyword arm as claimed. The argument-less shape genuinely reaches the arity gate rather than a zero-argument path: BindIntrinsic line 89 calls BindIntrinsicCore(name, ArgsOf(fc.functionArgList())) and ArgsOf returns [] when the optional paren group is absent, so `FUNCTION VARIANCE` draws COBOLNET1504 -- and the section 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 pre-check at line 87 only diverts a `NAME (start:length)` shape. TWO ATTACKS TRIED AND DEFEATED. (i) Reference modification of a NUMERIC function result -- the general format shows none and the grammar's `refModPart*` admits the tokens -- is rejected: IntrinsicBinder.cs#ResultRefMod lines 180-185 admits only ResultCategory Alphanumeric/National/Boolean and reports COBOLNET1629 citing section 8.4.3.3.3 SR2, so `FUNCTION VARIANCE(1 2 3)(1:2)` is loud. (ii) The grammar's OMITTED alternative inside functionArgument is not a hole in the format: IntrinsicBinder.cs lines 2452-2456 report COBOLNET1544 citing section 8.4.3.2 SR7. The ellipsis's real consequence (the section 15.3 ALL subscript) is generic and driven by sig.RepeatsAnArgument at TryBindAllArgument line 2578, the element enumerates row-major in CobolTable.cs#AllArgs, and the zero-occurrence case that section 15.3 leaves undefined is defined LOUD there (EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION + CobolFatalException, lines 130-135) -- so no VARIANCE body can be entered with an empty list today. Editions re-checked independently: a scan of the Annex E range finds no VARIANCE or STANDARD-DEVIATION row, so the batch default stands and agrees with the landed sibling rows FMT-15.62.2 and FMT-15.74.2. ONE DRIFT RISK RECORDED, NOT A DEFECT: the drift test pins only the MAX half of the format (MaxArgs unbounded <-> the ellipsis); nothing mechanical holds MinArgs against the format's BRACES, so a catalog edit to MinArgs 0 would leave every test named here green.

subject: WHEN-COMPILED function
notes: cite.py --check 15.99.2 "WHEN-COMPILED" => OK §15.99.2 (General format), rendering exactly `FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED` with both words underlined and NO parenthesised part at all; cite.py --check 15.99.1 "The type of this function is alphanumeric." => OK. THE FORMAT IS DECLARED AND ENFORCED. IntrinsicCatalog.cs:170 carries `Add(new("WHEN-COMPILED", IntrinsicType.Alphanumeric, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 0, 0, "", "WhenCompiled", IntrinsicBind.Fold, false, 85))` - Fixed arity with MinArgs=MaxArgs=0 and an EMPTY ArgKinds string, which is the format diagram transcribed. FOUR REFERENCE SHAPES TRACED, all in Binding/Procedure/Verbs/IntrinsicBinder.cs: (a) `FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED` with no suffix - BindIntrinsic reaches BindIntrinsicCore with an empty argument list and the arity gate at line 573 passes (0 in 0..0); (b) `FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED(x)` - the same gate reports COBOLNET1504 "FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED takes 0 argument(s); 1 given (ISO §15.3)" and returns BoundExprError, so an argument list is rejected rather than ignored; (c) the keyword-omitted bare name (§8.4.3.2.3 SR2) - KeywordOmittedFunction line 339 admits a bare catalogued name only when `sig.MinArgs == 0`, which WHEN-COMPILED satisfies (the comment at line 335 names it explicitly alongside CURRENT-DATE/PI/E), gated on REPOSITORY declaring the function; (d) `FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED (1:4)` - a depth-0 colon in the captured group routes to ResultRefMod (§8.4.3.3.3 SR2, result reference modification) instead of being read as an argument list, and DefinitionPermitsArguments (line 109, `sig.MaxArgs > 0`) is false so the SR6 arm cannot misfire. The §15.3 class screen agrees with the catalog: IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:722 `["WHEN-COMPILED"] = Uniform(' ', "§15.99.2 - no arguments")`, present (per the comment at line 715) so the drift test holds the table and the catalog in agreement. TEST: IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.WhenCompiled_CompileTimeConstant_PinnedToSpec (tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs:294-303) is spec-pinned, not a legacy differential - it calls AssertSpec (compile + run under CobolNetCompiler and Assert.Equal on the expected output), never AssertSameAsLegacy - and writes `MOVE FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED TO T` plus `IF FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE >= FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED`, so the keyword form with no argument list is exercised in both a MOVE sending field and a relation-condition operand. WHAT IS MISSING (does not change the verdict): the NEGATIVE half - COBOLNET1504 on `FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED(1)` - is implemented and read but has no negative-corpus fixture pinning it, and the keyword-omitted leg (2002+, REPOSITORY) is pinned for CURRENT-DATE (golden 2023/pb62_all_subscript_runtime_ranges) but not for WHEN-COMPILED. EDITIONS: no §15.99 edition delta - Annex E carries no WHEN-COMPILED entry and the §15.6 function table row (spec line 30004) shows no version marker, so the batch default stands; the catalog's own IntroducedIn=85 was NOT used to derive this. REFUTED: verdict UPHELD at CONFORMS, code-location CORRECTED. Citation re-derived independently: cite.py --check 15.99.2 "WHEN-COMPILED" => OK §15.99.2 (General format), the diagram being exactly `FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED` with both words underlined and NO parenthesised part; cite.py --check 15.99.3 "The character positions returned, numbered from left to right, are" / "The returned value is the date and time of compilation of the compilation unit that contains this function" / "shall denote the same time as the compilation date and time" => OK §15.99.3 1) / 2) / 3). CODE-LOCATION MOVED from IntrinsicCatalog.cs#IntrinsicCatalog to IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore: the catalog row is DATA (name, 0..0, empty ArgKinds) and enforces nothing; the site that makes the compiler CONFORM to the format is the binder's arity gate, and rule 7 wants the ONE path that implements the rule. I re-walked BindIntrinsicCore line by line to be sure the gate is actually reached for this row rather than diverted: the eight bespoke early returns above it (CONVERT, MODULE-NAME, LENGTH/BYTE-LENGTH, NUMVAL-C, EXCEPTION-FILE, the LOCALE-phrase case arm, STANDARD-COMPARE, TRIM/FIND-STRING/SUBSTITUTE) all key on sig.Name or on ArgKinds, and `sig.ArgKinds.EndsWith('l')` on the EMPTY string is false, so WHEN-COMPILED falls through to BindIntrinsicArgs + the `given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs` gate. THREE ATTACKS RUN AND ALL FAILED, which is why the verdict stands: (1) TWO-ARM DISPATCH on the >>COBOL-WORDS synonym — DefinitionPermitsArguments resolves ctx.CobolWords.Synonyms at line 105, so I checked whether the OTHER arm does; BindIntrinsicCore line 447 resolves the same map before the catalog lookup, so `FUNCTION <synonym>` and the SR6 pre-check agree and there is no drift. (2) THE EMPTY-PARENTHESIS FORM `FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED ()`, which §15.99.2's own diagram does not draw and which the adjudicator never considered: it is nonetheless LEGAL, because §8.4.3.2.2's function-identifier format makes the whole parenthesised part optional AND argument-1 inside it optional (its figure note: 'the whole parenthesized argument list is optional'), and §8.4.3.2.3 SR6's NOTE writes `FUNCTION RANDOM ()` as the argument-less spelling; the compiler accepts it (0 in 0..0) — correct, not a gap. (3) RESERVED-WORD ROUTING: §8.11 (spec line 9711) lists WHEN-COMPILED as an INTRINSIC FUNCTION NAME, not a §8.9 reserved word, so the bare form really does arrive as a dataReference and KeywordOmittedFunction (MinArgs==0 admission at line 339, DialectLevel<2002 routing gate at line 227) is the right arm to have read. TEST-REF UPHELD: AssertSpec (lines 26-31) is `new CobolNetCompiler(dialect).CompileAndRun(source)` + Assert.Equal on the expected output — no DifferentialGolden, no AssertSameAsLegacy — so it qualifies under rule 3. Noted but not a downgrade: the test runs at AssertSpec's DEFAULT dialect 85 only, so the 2002+ keyword-omitted leg of this format is code-verified and unpinned at every edition.

subject: YEAR-TO-YYYY function
notes: cite.py --check 15.100.2 'FUNCTION</u> <u>YEAR-TO-YYYY' OK (General format) - the format is 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY ( argument-1 [ argument-2 [ argument-3 ] ] )', both words underlined hence required, with argument-3 NESTED inside argument-2's brackets. READ: there is no bespoke grammar for this function - CobolExpressions.g4's functionCall carries 'FUNCTION functionName' plus a parenthesised argument list of arithmeticExpressions separated by §8.3.5 separators, and IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 205 supplies the shape: Add(new("YEAR-TO-YYYY", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.OptionalTrailing, 1, 3, "iii", "YearToYyyy", ...)). IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore line 573 enforces it - 'if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs)' => COBOLNET1504 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY takes 1..3 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)'. The BRACKET NESTING needs no separate rule: the arguments are positional, so 1, 2 or 3 written arguments is exactly the language the nested brackets generate (argument-3 cannot be written without argument-2). Result type Integer matches §15.100.1 'The type of the function is integer'. Every arity is live in code - the 3-argument form is pinned end to end by conformance:2002/intrinsics_date_window (11 hand-derived lines), the 1-argument form by unit:CobolDateWindowingTests.YearToYyyy_DefaultArg3_IsExecutionYear; only the 2-argument form has no test, and no fixture pins the COBOLNET1504 over- or under-arity rejection for this function. The below-2002 edition gate is pinned by conformance:negative/date_window_below_2002 (COBOLNET1502). NOTE for the reader of AR-15.100.3-5: the 1- and 2-argument forms PARSE and COMPILE correctly on every carrier - the divergence recorded there is in the runtime default, not in this format. REFUTED: REFUTED: verdict UPHELD at CONFORMS - the implementation reading survives independent re-derivation - but ONE EVIDENCE CLAIM IS FALSE AND IS WITHDRAWN. cite.py --check 15.100.2 'YEAR-TO-YYYY' -> OK §15.100.2 (General format), rendering '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>YEAR-TO-YYYY</u> ( argument-1 [ argument-2 [ argument-3 ] ] )'. I verified every arity edge by READING, not by sampling: IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 205 gives IntrinsicArity.OptionalTrailing with MinArgs 1 / MaxArgs 3; IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore computes 'long given = args.Sum(...)' and rejects 'given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs' with COBOLNET1504 before any per-function arm; and I confirmed the binder injects NO default argument for this function (the only injecting arm is BindNumvalCFamily), so the written arity survives to the renderer intact - which is precisely what makes the bracket nesting positional and correct. THE FALSE CLAIM: 'the 1-argument form [is pinned] by unit:CobolDateWindowingTests.YearToYyyy_DefaultArg3_IsExecutionYear'. It is not. That test (CobolDateWindowingTests.cs line 41) calls 'CobolDate.YearToYyyy(76)' - a direct C# call on the runtime API. It never compiles a COBOL one-argument reference and so exercises none of the grammar, the catalog arity, the binder's COBOLNET1504, or the renderer's arity-dependent emission. The one-argument SOURCE form has no test on any path, and per the REFUTED note on AR-15.100.3-3 it is in fact the broken form on the float carrier. The two-argument source form is likewise untested, and no negative fixture pins the COBOLNET1504 over- or under-arity rejection for this function. That is a test debt, not an implementation gap - rule 3 makes CONFORMS with a thin test-ref a legitimate outcome - so the verdict stands and the claim is struck. EDITIONS (rule 4): '2002,2014,2023' is NOT taken from IntrinsicCatalog's own 2002 field nor from ConstructRegistry.g.cs, both of which are the code under review. Annex E of the 2023 standard carries no §15.100 entry (it lists changes from 2014), and the value matches the landed sibling inventory rows FMT-15.23.2 / FMT-15.25.2 for the same Y2K trio.
